News.title: Our seaside town has been decimated by an abandoned Pontins surrounded by barbed wire and ringing with GUNSHOTS
News.content:
Next

FURIOUS locals are demanding answers over a giant abandoned holiday park left to rot for three years.

The decaying site is surrounded by barbed wire fences and residents say the closure “decimated” their town.



Camber Sands Pontins was shut down in 2023 – and three years on has decayed into a Walking Dead-style wasteland.

Angry residents say the closure has damaged the town – with the abandoned site becoming an eyesore.



The ruin is occasionally used for armed police training, with locals saying gunshots ringing out are the only sound they now hear from the once bustling park.

When The Sun visited, we found technicolour entrance is plastered in crumbling paintwork and the site surrounded with collapsing marquees.





Around 820 chalets have been left festering across 32 acres of land.

Behind the uninviting barbed wire fencing we saw half blown down tents with smashed up golf carts inside.

Metal cages were flung into the bushes and benches had been rammed into staircases leading to the side entrances.

Pontins was the king of bang-for-buck bargain holidays, with several parks across the UK.

But after declining sales and massive financial losses, swathes of the joints closed their doors leaving just a couple still standing.



In a shock decision from owner Britannia Hotels, Camber Sands’ Pontins closed, leaving what locals say is a gaping hole in the local economy and a huge holiday complex abandoned.

The site has been decaying ever since and is a “horrendous eyesore” that should’ve been knocked down years ago, residents say.

To the disdain of residents, cops use the grounds for counter terrorism training and neighbours say they hear gunshots, police dogs and suffer a 24/7 spotlight.



But there’s little hope for change as Britannia Hotels holds a long- term lease with over 100 years left on the site.

Residents say the council’s hands are tied.

Local Chris told The Sun he suffers a 24/7 spotlight that’s left on behind the barbed wire fence facing directly across the road from his bedroom window.



He’s seen armed police training in Pontins and was forced to get extra thick curtains to shut out the bright beams.

He said: “I’ve seen police dogs over there, they’ve frightened the life out of us.

“They don’t ask permission or warn us and let off really loud explosions.

“They’re effing and blinding even in the Summer when there’s kids around.

“There’s police vans and SUVs that go in there, it’s armed police, I’ve seen chaps with cross body rifles on them.



“It’s a mess, we’re in the dark about it and the building itself is festering, it’s horrendous.”



Across the road, pensioner Maureen Reid, 85, is livid at the state of Pontins.

She’s concerned the building has been left to rot despite rumours of redevelopment.

Maureen told The Sun: “Britannia said they’re going to do it up, but since then it’s been a training group here and a training group there.

“We had no idea what’s happening.

“It’s in total disrepair; you think the district council will do something about it, but nobody seems to want to upset anyone or do anything about it.



“We just don’t get any answers, even the MPs are like chocolate teapots.”

The Camber Sands site opened in 1968 with a capacity of 3,000 holiday makers.

Since closing, local Dave Turby reckons it has left a gap in the Camber Sands economy.

He said: “It’s frustrating because it’s decimated the village, especially through the summer months.

“No one’s been told what’s going on with it, the majority of business was from tourists going to Pontins.”



Local MP Helena Dollimore said it was Britannia Hotel’s intention to “redevelop the site as a holiday destination” after a meeting with company bosses in 2024.

She told The Sun: “Camber residents have been left in limbo since Britannia Hotels closed the Pontins site.

“Britannia are set to reopen the site as a holiday destination, but they have been dragging their heels.

“This process has been far too slow and residents deserve answers. Britannia Hotels and Rother District Council must get their act together and provide clarity on how they will move this forward to get the best outcome for our community.”

Down the street, resident Michael has little hope that the Pontins site will be turned around.



He said: “We hear the odd shots, I think it’s an electric thing they use on their guns.

“Until Britannia decide to do something it won’t change.”

Round the corner we spoke to Rob Stuart who has watched the Pontins building become more and more grotty since 2023.

He said: “It’s in disrepair really, we’re worried about what they’re going to do with it next.

“But the whole country is broken, our best days are behind us and none of these politicians will fix anything.”



Britannia Hotels Group told us it’s met with local authority planning officers at Rother District Council to present its pre-application proposals for the site.

A spokesperson said: “We’re grateful for the positive and constructive comments received.

“This feedback will inform the next stages of the process as we progress the proposals and work continues to support a positive long-term outcome for the site.

“In the meantime, while the site remains unoccupied, it continues to be available free of charge to the police and other emergency services for training exercises.”

A Rother District Council spokesperson told The Sun: “Although the council is the freeholder of the site, Britannia Hotels has a long-term lease and is responsible for all buildings and site management.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As a result, the district council has very limited powers to control or influence what happens to the site.

“We met representatives from Britannia Hotels in the summer to discuss their proposals for bringing the site back into use and await further details.”

News.title: Shocking moment yobs launch fireworks in UK city centre with onlookers fleeing in horror as boy, 15, among 7 arrested
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a group of yobs shoot fireworks at police in a busy city centre amid a night of Halloween chaos.

Seven people were arrested after police were called to reports of disorder in Birmingham last night.



Shocking footage from the evening shows police officers being bowled over by rowdy revellers as they struggle to keep the peace.

At least five officers can be seen in one clip chasing a group of fleeing thugs as they attempt to bring the chaos to an end.



Further footage shows fireworks being let off in crowds and launched at responding cops.

Several police vehicles responded to the city centre with a crowd gathering around them.



Large pyrotechnics were launched at the police vans – exploding in bright flashes.

More fireworks were launched at bystanders with yobs dressed in black seen setting off the colourful explosives.



Members of the public ran for cover and recorded on their phones as sparks rained down on them.

Rockets could be seen flying up and down a busy street as fireworks were launched back and forth between crowds of revellers.

Crowds of people could be seen running away and screaming in terror after the rockets were launched along New Street.

Police were called to the scene after the city centre was turned into a “war zone” by the thugs.

West Midlands Police said seven people – aged between 15 and 26 – had been arrested for a variety of offences.



Some were taken into custody on suspicion of assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.

All seven remain in police custody at this time, the arrests were made in and around Stephenson St and Corporation St.

One onlooker said: “It was like a warzone. People were just letting off fireworks at each other like it was just a bit of harmless fun.



“I didn’t see anyone getting hurt but I would be amazed if nobody was injured during that as fireworks were exploding next to people in the street. It was mayhem.”

Other residents expressed their shock and dismay on social media with one person writing: “Absolute morons, somebody could have been killed.”

Another added: “That is absolutely crazy, fair play to that one woman on her phone walking by as if nothing is happening. I would have been running for my life.”

A police spokesperson said: “We responded to reports of fireworks being set off in a dangerous manner.

“In total we arrested seven people (aged between 15 and 26) for a number of offences including assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.



“They all remain in custody for questioning.

“A Section 60 which was in place last night (Sat) and into the early hours of this morning, gave officers extra powers to carry out stop and searches of those suspected of carrying weapons or fireworks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The arrests were made in and around Stephenson St and Corporation St.”

Anyone who witnessed antisocial behaviour last night in the city can contact West Midlands Police, the force said.

News.title: Kim Jong-un tests cluster bomb warheads capable of ‘turning into ash’ areas the size of 17 football fields
News.content:
Next

NUKE-obsessed Kim Jong-un has test-fired a new range of cluster bomb warheads capable of turning a 30-acre area to ashes in seconds.

The Hermit Kingdom vowed to produce more variants of the terrifying weapon by the end of the year as it conducts a slew of military drills.



North Korea has ramped up its show of force lately, trialling attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.

The latest test, conducted on Saturday, found that a Type 2 cluster bomb warhead can turn a 30-acre area to ashes with its highest density, ​per a state report.



Cluster bombs scatter dozens, sometimes hundreds, of smaller bomblets across a wide area, enabling it to hit multiple targets simultaneously.

​North Korea will enable its military units by ​the end of 2026 to use all types of the ‌bombs, ⁠depending on their operational purposes, KCNA said.



It comes amid flaring tensions on the Korean peninsula over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border.

Three South Korean soldiers were injured in the incident, with the North denying responsibility.



Instead, Pyongyang vowed to strengthen its border areas and resume its loudspeaker campaign.

Saturday’s test was conducted to “assess adaptation to combat and power of a cluster-bomb warhead to be tipped on tactical ballistic missiles”, the official Korean Central News Agency reported Sunday.

Officials said it confirmed the weapon “is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 12 to 13 hectares with its highest-density power“.



The general director of North Korea‘s Missile Administration said: “Within this year we will enable units to select and use all those types according to operational aims and specific features of targets.”

Photos released by KCNA showed a projectile firing from a mobile launcher, with an orange exhaust plume. Another image showed multiple cluster-bomb impacts on an island target.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was not present on Saturday, although he had overseen a test-launch of cluster-bomb warheads mounted on a ballistic missile in April, accompanied by his daughter Ju Ae.

It comes as the FBI confirmed that Kim’s state-sponsored hacker squad stole $6.3billion in crypto assets from Binance, prompting the exchange to suspend activity.

The shady Lazarus group – which has perpetrated some of the most costly attacks on Western banks – gained access to the system by compromising an engineer’s computer.



Around 90 per cent of the assets were frozen, Binance later announced, and the world’s largest currency exchange has begun a phased reopening of customer withdrawals.

Earlier this week, a bombshell investigation revealed that North Koreans are being sold online to Russian businesses as part of a state- sponsored forced labour programme.

The twisted scheme allows Vladimir Putin to bolster his war machine with a brutally controlled workforce while Kim snatches their wages to fund his ballistic missile programme, it claims.



The Global Rights Compliance (GRC) exposed how the two states use the network to “bypass international sanctions” and fuel their military “aggression”.

GRC Legal Advisor Elise Lauriot Prevost, who worked on the investigation, told The Sun: “Cooperation between the DPRK and Russia is only getting stronger.

“The DPRK is getting hard cash and fuel while Russia is getting workers to supplement its manpower shortages.”

The report follows a nine-month undercover investigation into KNDR.su, a broker network run by Moscow businessman Vladimir Sokolov.

The platform, which markets North Korean workers for sale, charges a commission of £900 to £1,350 per worker for a minimum of 50 workers.



GRC identified nine sites in Russia associated with North Korea through Sokolov’s network alone.

Elise said: “Both countries treat people as instruments of state power.

“But none of this is new. North Korea has exported forced labour for more than two decades.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The same can be seen through Russia’s aggression in Ukraine and the high death toll of their own soldiers.

“It seems both countries are willing to sacrifice their own civilians for their military machines.”

News.title: Baby boy dies after swallowing part of balloon at Halloween party days before first birthday – his mom saw him turn blue
News.content:
Next

CELEBRATION turned to tragedy after a baby boy died at a Halloween party when he swallowed part of a balloon animal.

Don’Vyaire Avita-Mays was at a family party on October 24, just two days before his first birthday, when a balloon animal popped and the knot and attached latex lodged in his throat.



His horrified mom Kisha Avita-Wilson from Wisconsin recalled the harrowing moment she desperately tried to save her son as he turned blue.

“I grabbed him immediately out of his car seat. I performed CPR … I stuck my fingers down his throat,” she told NBC Chicago.



“The person that I was with tried to do the same things also, and he turned blue immediately and went into cardiac arrest.”

She described how first responders tried to remove the piece of balloon using a tube and some pliers.

read more on news GUN HORROR One dead & 8 injured in 'senseless' Halloween shooting at college football game

“It was nothing that we could have done to save my baby boy,” she said.

Kisha explained how everyone at the family event had been actively trying to keep the balloons away from Don, but one came undone and he grabbed it and bit it.

A heartbreaking update shared on a GoFundMe page for funeral expenses revealed that Kisha is seven months pregnant and has been hospitalized due to the stress of the tragedy.

The expectant mom is due in January but already experienced contractions as “the stress and heartbreak is taking a toll on her physically, mentally, and emotionally,” her aunt and adoptive mom wrote.



Meanwhile, the grieving mom is warning parents about the dangers of balloons and demanding that they should stop being sold altogether.

“Balloons have warnings on them, but that is not enough,” she said.

“They should stop selling them. Stop marketing them to kids. Stop producing them.”

News.title: Two dead and another two left injured after ‘being electrocuted’ at luxury hotel swimming pool
News.content:
POOL TRAGEDY Two dead and another two left injured after ‘being electrocuted’ at luxury hotel swimming pool







Next

TWO guests have died following a suspected electrocution in the swimming pool of a five-star hotel.

The incident left a further two people injured, with police believing the tragedy was caused by an electrical leak.

Cops identified the deceased as Alexander Maximilian Theiss, 57, a German national and Lufthansa crew member, and Juraj Horvat, 45, a Slovak national who worked as a project manager for IBM.

Alexander’s wife reportedly filed a police complaint alleging that the men were both shocked while trying to get out of the pool and drowned, NDTV reports.





Police have launched an investigation the tragic accident at the Conrad Bengaluru hotel in India.

A 41-year-old American guest, Mathew Desantis, and Rahul Tiwari, a 28-year-old pool attendant and lifeguard, were injured while bravely trying to help the two men in peril, according to The New Indian Express.

Alexander’s wife alleges the tragic deaths were caused by negligence by the hotel’s management in maintaining the pool.

The Conrad Bengaluru Hotel said it was “deeply saddened” by the deaths of two of its guests following a “tragic incident”.



They said the cause “has not yet been established” and say they will be cooperating with police.

All victims were rushed to Manipal Hospital Old Airport Road, however sadly one of the men was dead on arrival.

The other arrived in a state of cardiac arrest and could not be revived.

The hospital said the men died following a “water-related incident” at the hotel.



Reports suggest the two injured victims are both in stable conditions.

Lufthansa confirmed that one of their crew members died in an accident during a layover in Bengaluru.

They told FoxNews: “Our deepest sympathies go out to the family, relatives and friends of the deceased crew member.”

The hotel has said on its website that the pool will be “closed for maintenance” from October 31 to November 30.

Conrad is a luxury 24-storey five-star hotel, part of the Hilton group.



The state government agency responsible for enforcing electrical safety standards, regulations, and inspections in the state, is reportedly examining the underwater light as part of the probe.

Investigators are also verifying whether key safety devices, including earth-leakage circuit breakers, were operational at the time.

In January, a mother and her 11-year-old son tragically died after being electrocuted in a swimming pool while on a luxury family holiday.

Luciana Klein Helfstein, 39, and her son Arthur Klein Helfstein Alves were electrocuted to death in the pool at a guesthouse in Maragogi, a popular resort on Brazil’s Caribbean coast.

The mothers boyfriend tragically found the pair lifeless in the pool.



Despite desperate efforts to resuscitate the mother and son, they were later declared dead at a local emergency unit.

News.title: I was raped by my cousin – he abused me & my sister for YEARS when we were children & now we’ve been robbed of justice
News.content:
Next

FAMILY gatherings are a time of great excitement for most children growing up – seeing relatives for a catch-up and building life-long bonds.

But for sisters Megan and Krista Minnock they were the stuff of nightmares.





Evil Kaylum Hay repeatedly sexually abused his cousin Megan over many years from when they were both very young.

A court also heard how Megan’s sister Krista also claims Hay, now 27, abused her too, but because he was under 10 at the time of the alleged offences relating to her, he couldn’t be prosecuted for them.

He denied all allegations against him.

And to make matters even worse, despite being convicted of eight serious sexual offences against Megan, the predator walked free, having avoided an immediate jail sentence.

The sisters reported Hay to cops together in 2021 – before waiting five years to see him stand trial in August.

Megan, now 26, originally from Kent, said: “He took my childhood away, and my whole life up until this point has been controlled by what he did to me and my family.”

Canterbury Crown Court heard how Hay forced Megan into sexual acts and raped her twice when he was a teenager.

Many such attacks took place during family gatherings.





Megan continued: “The abuse was nearly every weekend.

“He would always find a way to get me alone. The last time I remember being raped, I was 15 or 16.”

She described being left “paralysed” with fear as Hay ignored her cries for him to stop.

She added: “Eventually, I learned that giving in was safer than resisting. I stopped caring about myself and still struggle to this day.”

Hay denied three charges of causing or inciting a child to engage in sexual activity, three of sexual assault and two of rape, but was convicted of all eight counts.

But at sentencing on October 2, he was spared being sent straight to prison, and instead was handed a three-year jail sentence suspended for three years.

“It was a kick in the teeth,” Megan said. “He doesn’t even get as long as we have had to wait for this court process.

“It’s really unjust and I feel let down by the system. We have been made to feel very unimportant. I’m so upset. I feel so let down. This is why girls are so scared to come forward.”



During the sentencing hearing, prosecutor Allister Walker told the court that Hay, who continues to deny any wrongdoing, first raped Megan when he was 14.

In a statement read by Mr Walker, Megan told how she had been left “messed up” and her life “massively” impacted by her ordeal.

Speaking after the sentencing, Megan said she had been frightened of Hay as a young girl.

“He’s not a nice person at all,” she said.

“He’s very intimidating and manipulative. He made me feel like it was my fault.”

Krista, now 28, who lives in Cornwall, also gave evidence at Hay’s trial, alleging she too had been sexually abused by him when they were children.



She alleged to the court Hay made the sisters perform sexual acts on each other and on him when they were very young.

She recalled an occasion when an adult discovered the children behind a shed, and was left embarrassed when they were told off.

However, her allegations were not subject of the jury’s verdicts and were denied by Hay, like all the accusations against him.

On the prospect of speaking out, Megan said: “I think I’m more angry than scared.

“I don’t want to do this for attention. I want to do this for other people.”

She added: “I need to say this because it has caused me immense guilt for years: I was a child being abused. I did not choose any of this.”

Krista said: “We are sharing our stories to raise awareness and hopefully prevent anyone else from suffering at his hands.”

The court heard that Hay had “significant developmental and cognitive” difficulties which have since been diagnosed as dyslexia, autism and ADHD.



His lawyer Ethan Dighton urged the court to take a “more holistic” approach and not jail the defendant, who is now a father himself to a young child.

“He is a very different man to the child that committed those offences in a different stage of his life,” he said.

During sentencing, Recorder Duncan Atkinson explained that an adult convicted of the crimes would face a prison term of at least four years.

But because Hay was a child at the time, he only faced either a non-custodial sanction or one year in jail. And the decision made would be “heavily influenced” by age, immaturity and culpability.

Recorder Atkinson added the offences were “kept secret for as long as they were” because of the threat Hay made if Megan revealed the truth – a threat which was “effective for a long time and caused lasting damage”.

As well as the suspended sentence, he is also required to sign on the sex offender register indefinitely, as well as a 10-year restraining order.

Megan said she “cried so hard” when Hay was spared prison.

“Not only did he take away my childhood and my virginity – he took away so much more,” she said.

“He’s made it really hard for me to trust anybody, if I were to have children of my own – if someone in my own family can do that to me.

“It pains me deeply and I will never forgive him for what he’s done not just to me but to all of us.



“It’s going to stay with me for the rest of my life.”

Krista added: “His sentence feels like no justice at all.”

The sisters have now applied to the Attorney General’s Office to review the sentence as they believe it is too lenient.

The sisters reported Hay to Kent Police in April 2021 and officers interviewed him the following month.

Due to the complexity of the case, police did not go to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) for a charging decision until August 2023.

Kent’s Police and Crime Commissioner, Matthew Scott, said he shares the sisters’ “frustration” with how long cases are taking to get to court.

“Criminal Justice Partners locally are doing everything possible to drive down these delays, which can be incredibly traumatic for all involved,” he said.

“However, on a local level we cannot do this alone. We do need more support from government for extra court capacity, staffing and judges.”



Mr Scott said he was sorry to hear about the sisters’ ordeal and highlighted that support is available for victims via the confidential Kent Sexual Assault & Abuse Service, which he commissions.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Our sympathies remain with the victim in this case, and we commend her bravery in speaking out.

“Violence against women and girls is an epidemic we are determined to halve within a decade.”

They added: “Sentencing is a matter for independent judges in line with the law and Sentencing Guidelines, but a suspended sentence does not mean freedom.

“Offenders must comply with strict conditions on their activity and movements or risk being sent to prison.”

News.title: Five teenage boys, 16 & 17, seriously injured in stabbing at Halloween house party
News.content:
KNIFE CARNAGE Five teenage boys, 16 & 17, seriously injured in stabbing at Halloween house party







Next

FIVE teenagers have been left with serious injuries following a stabbing at a house party on Halloween.

Officers were called to reports of an incident at an address in Chandlers Ford, Hampshire, just after 10pm last night.

Three 16-year-old boys and two 17-year-old boys suffered serious injuries in the horror.

All five have been taken to hospital for treatment.





Police say an “unknown group” had gained entry to the address on Park Road – where a party was being held – before the stabbing unfolded.

An investigation into the horror has been launched with cops asking anyone with any information that may assist their probe to come forward.

Hampshire Police DCI Elizabeth Pirie said: “We are already hard at work identifying anyone who was at the party who may be able to assist our enquiries, whether that be having directly witnessed what took place, having filmed any footage which may be relevant, or who may be able to help us identify the unknown group.

“I understand the response the local community may have to hearing about this incident this morning, and I do not underestimate the impact our scenes will be having on those living in the area.



“These scenes are vitally important for our enquiries and we are grateful to the understanding of our communities whilst we work to establish the facts.

“If you do have any concerns or information, then please do not hesitate to speak to us.

“We particularly want to hear from anyone who can provide information to support our investigation.

“If you were at the party and have not spoken with officers yet, or you have any CCTV, mobile phone, dash cam or doorbell camera footage covering Park Road and the surrounding area, then please get in touch.



“Any information, however small it may seem, could help our enquiries.”

Liz Jarvis, MP for Eastleigh, said on X on Sunday: “My thoughts are with the victims and their families and all those affected by the incident in Chandler’s Ford last night, and my thanks go to our local police and emergency services for their prompt response.

“It’s important not to speculate or share unverified information.”

News.title: Labour minister sparks MORE Budget fury after claiming bosses are not ‘working people’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CLASS DISMISSED Labour minister sparks MORE Budget fury after claiming bosses are not ‘working people’







Next

A LABOUR minister has sparked fury after claiming bosses are not “working people”.

Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds insisted employers did not count because they were “companies” – reigniting a bitter row over Labour’s tax promises.



She told GB News: “I don’t think employers are working people, they are companies.”

And when challenged on whether someone who employs a cleaner is therefore not a working person, she insisted there was “a difference between employers and employees”.



Her remarks sparked a furious backlash from Tories, who accused Labour of insulting hardworking small business owners.

Shadow business minister Bradley Thomas blasted: “Labour’s patronising, out-of-touch, politics of envy on display here from Minister Emma Reynolds.



“What about the thousands of small businesses who employ people? The electrician who works but takes on apprentices? The florist who runs her shop and has a young person work a few hours on weekends?

“The list is endless and so is Labour’s vindictiveness and denial of reality.”

And former minister Helen Whately fumed: “This attitude is why Labour is killing our economy. They don’t understand businesses are built by hard graft. By working people.”

The row revives a long-running battle over exactly who Labour considers a “working person”.



The party swept to power in 2024 promising not to raise taxes on working people, including income tax, VAT and National Insurance.

But just months later, then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves hiked employers’ National Insurance contributions, prompting accusations that Labour had broken its manifesto pledge.

Ministers insisted the promise had not been breached because the rise hit employers rather than employees.

And the definition has remained a political headache ever since, with senior Labour figures offering different explanations of who qualifies.

Ms Reynolds defended the Government’s record, insisting it had not increased the headline rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance for employees.



Her comments came just days after Chancellor John Healey’s first Budget slapped an extra 2p income tax on landlords and savers from April 2027.

But Ms Reynolds insisted the tax rises were “targeted and fair”, pointing to the Chancellor’s £100 energy handout for millions of households and extended fuel duty cut.

News.title: Healey risks breaking minimum wage promise for younger workers
News.content:
The Chancellor, John Healey, has suggested that younger workers might not receive the same minimum wage as others before the next election, potentially breaking a Labour manifesto promise.

In 2024, Labour said it would remove "discriminatory age bands", vowing to end the gap between the adult minimum wage and pay for 18 to 20-year-olds.

But in last week's Budget, Healey said that younger workers would see the same increase as older workers, leaving a gap between the two rates this year.

Pay for 18 to 20-year-olds in 2026 will rise to Â£11.27, while over-20s will be paid a minimum of Â£13.21 an hour.

In a BBC interview broadcast on Sunday, Healey was asked if younger workers would be paid the same as older workers, when it comes to the minimum wage, by the time of the next election?

"We'll take one step at a time," he said, suggesting that Labour might abandon its plan to close the gap before the next election.

It is a change that is likely to anger the unions and some on the left of the party.

Healey added that Labour was still committed to the ambition, but hinted the plan to equalise wages might be delayed, partly to encourage businesses to employ younger workers.

"There is no question about whether or if, it's a question of when - it's a question of how fast," he said.

"I want to make sure we can look hard at those trade-offs that are there between jobs and wages."

"I want to take business, I want to take trade unions with me, and with the government, because together we have to get into what at the moment is a moral shame on this nation. A million youngsters - written off without any prospect of being helped into work and making contributions to this country for the future."

News.title: Five teenagers stabbed at Halloween party
News.content:
Five teenagers have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party, police have said.

Officers were called to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, near Eastleigh, shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday.

The injured teens - three boys aged 16 and two aged 17 - were taken to hospital.

Hampshire Police said it believes an unknown group gained entry to a party at an address on Park Road before the stabbings.

The force has appealed for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward.

A police cordon remained in place on Sunday while officers continue their investigation.

Senior investigating officer Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie acknowledged the impact on local residents and thanked the community for its patience.

Earlier, an eyewitness told the BBC ambulances and an air ambulance had attended.

Another eyewitness said they saw someone running out of the house involved, shouting that he had been stabbed and that he was being chased by two people.

News.title: University of Cambridge scientist among those who died in Spanish train crash
News.content:
An award-winning University of Cambridge researcher died in the Spanish train disaster while on her way to collect a prize for scientific excellence.

Dr Marta Shahbazi was travelling to an awards ceremony on Wednesday when the train she was on crashed into another near Urda, south of Madrid, killing 69 people.

The mother-of-two was an affiliate associate professor leading a group of researchers at MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge and had earned several awards for work on human embryos and cell biology.

In a statement, the LMB paid tribute to the "inspiring, talented and passionate scientist" and described her death as a "profound shock and a huge loss".

The expert in cell biology ran the Shahbazi Laboratory at the LMB, based on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus.

She had been announced as the winner of a Spanish Society for Developmental Biology award for her contributions to the study of early human development and was due to collect the award at a conference in El Rompido in Andalusia.

The LMB said: "As a wife and mother of two young children, Marta wrote eloquently about balancing her family and career, serving as a much-admired role model for a 'mother scientist', a term she used to describe herself.

"Marta was an inspiring, talented and passionate scientist whose research shed light on the earliest steps in the development of human embryos and how errors occur that lead to failed pregnancies," the LMB said.

The institute said her death was "a profound shock and a huge loss for LMB".

Her work had been recognised with "many awards and prizes", the laboratory added.

News.title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy
News.content:
More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.

Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action."

The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made. The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".

At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.

The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation, after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.

The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.

Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine."

In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.

Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon - had travelled from Cumbria to participate. He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".

"I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.

David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".

Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".

According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026. Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.

The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.

Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.

Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.

News.title: King to address slavery in Antigua as PM says he is open to possible UK apology
News.content:
King Charles III is to speak with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" on the lasting pain of the transatlantic slave trade, during the final leg of his Caribbean tour in Antigua, Buckingham Palace has said.

The King will address Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday in a speech which will touch on the issue.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier he was "open" to the possibility of the UK formally apologising for its role in slavery - a change in the government's stance.

It is understood the Palace was told in advance of Burnham's comments in an opinion piece on Friday night, and the King has not made any changes to his speech in light of them.

The British government has never formally apologised for slavery or offered to pay reparations.

Burnham has previously stuck with the policy of his predecessors, and stopped short of offering any consideration of reparation payments.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch described "endless talk about apologies" as a "distraction" from solving current problems.

She told BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "The transatlantic slave trade happened centuries ago. It is time for the Commonwealth to start looking forwards, not endlessly backwards."

The King will make his speech at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).

He "will not shy away from confronting the most shameful aspects of the past during this visit", a Palace spokesperson said.

"You may therefore expect him to address them in his speech with unflinching honesty, sincere sorrow, and respect for the wider discussions that will be taking place between relevant governments on this issue at CHOGM and beyond."

When asked about the King's reaction to the prime minister's comments, the spokesperson said it would "not be appropriate" for the King to address matters of policy relating to "the UK government's position".

The Caribbean tour has again thrust King Charles into the difficult debates over the UK's colonial legacy in the region.

On his first stop in the Bahamas, the King delivered a speech where he spoke of the "suffering of the past".

In Guyana, he visited the site of a Slave Rebellion where hundreds of enslaved people were killed.

Buckingham Palace said it was a moment for the King to learn more about the history of slavery and resistance. His engagements have also covered the environment, opportunities for young people and trade relationships with the UK.

News.title: Watch: Heidi Klum as giant severed hand for Halloween bash
News.content:
The supermodel and TV host Heidi Klum continued her pose as the queen of Halloween by transforming into a giant, bloodied and severed hand for her annual costume party on 31 October.

Klum, 53, was completely unrecognisable arriving at her event in what she described as her own chopped-off "left hand".

This year was the 25th anniversary of the party, which has provided viral pop culture moments over the years, like when Klum dressed up as a worm in 2022.

News.title: Who are the real winners of Celebrity Traitors?
News.content:
Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from The Celebrity Traitors final

In some ways, all the players on The Celebrity Traitors can be seen as winners.

They all got to appear on a hugely popular TV show, rubbing shoulders with other stars and gaining new fans along the way.

But there are certain celebrities, such as Miranda Hart, King Kenny, Maya Jama and Joanne McNally, who have been tipped by industry experts as getting the biggest career boost after the show.

Sebastian "Bash" Croft - who won the game, alongside Romesh Ranganathan - could also now be in line for greater roles.

We've taken a look at the breakout stars of the series and what might lie ahead for them.

News.title: No more washing up: Airbnb's new house rules divide hosts and guests
News.content:
When Lisa Clewes returned to her Welsh holiday let after a group of guests checked out, she was horrified by the mess.

Just days earlier, she had met the group in person and helped with their luggage.

But after a dinner party, the house was left "in a complete mess" with broken glasses, drinks cans on the floor, pans full of food on the table and fish guts left in the garden.

"It was really unbelievable. Had I had another booking the same day, I would have had to cancel or delay check-in," says Clewes.

She charges a cleaning fee that covers around 75% of the cost of a cleaner and asks guests to empty the fridge, put rubbish in the bins and load the dishwasher.

News.title: Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU
News.content:
Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK's future should be inside the EU, and that Brexit has made the country "poorer, weaker and less secure".

In her first major intervention since leaving the Treasury, Reeves said she welcomed debate around the UK's relationship with Europe.

At the last election, Labour's manifesto said a Labour government would stay outside the EU and make Brexit work.

But Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there needs to be an honest discussion about what the future relationship looks like.

The Conservatives have said there is no desire to rerun the Brexit debate and Reform UK's Nigel Farage has said there is no mandate to pursue closer EU ties.

Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.

Burnham has said that any changes would require a mandate at a general election, which is next due by 2029.

In the Sunday Times, external, Reeves wrote: "No-one in the Treasury ever doubted where my instincts were. I do believe Britain's future lies in the European Union."

She said supporters of rejoining the EU had to "make the argument, demonstrate tangible benefits and to get the next steps right".

Reeves added that at the forthcoming UK-EU summit, she hoped for confirmation of the youth mobility scheme she has been pushing for since she was in office.

She also said she was hoping for "progress towards entry" into the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) scheme.

Announced last March, SAFE is part of an EU-wide effort to rearm after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

A defence pact agreed with the EU last May paved the way for UK-based defence companies to be part of projects funded by SAFE.

In her piece for the Sunday Times, Reeves also sought to defend her record in office.

She wrote about the need for governments to be "braver" in building big infrastructure projects and "clear eyed" about the risks and benefits AI would drive in advanced economies.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said she "can't even believe we are reopening" the Brexit debate.

She told BBC One's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "This is not something that is needed in order to cut welfare, in order to spend money on defence.

"We are having yet another Westminster bubble argument about the EU when it is time for us to actually start using the opportunities, fix mistakes that have been made and go into the future."

Badenoch added: "I do not want to indulge Andy Burnham's fantasies about redoing the referendum because he doesn't have a plan for what to do today."

Burnham told Badenoch during the most recent session of Prime Minister's Questions that he was focused on "getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility".

The next UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November.

News.title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death
News.content:
A hospital trust has taken full responsibility for 24 failures that led to the death of a 21-month-old.

Eleanor Hazel Aldred-Owen died at Liverpool's Alder Hey Hospital on 2 October 2023 - a coroner concluded she died as a result of misadventure, contributed to by neglect.

She had routine surgery for craniosynostosis, external, a birth defect affecting the skull, but an abnormal chest X-ray was not flagged.

Eleanor suffered a cardiac arrest and an unsurvivable brain injury, and died in her parents' arms.

Her family, from Mold, Flintshire, said they had lived with "unbearable" guilt and trauma ever since.

Alder Hey Children's Hospital NHS Foundation Trust said her "tragic" death "should not have happened".

Eleanor's dad Chaz said: "Not knowing how or why Eleanor died was the key factors and what kept us going was justice for her.

"The real victory is making sure what happened to Eleanor doesn't happen to anyone else. No other family or child will have to go through what we have."

He added both he and his wife Rachel were "fairly certain it was neglectful" but did not realise the extent of it, and were "at the mercy of what Alder Hey were telling us".

"They said it was breach of duty and not gross neglect and it took a long time for the trust to admit that."

He said the trust "being compelled to admit gross neglect" was the hardest thing.

News.title: Seven arrested after city centre firework disorder
News.content:
Seven people have been arrested after disorder, involving fireworks being set off, in a city centre.

Footage posted on social media showed crowds gathered on Corporation Street in Birmingham, with fireworks being set off close to police officers and vehicles.

West Midlands Police had warned firm action would be taken against anyone involved in fireworks-related disorder, following serious incidents in the city during Bonfire Night last year.

Those arrested, aged between 15 and 26, were held on suspicion of offences including assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.

They all remain in custody for questioning, the force said.

Officers used Section 60 stop-and-search powers, which allow searches without the need to have reasonable grounds to do so.

The arrests were made in and around Stephenson Street and Corporation Street, after officers responded to "pockets of disorder," involving fireworks being set off in a dangerous manner, said the force.

Ch Supt Tom Boyce said: "Misusing fireworks is not only dangerous: it's illegal and can lead to fines, arrest and criminal charges."

The force said extra officers had been deployed at key locations to prevent a repeat of last year's violence.

On 6 November 2025, 21 people were arrested after officers were attacked with fireworks on Dale End and Staniforth Street.

News.title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader
News.content:
Ramsay also said he has made it clear he is "deeply uncomfortable" with the motion adopted and suggested there is an "opportunity to take some action in relation to the motion in the run-up" to the party's spring conference next year.

He said the question now is how Polanski and the party as a whole responds to the motion.

Ramsay said: "I think there's a real crossroads point for the party at the moment.

"One option is to sort of dig in more down this approach, not only in relation to this motion, but I think that there's a risk it brings with it - a quite divisive, a quite internally focused approach to politics."

Ramsay said this is "perhaps seen from small groups of people on the hard left of politics who go around different parties try to influence how those parties are run".

He added: "What I want to see is the party really focus back in on our core aims as a party and our core values."

Ramsay said this includes ensuring the party is "consensus-building in how we approach our politics" and that "we engage the grassroots of our membership".

He added the party needs to be "very externally focused, because we're only going to be able to bring the environmental changes that we need to have to safeguard our society for now and for the future if the majority of the British public come behind that".

Ramsay served as co-leader of the Greens from 2021 to 2025 alongside Carla Denyer, who is also now an MP.

He unsuccessfully stood on a joint ticket with fellow MP Ellie Chowns in 2025, with the pair losing to Polanski in the leadership contest.

Polanski, who missed the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, previously said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.

However, he said the "substantial part of the motion", that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology" was "obvious". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.

Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.

News.title: Northern Lights dance across UK sky on Halloween night
News.content:
Stargazers around the UK were treated to the vivid colours of the aurora borealis on Saturday night.

As cloud and rain on the weather front cleared southwards, parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland were perfectly placed to catch the display.

The eerie glow provided a fitting finale to spookiest night of the year, delighting skywatchers and photographers alike.

Aurora activity may continue into Sunday night, especially in northern skies, but the display is likely to be less intense than the one seen on Halloween night.

News.title: Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix
News.content:
Russell, who said he was happy to have ended a run of difficult form but could not explain why, took a unilateral decision not to do a preparation lap after his out lap on his final run.

He said he had a "gut feeling" that it was the best approach, but the team had insisted on a prep lap and had fuelled the car for the extra mileage.

"[The time loss for the extra fuel weight is] such a small number," said Russell, "but it's bigger than the gap to pole. Nevertheless, I'm just happy to be up here."

Verstappen said traffic with another car is what led to his loss of time.

"Already going into (Turn) 12 I had a car very close to me and I already lost time there with the dirty air," he said.

"And then going into the hairpin, instead of going on the left, I had one car on my right where you normally want to open up the corner. So its a bit of an awkward angle you have to go into the hairpin.

"Plus you lose your reference on the right-hand side where you are constantly looking. It's a difficult corner to get right, that killed my lap. The most promising thing is how we turned it around as in practice I was not that happy and we turned it around, I was in the fight for pole."

McLaren's Lando Norris had looked in contention for pole, fastest in the second session and on the first runs in the final session, when he was third fastest behind Leclerc and Verstappen.

But he failed to improve on his final lap and had to be satisfied fight sixth.

"Just not quick enough that's all," said Norris. "The lap was incredible in Q2 to put me P1. That was very unrealistic in terms of achieving that again in Q3.

"I am pretty happy with P6, can't ask a lot more and pretty happy with the job I did with the car I have."

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls pair Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Pierre Gasly completed the top 10.

Lawson was later disqualified from qualifying for an Infringement of the technical regulations regarding the usage of the electrical deployment of the power unit and will start from the back.

Fernando Alonso looked to be in contention for his best qualifying of the year for Aston Martin when he went fastest on his first lap of the session ahead of a number of cars that for most of the season have been ahead of him.

But his engine suffered a water leak in the energy recovery system as he started his second attempt, when he was still lying third, and he was ordered to stop the car on track.

Alonso's frustration after a year of poor performance and reliability from the Honda engine was clear in an interview with the official television channel afterwards, when he said a total of nine words in answer to four questions.

In those words, he confirmed it had been an engine problem, said "it was" a good opportunity and it was "correct" that the car has been looking good all weekend - but that he could not do anything in the race "from the back".

News.title: Sir Tom Jones mentors Cardiff singer to victory on The Voice UK
News.content:
A singer who began her career as a teenager busking on the streets of Cardiff has been crowned winner of The Voice UK.

Cate McHugh, from Llantwit Major in the Vale of Glamorgan, appeared stunned when she heard her name announced on the ITV show, telling viewers "I did it" when asked how she was feeling.

The performer, who has a degenerative sight condition which has left her registered blind, was given a congratulatory hug by her coach Sir Tom Jones on his final appearance on the show after previously announcing he had been "fired".

Speaking after the show, McHugh, 31, said: "I won The Voice! I'm entirely gobsmacked and absolutely haven't fully processed this information just yet."

Footage shared by McHugh on social media showed her laughing and smiling with family and friends screaming in delight as they celebrated her victory at a watch party in Cardiff.

McHugh's prizes include a Â£50,000 cash prize and a recording contract, with her first ever single, a cover of The Beatles classic Blackbird, now released.

Posting on social media, she said: "From the bottom of my heart I want to say THANK YOU for following my journey, and joining my world! This is where it's going to REALLY get fun!"

News.title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland
News.content:
Police Scotland received 144 fireworks-related calls on Saturday night - down on 160 on 31 October last year.

Fireworks were thrown at people, buildings and vehicles in some parts of Scotland on Halloween.

Officers said in general there was "outstanding behaviour and co-operation" around the country but were working to identify to those responsible for disorder.

Firework Control Zones (FCZs) - where it is an offence to set off fireworks - are in place in 14 areas in Edinburgh and four in Glasgow until early November, and dispersal zones are in force in some places.

On Halloween there were reports of fireworks lit in the street and some thrown at members of the public in Glasgow, Tranent in East Lothian and Bonnyrigg in Midlothian.

Police said no officers were injured and inquiries to identify those involved were ongoing.

News.title: Badenoch claims British empire was force for good overall: ‘We have had enough of apologies’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Kemi Badenoch has said she believes the British Empire was “overall a force for good” as she criticised Andy Burnham for considering issuing an apology for slavery.

The Conservative leader acknowledged there were “terrible things that happened” but told Sky News on Sunday “there were terrible things that happened all over the world in all empires, and even in countries and regions where they didn't have empires”.

It comes ahead of a Commonwealth leaders’ summit being hosted by Antigua next week, where the King is expected to speak about the issue of slavery with “unflinching honesty” and “sincere sorrow”.

The Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting has increased interest after prime minister Andy Burnham offered Commonwealth nations the opportunity to discuss a slavery apology from Britain, but insisted financial reparations will not follow.

Mrs Badenoch accused the prime minister of not “thinking about the repercussions of his actions”, warning he risks putting “pressure” on the King during his visit.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham offered Commonwealth nations the opportunity to discuss a slavery apology from Britain, but insisted financial reparations will not follow. ( PA Wire )

“It encourages many of those countries to think that we're looking weaker than we are,” she said.

“I don't want people to see Britain as a weak country. We are a strong country, and I want our Prime Minister to be the biggest defender of the UK. Not another person going in to start apologising.

“We've had enough of apologising. It's time for us to move on.”

Asked about whether she believes the British Empire was a “force for good”, the Tory leader said: “I have always said that I think that overall the British Empire was a force for good, and I think that that we have to be honest about the history.

“Of course, there were terrible things that happened, but there were terrible things that happened all over the world in all empires, and even in countries and regions where they didn't have empires.

“What we cannot do is build a time machine and go back into the past. It's time for us to start looking to the future.”

open image in gallery The prime minister’s comments came as King Charles embarked on a Caribbean tour ( Getty )

The UK has issued formal apologies for a number of historic wrongs, including its treatment of Windrush citizens, Bloody Sunday and the Hillsborough disaster.

Bur Mrs Badenoch has said she is “worried” that next week’s Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm) will be “yet another opportunity for people to start asking Britain for money”.

Asked what she believes would be the problem with Britain offering a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, Mrs Badenoch told Sky News: “It’s because of what will happen next.

“What I’m worried about is that this Chogm summit is yet another opportunity for people to start asking Britain for money because of the slave trade.”

open image in gallery Mrs Badenoch has said she is “worried” that next week’s Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm) will be “yet another opportunity for people to start asking Britain for money” ( AP )

She added: “We need to start looking at how we can bring the Commonwealth together – start looking forwards, not backwards.

“I don’t think we should be giving any money to compensate people for the slave trade, and I don’t think that Andy Burnham needs to be apologising because it is a lever to wedge open the door to ask for cash.”

Chancellor John Healey said Britons should not have to accept the financial liability for the slave trade “in which they had no role”.

He told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg programme: “The Prime Minister has said, look, we are open to a discussion about an apology.

“He feels that that’s the right thing, particularly ahead of the Commonwealth leaders’ conference.

“But he doesn’t believe that reparations are the right approach, and considering a formal apology doesn’t mean accepting that British people now should accept the financial liability for any part in things that happened hundreds of years ago, in which they had no role.”

News.title: Five teenage boys stabbed by 'unknown group' during Eastleigh Halloween party
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Five teenage boys have been seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party in Hampshire.

Police are asking for information about an “unknown group” involved in the incident.

The boys, aged 16 and 17, were found injured after police were called to a property in Eastleigh just after 10.30pm on Saturday.

All were taken to hospital with serious injuries, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said.

After officers arrived at the scene, it was established an “unknown group” had gained entry to a party at a property in Park Road.

An investigation was launched and scenes remain in place in Park Road and Valley Road.

open image in gallery The junction of Park Road and Valley Road in Eastleigh ( Google )

Senior investigating officer DCI Elizabeth Pirie said: "We are already hard at work identifying anyone who was at the party who may be able to assist our enquiries, whether that be having directly witnessed what took place, having filmed any footage which may be relevant, or who may be able to help us identify the unknown group.

"I understand the response the local community may have to hearing about this incident this morning, and I do not underestimate the impact our scenes will be having on those living in the area. These scenes are vitally important for our enquiries and we are grateful to the understanding of our communities whilst we work to establish the facts.

"If you do have any concerns or information, then please do not hesitate to speak to us.

"We particularly want to hear from anyone who can provide information to support our investigation. If you were at the party and have not spoken with officers yet, or you have any CCTV, mobile phone, dash cam or doorbell camera footage covering Park Road and the surrounding area, then please get in touch.

"Any information, however small it may seem, could help our enquiries."

The force said they were interested in speaking to anyone who attended the party or has footage, including doorbell camera footage covering Park Road and the surrounding area.

Liz Jarvis, MP for Eastleigh, said on X on Sunday: “My thoughts are with the victims and their families and all those affected by the incident in Chandler’s Ford last night, and my thanks go to our local police and emergency services for their prompt response.

“It’s important not to speculate or share unverified information.”
