News.title: Americans face higher costs and fewer options as Affordable Care Act open enrollment begins
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Affordable Care Act open enrollment has begun and Americans face higher costs and fewer healthcare coverage options.

The open enrollment window for the marketplace, also known as Obamacare, opens on Sunday in most states and closes on Jan. 15.

Health insurance bought through the Affordable Care Act marketplaces is expected to cost 13% more on average in 2027, according to an analysis of new CMS data by the healthcare research nonprofit KFF.

Aside from higher premiums and fewer coverage options in 2027, anyone planning to sign up should also brace for expiring financial assistance, rising rates, potential delays in working with a broker, new restrictions on immigrants, and stricter enrollment checks.

Financial help, including premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions, is now restricted for many groups of people who were previously eligible. Healthcare experts predict less coverage and higher prices across the board.

Increases are driven by multiple factors

Cynthia Cox, a vice president and director of the ACA program at KFF, said the increase is primarily driven by rising healthcare costs, hospital market concentration, and potential factors such as the No Surprises Act, which took effect in 2022 and bans surprise billing, or the rising availability of GLP-1 drugs.

open image in gallery The Trump administration has been removing ACA enrollees from the program as part of the ongoing campaign against what it characterizes as waste, fraud and abuse ( AFP/Getty )

The people who will be most affected by the new increases are those who do not qualify for a subsidy.

“They may or may not be able to afford to continue to keep their coverage into next year,” Cox said, adding that “a lot of them have already moved into bronze plans, which are the cheapest plans."

A CMS fact sheet about open enrollment distributed Friday says “Americans using HealthCare.gov will have robust access to low-cost plans.”

The price of ACA insurance has skyrocketed for many people during Trump's second term after Republicans opposed extending COVID-era subsidies that had helped offset the costs of health insurance for most enrollees during Democratic President Joe Biden's administration.

That resulted in 1.2 million fewer people signing up for coverage in the exchanges.

Nearly 20 million people in US are actively enrolled in ACA plans

As of February, roughly 19.2 million people in the United States were actively enrolled in ACA marketplace health plans, according to the Department of Health and Human Services website.

The number of enrollees grew during the COVID-19 pandemic, when enhanced subsidies became available through the American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act, both signed into law by Biden.

New regulations starting in 2027 will also limit tax credits for certain lawfully present immigrants, which could result in an additional 1 million uninsured individuals over time.

The Trump administration has also been removing ACA enrollees from the program as part of its ongoing campaign against what it characterizes as waste, fraud and abuse.

In September, Vice President JD Vance and other officials in the Republican administration announced plans to remove 760,000 ACA enrollees from public healthcare exchanges, alleging the individuals were fraudulently enrolled in the program or simply did not exist.

Vance said the discovery and canceled subsidy payments for hundreds of thousands of people from the exchanges, part of an administration-wide crackdown on fraud, would result in $2.2 billion in cost savings.

It's unclear how many more people will drop off of ACA coverage in 2027, Cox said.

But with higher premiums, immigration eligibility changes and the anti-fraud efforts, “I think there’s going to be fewer people enrolled in this market, but it’s going to be harder to understand why.”

News.title: Treasury minister criticised for suggesting employers are not ‘working people’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Treasury minister has come under fire after suggesting that employers are not “working people”.

Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds faced the criticism over her remarks, which have reignited a row over Labour’s definition of the term.

The controversy stems from an interview on GB News on Sunday, in which Ms Reynolds was questioned about people hit by Labour’s economic policies.

She told the broadcaster: “I don’t think employers are working people, they are companies.”

Later in the interview, host Camilla Tominey asked whether, because she employed a cleaner, she was not a working person.

Ms Reynolds replied: “No, but you’re an employee probably of your company, and I’m saying there is a difference between employers and employees.”

The party’s 2024 manifesto included a pledge not to raise taxes on working people, including through VAT, national insurance, and income tax.

The exchange has revived the debate about who Labour considers to fall into that category.

open image in gallery Chief Secretary to the Treasury Emma Reynolds (right) spoke out the day after Chancellor John Healey (centre) announced his Budge. ( PA )

In October 2024, former chancellor Rachel Reeves increased the employers’ rate of national insurance, which led to accusations of a manifesto breach.

Ministers argued at the time that it was not a breach, because it hit employers, not employees.

Ms Reynolds told the broadcaster: “In the manifesto, we were clear that we would not increase the headline rate of income tax, which we haven’t done, and we haven’t increased VAT, and we haven’t increased national insurance for employees.”

Tory shadow business minister Bradley Thomas commented on the clip on X: “Labour’s patronising, out-of-touch, politics of envy on display here from Minister Emma Reynolds.

“What about the thousands of small businesses who employ people? The electrician who works but takes on apprentices? The florist who runs her shop and has a young person work a few hours on weekends?

“The list is endless and so is Labour’s vindictiveness and denial of reality.”

Shadow work and pensions minister Helen Whately said: “This attitude is why Labour is killing our economy. They don’t understand businesses are built by hard graft. By working people.”

Shadow defence secretary James Cartlidge wrote: “Employers aren’t working people??

“Employing people is one of the hardest jobs there is. And Labour are making it harder.

“Building the team to make a business grow is rewarding but also a massive challenge – be great if someone in Labour understood this.”

Reform UK Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “Labour don’t think employers are working people.

“Tell that to the millions of small business owners who employ people.

“Labour haven’t a clue about business.”

Ms Reynolds was also challenged during the interview over landlords and savers being hit by an extra two percentage points added to income tax on property and savings income.

She defended measures announced by Chancellor John Healey on Wednesday.

She said: “We made a very conscious decision in this Budget for the tax increases to be targeted and fair.

“We increased the corporation tax on banks in order to pay for the breathing space measures for families, particularly the £100 energy support package for families in council tax bands A to D, taking VAT off electricity for a further three months, and also extending the fuel duty cut.”

The Treasury has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Alaska attorneys say 'meritless' Trump demand to set aside Senate ballots is 'disturbing and impossible'
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Alaska's Republican-run state government urged a federal judge on Saturday to dismiss a Trump administration lawsuit to stop the certification of a possible Democratic win in that state's pivotal U.S. Senate race, writing that there is “no reason for this Court to entertain this meritless lawsuit any longer.”

The scathing filing from the state's attorney general's office comes as U.S. District Court Judge Sharon L. Gleason set a deadline of Saturday for arguments over whether she should dismiss the lawsuit without even a hearing.

The complaint from the U.S. Department of Justice has been roundly criticized by election law experts and demands that the judge halt certification of a possible win by Democrat Mary Peltola until it is determined whether voters were confused by the presence of a second candidate on the ballot with the same name as her main rival, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan.

The Department of Justice on Friday added a request that the judge separate all ballots showing votes for the second Dan Sullivan until it can be determined whether voters were fooled into wasting their votes for a spoiler candidate. In its Saturday filing, Alaska said this was "both disturbing and impossible.” It added there would be no way to do that without violating voter privacy.

open image in gallery Trump’s DOJ filed a lawsuit in an effort to halt certification of a possible win by Democrat Mary Peltola until it is determined whether voters were confused by the presence of a second candidate on the ballot with the same name as her main rival, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan ( AP )

Trump has also demanded that Peltola be prosecuted after The New York Times this week reported that internal texts and posts appear to show the Democrats' campaign was involved in recruiting the second Sullivan, a retired school teacher in the remote fishing village of Petersburg, onto the ballot. But the state filing notes that the two Sullivans are distinguished from each other on the ballot — the senator is listed as a Republican and the incumbent, while the other simply as “Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.”

“State officials carefully designed the ballot to minimize voter confusion,” Alaska officials wrote. “The Court should immediately dismiss this lawsuit with prejudice and allow state officials to conduct the general election — including ballot counting and certification — free from unwarranted federal interference.”

The Trump administration argued that a preamble to the 1990s law governing voter registration gave it the responsibility for ensuring states maintained the “integrity” of federal elections. It has said it’s simply trying to combat fraud by preventing the Democrat from being declared the victor in a race that could determine which party controls the U.S. Senate.

The Department of Justice issued a wave of subpoenas and announced it was conducting a criminal investigation in the case as the administration has stepped up its use of its legal powers to support Trump's side in the midterm election.

Peltola has denied involvement in the presence of the second Sullivan on the ballot. The Times report was based on interviews with her former campaign manager, texts and contributions from a political group backing Peltola to an out-of-state Democratic consultant who recruited the second Sullivan.

open image in gallery Trump has called for the Democratic candidate to face charges over allegations she recruited Dan J. Sullivan, which she denies ( AFP/Getty )

Alaska’s Republican governor, Mike Dunleavy, who announced a state probe into the situation after the Times story, has condemned the placement of the second Sullivan on the ballot. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled this summer that the second candidate fulfilled all legal requirements to stay on. The state government’s filing on Saturday says that the new revelations about the possible role of Peltola’s campaign don’t change the fact that he’s legally on the ballot.

“Not every wrong can be righted in federal court,” the state wrote.

Peltola's campaign and voting rights groups also have urged Gleason to dismiss the case, putting them in unusual alignment with Alaska state officials.

“Imagine if the federal executive could pluck a few words like ‘election integrity’ from some statutory preamble and, on that basis alone, bend the machinery of state elections to his will, preemptively blocking certification of a U.S. Senate election to protect his preferred candidate from defeat and then subjecting voters to a law-enforcement-led inquest about who they ‘really’ supported,” the American Civil Liberties Union wrote in a filing urging the lawsuit's dismissal.

“Imagine that world and ask whether it is what the Framers wanted or precisely what they most feared.”

News.title: Falkirk stun Celtic for first time in 19 years to open up title race
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made 10 saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in 10 matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

open image in gallery Ethan Ross scored an early goal ( PA )

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

open image in gallery Falkirk stunned Celtic for the first time in 19 years ( PA )

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s No 1’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

PA

News.title: Police investigate pig heads left in park in ‘disturbing and disgusting’ display
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Police are investigating after real pig heads were discovered in a public park in Northern Ireland in a “disturbing and disgusting” display.

One pig’s head was driven onto a wooden stake, and another was left on the ground, along with a sign with the words “here piggy piggy” spray-painted in red.

Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) has confirmed it is investigating the incident in Kilbroney Park in Rostrevor, County Down, after the heads appeared on Saturday morning. Officers are keeping an open mind as to the motivation.

Independent councillor for the Newry, Mourne and Down District Council, Mark Gibbons, has condemned the “disturbing and disgusting” incident.

“Leaving real pigs’ heads in Kilbroney Park is vile, sickening and utterly disgraceful,” he wrote on Facebook.

“Halloween is no excuse for such a revolting act. This is a public space used by families and children. Whoever is responsible should be ashamed.”

He said he will not be sharing a “disturbing” image of the discovery, adding: “Such a disgusting and disturbing thing to do. Imagine a child seeing this?”

open image in gallery Police have appealed for information following the discovery ( PA Archive )

Families were urged to stay away from the area in a social media post on Saturday, which alerted park users to the “deeply disturbing display”.

The warning on Friends of the Meadow & Kilbroney Forest Park, Rostrevor, added: “We ask members of the public, particularly families with children and those walking dogs, to please avoid the area for the time being to allow the relevant authorities to deal with the situation.

“Friends of the Meadow unequivocally condemns this behaviour. Our meadow is a shared community space, enjoyed by people of all ages, and such disturbing and unacceptable actions have no place here in Rostrevor.”

One dog walker told the BBC of his shock, adding: “This is a public space used daily by families, young children and people walking their dogs. Whatever the intention behind it, leaving animal remains on display like this is completely unacceptable.”

He said whether it was a Halloween prank or not, “it's crossed the line from harmless fun to something disgusting”.

“There's absolutely no need for this in a public park,” he added. “It's disturbing, unhygienic and shows a complete lack of consideration for everyone else using the space.”

A spokesperson for PSNI confirmed the force has launched a probe and appealed for anyone with information to come forward, adding: “The items have been removed and enquiries are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

“Officers are keeping an open mind as to the motivation behind this report, and are considering all potential lines of enquiry. We also continue to liaise with the local council.”

Anyone with information can contact police on 101, quoting reference number 326 31/10/26, or report online at: https://reporting.psni.police.uk/appeals

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

News.title: Brighton underline title credentials with impressive win over Man City
News.content:
This Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

News.title: Man Utd the masters of self-destruction as pressure piles on Carrick
News.content:
The strange thing is this could and probably should have been a day when they at least stopped the rot for a few days. But more non-existent defending and brainlessness from Martinez, who was sent off for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face, put paid to that in a second half in which Carrick admitted United “unravelled”.

Chelsea were cut open on at least five occasions in a see-saw first half and Matheus Cunha also had a goal disallowed for a narrow offside. Xabi Alonso’s side had opportunities of their own – you will always get them against this United team – but they were second best and lucky not to be behind. Everyone talks about United being there for the taking, but the truth is Chelsea, coming off the back of a miserable defeat to Spurs and Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool, were here.

The problem is Carrick’s team could not hit a barn door at the moment. They have scored just three goals in their last six league games and that lack of cutting edge was evident in the way Bruno Fernandes, back in the team as captain, and Amad Diallo (dangerous but with no end product) wasted excellent chances. That wastefulness would put pressure on any back line, let alone one with all the fortitude of wet cardboard. Chelsea were spared and exploited it with the help of the second and most corrosive acts of United’s self-mutilation.

We will come to Martinez’s sending off in a moment, but there had already been a cowardly act of a different kind from the Argentine defender before then in the lead-up to Chelsea’s opening goal soon after the restart.

Take nothing away from Morgan Rogers – his 40yd dash from the edge of the centre circle in United’s half to the six-yard box and the finish that followed were top notch. But where was the challenge? How could not a single player in red have stood in his path? “Come on Morgan, run through us buddy” seemed to be the message.

News.title: Red Roses cruise to dominant victory over United States in final WXV game
News.content:
English rugby chiefs have been on a charm offensive in the United States this week, but the players on the pitch opted for more of a brute-force approach.

The Red Roses were in the unfamiliar position of coming off the back of successive defeats and Meg Jones had called on her team to respond. They certainly did that, looking far more like world champions than they have over the past fortnight with a convincing nine-try win – four of them scored by Claudia Moloney-MacDonald – albeit there is still room for them to “grow”, as Jones put it after the game.

That is what the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have been trying to do off the field. Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, and his colleagues used this fixture in New Jersey as an opportunity to tap into the US market by “creating connections” with business leaders and potential investors.

It is little wonder English rugby is trying to get a piece of the American pie. There are an ever-growing number of US owners in British football and with the US hosting the men’s and women’s Rugby World Cups in 2031 and 2033 interest in the oval-ball game is sure to grow too, although the sparse crowd in New Jersey would suggest there is work to do on that front.

News.title: Embarrassing England on brink of historic World Cup exit
News.content:
It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

McDermott is not blameless. The directives were clearly to offload when they could, and perhaps when they should not have, and the call to start Jez Litten over Brad O’Neill at hooker was, on reflection, a mistake. Litten has so much more impact off the bench and the Hull KR livewire could have been the spark England required when it proceeded to fall flat. It was also strange to see Lewis coming on in the No 9 role.

Yet it must be noted that this was just McDermott’s third match in charge and that Tonga was his first. With no warm-up game and with his English-based players at a disadvantage because of travel and the jet lag, that all-important opener was appallingly timed. Yet having been a member of the exclusive top three for so long, England must now concede they are merely in the top five. This tournament proved as much.

Sports.title: EFL cult hero performs shock retirement U-turn as he joins new club just WEEKS after hanging up boots live on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
Next

EFL cult hero Billy Sharp has sensationally returned to football just weeks after announcing his retirement.

Sharp has re-signed for former club Rushden and Diamonds, who he played for back in 2005.



It comes after the 40-year-old announced his retirement from football LIVE on TV just weeks ago.

Rushden and Diamonds confirmed the signing on their socials on Sunday.



The club, who play in the eighth tier, posted: “After 21 years away, AFC Rushden & Diamonds are excited to announce that Billy Sharp becomes a Diamond once again. Billy scored the first of his 299 goals for Rushden & Diamonds back in 2005.

“The man who put the ball in the cobblers net, has 299 career goals spanning over 22 years. Featuring for RDFC, Sheffield United, Doncaster Rovers, Southampton, & Scunthorpe to name a few!



“Billy comes in to help the Club with James Clifton being suspended and we can’t wait to see him pull on the shirt one final time as we go to Burton Albion in the FA Cup 1st Round Proper for the first time ever in AFC Rushden & Diamonds history.”

So it appears to be one last dance for Sharp, who will play for his ex-club one last time, but in the FA Cup.

The Diamonds will be seeking to stage an upset as they travel to Burton Albion on Saturday November 7.

The sides are separated by five divisions, but Sharp will be hoping for some FA Cup magic in his final ever competitive game.

It comes as a surprise after his retirement just weeks ago on Sky Sports.

Perhaps he wants one more goal to reach the elusive 300 career goals, after bowing out on 299.

Sports.title: ‘When you accidentally press square’ – Andrey Santos trolled for ‘pretend tackle’ in Man Utd’s defeat at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Next

ANDREY SANTOS made a nightmare return to Chelsea on Saturday – and the Manchester United midfielder was brutally slammed on social media.

The Brazilian, 22, swapped Stamford Bridge for Old Trafford when he sealed a monster £50million move in the summer.

But Santos could not stop United falling to a 2-0 defeat when he headed back to his former club for the first time.



And the midfielder was ruthlessly trolled after Morgan Rogers gave Chelsea the lead.



Santos made a wayward sliding challenge as the Blues’ livewire ran unopposed into the penalty area.

Fans raced onto social media to poke fun at the ex-Strasbourg loanee as he failed to get close to stopping Rogers in his tracks.

One, comparing the incident to video gameplay, said: “When you accidentally press square.”



Another added: “What was that pretend tackle by Santos?”

A third chimed in: “Literally looks like on Fifa where the game won’t switch to the right player so the opponent can just run straight through.”

A fourth noted: “That’s a Brazil international right there.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And a fifth claimed: “Looks like a glitch in the Matrix or something.”



Santos has come under fire since his mega-money move to United – with it emerging that he was not among their first-choice targets.

Red Devils chief Michael Carrick initially wanted Elliot Anderson, Mateus Fernandes, Aurelien Tchouameni and Ederson before raiding Chelsea.

And Santos was hauled off just after the hour mark as United desperately looked for a route back into their showdown with the West Londoners.



But, following Rogers’ opener, Chelsea were handed a golden opportunity to double their lead when Lisandro Martinez was sent off following a moment of madness.

Cole Palmer dispatched the resulting penalty and United ended up making it nine games without a win.

Sports.title: Vile football fans ‘taunt’ Sunderland supporters with Bradley Lowery photo – as mum blasts ‘cruel’ act
Sports.content:
Next

SICK football fans have been caught taunting Sunderland supporters with a photo of Bradley Lowery during a match.

Videos circulating online show the fans mocking a picture of Bradley, a six-year-old who died from cancer in 2017, during a Coventry City FC game against Sunderland.



The boys can be seen sneering and pointing at the image, as appalled onlookers record the tasteless taunt.

Coventry City FC released a statement: “Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.



“The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.”

A video of the vile stunt posted by Sunderland’s Roker Report racked up over 11m views on X, with the caption: “Disgusting. Let’s make this a****** famous”.

It follows a similar incident in 2023, which saw Sheffield Wednesday fans arrested for mocking the six-year-old, who was diagnosed with the disease at just 18 months.

Photos show the men laughing as they brandish a picture of Bradley, causing outrage online with dozens calling for the pair to be banned.



Mum Gemma Lowery has spoken out against the footage which emerged during the Premier League game on Saturday.

In a heart-wrenching statement shared through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, she said: “My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate.

“Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters.

“As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

“I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun.



“Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

“So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

“To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.”

The nation were left devastated by Bradley’s death in 2017.

He was diagnosed with the disease before the age of two, with tumours spreading through his chest, lungs, lymph nodes, bones and bone marrow.



After undergoing major surgery and chemotherapy, Bradley pulled through and went into remission for 18 months.

But the cancer tragically returned.

More than £700,000 was raised to send him to the US for special antibody treatment.

But in December 2016, his family were dealt the crushing blow that his disease was terminal and the US treatment would only give them more time.

Brave Bradley underwent radical immuno-therapy treatment at Great Ormond Street Hospital as a last chance, but sadly didn’t make it.



Mum Gemma revealed Bradley had passed away on July 7, 2017, in a Facebook post paying tribute to “our little superhero”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

West Midlands Police have been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Geoffrey Richmond dead at 85: Ex-Premier League club chairman behind Bradford’s incredible rise dies as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
Icon gone Geoffrey Richmond dead at 85: Ex-Premier League club chairman behind Bradford’s incredible rise dies as tributes pour in







Next

BRADFORD have announced the sad news that former chairman Geoffrey Richmond has died.

Richmond passed away at the age of 85 on Friday.



Richmond was born in Leeds and became the Bradford chairman in 1994.

His first act was to lend the club £2.3million to clear its debts.



The Richmond era at Valley Parade ushered in the club’s most successful period.

He oversaw their first-ever Wembley appearance in the 1996 Second Division play-off final.



And in the 1998/99 season they earned promotion to the Premier League.

Their stay in the top flight proved to be short-lived, with the club relegated in 2001.

Richmond then resigned when the club subsequently went into administration in 2002 after losing the confidence of the fans.

He recalled: “I went into my office on the following Monday and cleared my desk.



“As I drove away, I was in tears… I have never been back since.”

Their financial ruin was put down to heavy spending in their second Premier League season and the collapse of ITV Digital.

Richmond himself was declared bankrupt in 2004.

Bantams fans paid tribute to Richmond on social media, one said: “The only owner to have the minerals to do what he said he’d do, RIP Geoffrey.”

A second said: “RIP the only man who’s been in charge of the club who allowed us all to dream, & made the previously impossible possible.”



A third added: “Rest in peace Geoffrey. Thank you for giving us the dream and realising the potential of not just the club, but the city itself. Promotions, Wembley, Stuart coming back and the best attacking team I’ve ever seen at Valley Parade.”

Another said: “Lived the dream and delivered our club to the Premier League and into Europe. Personified there never being a dull moment at this club.”

A fifth added: “Sad to hear of the passing of Geoffrey Richmond. Simply put, the most influential owner our club ever had, for good and bad. Took us to dizzy heights then back to the depths. Still wouldn’t change 1995-2000 though. Thanks for the journey Mr Richmond.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bradford, now in League One, said in a statement: “Former Bradford City AFC chairman Geoffrey Richmond has sadly passed away. Our thoughts are with his family and friends at this time.”

Richmond had four children, three from his first marriage with Barbara, and then a son with his second wife, Elizabeth.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick’s Man Utd on collision course for relegation as they match horror record from disastrous 1973/74 season
Sports.content:
Next

MAKE no mistake, Manchester United are on a collision course towards relegation.

And it doesn’t matter who the manager is.



It is fair to say it is unlikely to be Michael Carrick after Chelsea’s 2-0 victory made it NINE games without a win and four defeats from five.

United have failed to win any of their first seven away games in all competitions for the first time since, you guessed it, 1973-74 – when they were last relegated from the top division.



Handy defeats suffered by Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Nottingham Forest kept United 17th and level on points with the Eagles.

Not since November 1986 have United been in the bottom three past August.



As each game passes, a new record is shattered and a new low hit, making the idea of relegation not to be scoffed at.

United, whose only league win this season came against newly-promoted Ipswich Town on August 30, have picked up just seven points from a possible 27, averaging 0.77 points-per-game.

That adds to 29.3 points over the course of a 38-game season and no team has ever survived the drop with fewer than 30.

Maybe the players are panicked, too.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Lisandro Martinez, sent off at Chelsea, appears to be begging to leave in January. Perhaps Bruno Fernandes is heading for the door after the New Year, too.

The Old Trafford skipper, teary-eyed at Stamford Bridge, would go from a Bryan Robson figure – a star in an underperforming United side – to nothing if he captains this lot to the Championship.

The running joke is whether a massive points deduction for City, if the club loses its appeal against more than 100 guilty charges for breaking financial rules, would be enough to keep United up.



Manchester derby in the Championship, anyone?

Many have pointed to that famous phrase: “Remember when United were ‘too good to go down’ in 74?”

George Best and Sir Bobby Charlton were months away from being relegated, both leaving in 74 and 73.

After Sir Matt Busby retired, a revolving door of managers—including Wilf McGuinness, Frank O’Farrell, and utimately Tommy Docherty struggled to find stability or control over a fractured dressing room.

The goals were non-existent 52 years ago. Just like they are now.



United have scored ten in the league this term, Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo with four each, Matheus Cunha has popped up with one and an Ipswich own goal was the other. That’s your lot.

United might have to go through the entire season without a recognised striker at this rate.

Their only natural No 9 Benjamin Sesko is set to be ruled out until January, with a different face popping up at false nine each game.



Sesko, even when fit last season, was not a starter under Carrick, who benefited from his impact off the bench. Sesko missed the final month of last term and all of pre-season.

Still, United did not spend any of their £163m summer cash on another striker and it’s nearly impossible to see where the goals will come from this season.

If United fail to beat Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday, it will be their joint-worst run of results in 75 years.

Not even the ’74 season would have been that bad form wise.

Sources say United chiefs privately agreed to try to reach the November international break before acting on Carrick’s position during crisis talks after Bournemouth’s 3-0 win last Sunday.



So, effectively, the biggest club in the country have made peace with writing off two results against Roma and Aston Villa to dither and dally.

United – under different directors before minority owners Ineos arrived – did the same with fellow club legend Ole Gunnar Solskjaer five years ago.

They forced the Norwegian to go through needless pain while they lined up a replacement.



Carrick has had an easy pass. Most are aware the rot starts from the top down and the players have either downed tools again or are not good enough.

However, Carrick’s shortcomings become more glaring with each passing game.

While Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said the midfield needed to be controlled after the break, Carrick spoke of “not getting going”.

Some supporters think relegation could be the catalyst for a change in ownership, hoping the owners could release their cash cow.

But in reality the Glazers would only want to sell when United are worth the most money, which would be when they are in the Prem.



Whatever the damage from the upstairs club, this squad should have too much quality to actually go down next May.

But the squad does lack the basic qualities teams need to survive the drop: fight, leadership, togetherness, desire and grit.

Refusing to be drawn on the matter, Carrick said: “We have got to keep moving forward and winning games, simple as that.”

Tottenham, when they were reigning Europa League champions after beating United in the 2025 final, survived on the final day last season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United finished 15th under Ruben Amorim, their lowest standing since recording eighth the year before.



Yet it feels there is a new low United could sink to. The once unthinkable joke is now a looming reality.

FERMIN LOPEZ has delivered a blunt response to Manchester United after being linked with a move to Old Trafford, insisting he wants to spend the rest of his career at Barcelona.

The Spanish midfielder was asked about the interest from United following Barca’s emphatic 6-1 victory over Alaves last night.



He said: “Manchester United links? I don’t pay attention to that kind of news. I want to stay here at Barcelona as long as possible.

“I hope to END my football career at this club and retire here.”



United are understood to be keen on adding more goals and creativity to their midfield options, with Lopez emerging as a reported target ahead of next summer.

Lopez, 23, has also attracted interest from Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain.

His comments will come as a blow to United, particularly with captain Bruno Fernandes entering the final year of his contract and the club potentially needing to consider long-term options in that position.

Lopez was also linked with a move to Chelsea in the summer of 2025, when the Blues reportedly saw a £40million offer rejected by Barcelona.

He enjoyed a sensational campaign last season, recording 30 goal involvements in all competitions, with only Fernandes (31) managing more among players in Europe’s top five leagues.

The midfielder has continued that form this season and was at the heart of Barcelona’s demolition of Alaves, scoring once and providing two assists as they ran out 6-1 winners at the Camp Nou.

ROY KEANE has become a grandfather again after his son, Aidan, celebrated the birth of his first child.

Patsy, who is the wife of the Premier League icon’s son, announced the wonderful news in a TikTok video posted on Saturday.



Keane‘s daughter-in-law shared a video with a black-and-white filter displaying her baby bump which then changed to show their newborn daughter.

The post was captioned: “Heaven sent us an angel girl.”



The mention of heaven in the caption is possibly a reference to Patsy’s late mother, who sadly passed away shortly after their wedding.

Aidan and Patsy, who tied the knot last October, first announced they were expecting a baby in April of this year.



Patsy shared a video to social media showing her revealing the news to Aidan.

Congratulations were quick to come in from those who saw the video, with one saying: “Congrats to you all.”

A second said: “Amazing, congratulations.”

A third added: “Mama sent you this angel girl.”



The latest addition to the Keane family, whose name was not announced publicly, is the fifth grandchild for Keane and his wife, Theresa.

The ex-Manchester United, Nottingham Forest and Republic of Ireland star-turned Sky Sports pundit has been married to Theresa for almost 30 years.

They are the parents to five children: Aidan – the third eldest – and daughters Shannon, Leah, Alanna, and Caragh.

Last year, Leah – who is married to Southampton defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis – welcomed her first child back in December, a baby girl called Iris.

Dart's brilliant week in Guangzhou

After qualifying for this year's main draw, Dart defeated Tatiana Prozorova, No 2 seed Janice Tjen, No 5 seed Paula Badosa and 16-year-old wild card Sun Xinran to make her first career WTA Tour final



Before this week, her best Tour-level finish had been a semi-final run at 2024 Cluj-Napoca, losing to eventual champion Karolina Pliskova



Dart has risen from world No 115 to 83 in the live rankings; this time last year was ranked No 224. She reached career-high ranking of No 70 in September 2024



The 30-year-old from Hampstead broke back for 4-4, but Tagger hit straight back before wrapping up the first set.

The first break point of the second set came the way of Dart, who took it for 5-3 on her way to levelling the match.

However, Dart wiped that miss from her mind to serve out the match to 15, falling on her back in delight when victory was sealed with an unreturned serve.

She said on court: "I'll try not to get too emotional. A big thank you to my team this week. My boyfriend Stephen [Falck], my fitness coach Dario, but also the people at home. My coach Marion, really appreciate all your hard work, but also my family, my parents and my sister Phoebe.

"It's amazing to play in front of such a big crowd. It's been so much fun here and I really appreciate it and hope to be back next year."

She was introduced to tennis aged seven by her parents at the club they met at Cumberland LTC



Supports Arsenal



She splits her time between Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and London



Dart is dating Norwegian model Stephen Falck, who is also now her agent. Falck is a model and software engineer from Norway

An established member of the GB Billie Jean King Cup team, Dart is also a talented doubles player - having won one WTA 250 and two WTA 125 titles.

Sports.title: European champion Mageean dies aged 34
Sports.content:
Ciara Mageean: Ireland's European 1500 metres gold medallist dies at the age of 34 after battling cancer

Ciara Mageean has died aged 34

Ireland's European 1500 metres gold medallist Ciara Mageean has died at the age of 34.

Two-time Olympian Mageean, who won the European title in Rome in 2024, announced last year she had been diagnosed with cancer.

A statement on her Instagram account on Sunday read: "At 6:30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones. A beloved daughter, sister, wife, friend and inspiration to so many, she will be deeply missed."

A statement from Athletics Ireland read: "Athletics Ireland is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Ciara Mageean.

"Ciara was a much-loved and inspirational figure who touched the lives of so many. Her courage, warmth and spirit will leave a lasting legacy.

"The thoughts and heartfelt condolences of everyone at Athletics Ireland are with Ciara's family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.

"May she rest in peace."

Athletes from across the world of sport flooded the post with tributes.

Australian Olympic 1500m silver medallist Jess Hull wrote: "There are no words. Just the most beautiful person in every way imaginable.

"You will be so missed, our hearts and love are with Tommy and your family. Lucky to have shared some miles with you but even more special to have celebrated milestones at the finish line together, I'm so grateful for every moment, rest easy Ciara."

Scottish distance runner Eilish McColgan said: "Sending so much love and strength to all your closest. A remarkable person."

Jake Wightman, the 2022 world 1500m champion, shared the post in an Instagram story alongside the caption: "So sad to read this. A real bright light from our sport and the world gone. RIP Ciara."

Republic of Ireland footballer Amber Barrett wrote: "Devastated. A light of elegance and grace. Jesus Ciara, you've broken a nation. God rest your soul. I'm blessed to have had you in my life."

Barrett's team-mate and Republic captain Katie McCabe added on X: "Truly heartbreaking news to hear about Ciara this morning. Sending all my love & prayers to her loved ones during this incredibly difficult time. We were so lucky to have such an incredible athlete represent our country with so much pride. May she rest in peace."

Mageean, from Portaferry, County Down, in Northern Ireland, was married last month.

Mageean, who competed at the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 Olympics, also won European 1500m silver in 2022 and bronze in 2016, while she finished fourth in the World Championships in 2023.

She won silver competing for Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games in Birmingham in 2022.

A British Athletics statement read: "Everyone at British Athletics sends our thoughts and condolences to Ciara Mageean's family, friends, and coaches and all our friends at Athletics Ireland at this incredibly sad time.

"Ciara was a true inspiration on and off the track, may she rest in peace."

Sports.title: England out of World Cup after Tonga edge out Samoa
Sports.content:
England's elimination from the World Cup was confirmed after Tonga beat Samoa 20-18 in the final group match.

England sealed a 34-12 victory against Papua New Guinea on Friday but needed to win by a big margin to give themselves a chance of leapfrogging Samoa in Pool B and C and advancing to the semi-finals on points difference.

Brian McDermott's side's hopes rested on Tonga to win by more than 46 points to reach the last four for the seventh successive tournament.

Instead they are on the plane home from Australasia despite winning two of their three matches.

The 30-12 defeat by Tonga in the opening match proved costly, with an 82-0 win over France leaving England with 68 points to make up on Samoa.

They failed to make significant enough inroads in the 32-10 win over Papua New Guinea.

English hopes briefly flickered when Tonga led 8-0, Robert Toia scoring the opening try after a near 50-metre sprint.

With Isaiya Katoa converting and then kicking a penalty, England just needed Tonga to score another 39 unanswered points to stay in the tournament.

However, Brian To'o's try hauled Samoa back to 8-4 down at half-time.

Jojo Fifita put Tonga 14-4 ahead before To'o, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and Ronald Volkman edged Samoa into a two-point lead, only for Addin Fonua-Blake to win it for Tonga.

Tonga will play New Zealand in the last four, while Samoa will face Australia in a repeat of the 2022 final.

Is the Rugby League World Cup format flawed?

Image: England's defeat by Tonga in the opening match proved costly

The new tournament structure, which has been downsized from 16 teams to 10, came after Australia stepped in as hosts following France's withdrawal in 2023 for financial reasons.

It has effectively meant that each group game in Pool B and C has carried more jeopardy than before.

The tournament has two pools, one featuring four teams - Australia, New Zealand, Cook Islands and Fiji - and the other featuring six teams.

England were drawn in the second group, Pool B and C, alongside Tonga, Samoa, Papua New Guinea, Lebanon and France.

The top two teams from each group qualify for the knockout rounds, and in the event of a tie, teams are judged on their head-to-head record before points difference.

McDermott's side were beaten in their first match against Tonga which put their hopes of qualifying in the balance, despite later thrashing France by 82 points in round two.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Wilkin believes the structure of the Rugby League World Cup was 'fundamentally flawed'

Sky Sports' Jon Wilkin said: "Australia have done a great job to organise a tournament in such a short space of time, but it was fundamentally flawed, unfair in the extreme to the start.

"The actual competition structure is just diabolical. England were dealt an incredibly difficult task, because they essentially played their quarter-final in week one."

"England knew after their loss against Tonga that it was all going to be about points difference, and [qualifying] was going to be incredibly difficult," Wilkin said. "I think the structure and the setup of the competition was done in short notice.

"I think the International Rugby League, who set up this tournament, have done an incredible job to get it on and actually and get in a position where we can have the tournament.

"So, I commend them for that, but I just think the tournament structure is laughable. Like, no quarter-finals? There's a number of ways you could have manufactured or engineered a quarter-finals situation.

"England should be in the quarter-finals, of the World Cup. They had a disappointing 30-40 minutes against Tonga, and they're out."

RFL invites England legends to discuss national sides' international future

Image: Adrian Morley will be among the names to help map out a future for the national game

Some of the greatest players in England's modern history will convene to help map out a future for the national game, including further analysis of the pyramid, from grassroots and pathways to the player pool for the international stage.

After the disappointment of seeing England miss out on the World Cup semi-finals across both the men's and women's competition, recently-appointed RFL Chief Executive Ian Nolan has decided to call upon the knowledge of a raft of stellar quality to form an in-depth discussion on national performance.

Former Great Britain captain Paul Sculthorpe MBE and iconic forward Adrian Morley are among the names of those who will now get together to look at what extra can be done to help make the England teams a genuine force.

They will be joined by Gareth Ellis, who played in the last Men's side from these shores to defeat world champions Australia in 2006 and works as a current assistant coach with York Knights, plus recently retired St Helens and England captain Jodie Cunningham who will bring valuable perspectives for the Women's and Girls' game.

Sports.title: Yamashita holds off Liu to defend her LPGA Maybank Championship title

Miyu Yamashita successfully defended her title at the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship on Sunday, beating China's Yan Liu by two strokes.

The Japanese golfer sank five birdies with just the one bogey at the par-4 ninth in a near-perfect week where she led from Friday's second round until the final hole.

With her team trailing by six points at the half, Williams got going in the third quarter, hitting shots from all over the court.

After scoring just two points in the first half, she had 15 points in the third quarter to give the Valkyries a 45-44 advantage heading into the final period.

The game was tied at 53 when Williams scored nine straight points for the Valkyries, including a deep 3-pointer that made it 60-57 with 2:18 left. It was a lead the team wouldn't relinquish.

She didn't just perform on the offensive end. Williams, who was runner-up for the league's Defensive Player of the Year, had four blocks, setting the tone early.

"It's incredible. She's a humble superstar. She's the reason we're here. At halftime she was like 'I just got to get going,'" Veronica Burton said of Williams. "Once she got going there was no stopping her. She hit shot after shot and got stop after stop. She gets it done on both sides of the floor."

Sports.title: Celtic stunned as Falkirk claim first win in 19 years
Sports.content:
Falkirk claimed their first win against Celtic since 2007 as the champions missed another chance to extend their lead in the Scottish Premiership title race.

Martin O'Neill made three changes as he looked for a response after Celtic's midweek draw with Dundee United, but they were outclassed by the Bairns, who extended their winning run to four matches.

Ethan Ross was gifted the opening goal just three minutes into the game. Ryan Strain sent a cross into the box and Cameron Carter-Vickers sent the ball straight to him to fire into the net.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ethan Ross gives Falkirk an early lead against Celtic after an error from Cameron Carter-Vickers.

Scott Bain was more than impressive against his former team, denying Camilo Duran and Hasseim Hassan before Falkirk stunned with their second, this time Scott Tanser beating Carter-Vickers before lashing the ball into the net.

The hosts had the ball in the net again after the break, but it was ruled out with VAR confirming the ball came off Jacob Murrell's arm before crossing the line.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Falkirk's Jacob Murrell thought he had given Falkirk a 3-0 lead against Celtic but it was disallowed for handball.

Celtic piled on the pressure late on, but could not find a way past Bain as Falkirk moved up to fourth in the Premiership.

The Hoops remain four points clear of title rivals Rangers having played a game more.

More to follow...

Sports.title: USA's Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at Mexico Open
Sports.content:
Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open.

About the only thing Novak did wrong at Vidanta Vallarta was losing the handle on a club twirl at the par-five 12th while admiring a 279-yard shot that settled 20 feet away for an eagle.

That was part of his sublime stretch of three birdies and an eagle that extended his lead to seven shots. It was such a great day for Novak that even when he had a lie in the rough with a golf ball well below his feet, he hammered that out to six feet on the 14th for a birdie.

Novak ended the day on a 23-under 190, primed for his first individual title on the PGA Tour. His only other victory was teaming with Ben Griffin in the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year.

He had the low round of the day while playing in the last group, and goes into the final round coming off scores of 61-62.

"Very much the same, maybe a little sloppy at the end," Novak said of the two rounds. "But the putter saved it."

He holed a six-foot par on the 16th and made a 10-foot par putt on the 17th after coming up short.

Matthieu Pavon of France birdied his last two holes for a 65 to get within six shots. Doug Ghim had a 64 and was another shot behind.

"It makes it easier for me to be in my own bubble because I know that something significant would probably need to happen for me to have a chance tomorrow," Ghim said. "I'll do my best to put any pressure on him and see what happens."

Pavon needs something special, too, though he already is having a good week if he can hold his position. His two-year exemption from winning at Torrey Pines in 2024 runs out this year. Pavon came to the Mexico Open at No 140 in the FedEx Cup. A runner-up finish would move him just inside the top 100.

Image: The USA's Andrew Novak enjoyed another stellar day at the Mexico Open on Saturday

Kihei Akina, a 20-year-old, settled down after a bogey-bogey start and posted a 68. He was nine shots behind in a tie for seventh. Another finish in the top 10 would give him another point in the PGA Tour University accelerated program.

Everyone is chasing Novak, who has made only three bogeys through 54 holes.

"You want to back up a really low round with something low, but you don't usually expect that," Novak said.

"You expect usually there's going to be some give, and you've just got to be patient with it the next day. I still kind of came out firing today, was throwing some darts, making putts and trying to stay out of my own way."

Sports.title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
So much of life is luck: when we’re born, where we’re born and to whom we’re born; the the skills we have; who we meet and when we meet them.

Liverpool have lost one game this season. On the Premier League’s opening weekend, they needed a penalty in ninth minute of injury time for a point at Newcastle, recently benefitted from Brentford having two players sent off and, in midweek, Emmanuel Emegha missed a penalty that would’ve sent Chelsea past them in the League Cup.

Arsenal, meanwhile, spent chunks of last season struggling to score from open play, benefiting from avant-garde refereeing calls at set-pieces – one in particular when the title felt in the balance – and the absence of high-class challengers. In the annals of champions, they are not proximate to the greatest, yet Mikel Arteta’s men have every chance of doing what Arsène Wenger’s legends could not: retain a league title.

That, though, is only half of the story. Just as being blessed with intelligence and looks, helpful neurochemistry and secure home environment, is nothing whatsoever to do with those lucky enough to experience them, so finding the devotion, composure, discipline and focus to exploit that happy chance is within our gift. Who we are is genetics and circumstance, but also, who we are is a choice we’re able to make every single day.

While Andoni Iraola bedded in as Liverpool manager, his team persevered in the early stages, making the most of the opportunities which presented to establish standards and momentum, such that now, with the new manager’s methods taking effect, they’re well placed to impose the natural talent that suffuses their squad.

Arsenal, meanwhile, became champions thanks principally to monomaniacal resolve, separating themselves from the rest with their unity and organisation. Without that, it wouldn’t have mattered what was going on elsewhere; because of it, they’ve earned the freedom to express themselves in more expansive style.

Consequently, this afternoon’s match should be a belter, two teams making the most of what they give and what’s been given to them. Liverpool play the faster, more improvisational game, with Arsenal bringing the solidity and certainty they lack; Arsenal are certain they can take the title, while Liverpool will be starting to think it possible.

For either side, a win today would be a statement – to themselves as much as to everyone else. And ultimately, for all that goes on around us, what really defines what we make of life is how we perceive ourselves.

Kick-off: 4.30pm GMT
