Sports.title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
Sports.content:
Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to prior to kick-off.

The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But the fact London City have even played their way into the conversation about this season’s title contenders in only their second WSL season is hugely impressive.

The Manchester City manager, Andrée Jeglertz, praised the ability of his team to win in different ways after three games in eight days. “We said afterwards, the players should be so proud of what they put into this game,” he said. “We’ve learned we’re a great team who can keep the ball for 75% of the game and win that way or we can win like this.

“That quality to win in different ways is good to have, but the players also have to adapt to that and feel it’s OK to not have the ball all the time, take pride in defending and only having three or four chances but finishing off those chances.”

Ahead of kick-off, cameras showed superstar summer signing Alexia Putellas opening the boot of her car and taking out a heavy leather-clad square item, her third Ballon d’Or trophy safely encased inside. The mercurial Spain midfielder did not present her trophy to fans in the stands ahead of kick-off, instead choosing to put it on display so supporters could queue to have photos taken with it.

The only nod to the player’s stunning individual year, in which she won the quadruple with Barcelona before joining London City, was on her feet, the geometric gold on her custom Ballon d’Or-themed boots glinting on their first outing.

There have been jokes aplenty about the unlikelihood of the world’s premier individual award heading to its new Bromley home. To reach the stadium from Hayes Lane, you pass a field of horses on your left. London City Lionesses are not Barcelona, and they have become the home of the Ballon d’Or winner by default rather than being the key component of that individual success.

Except, based on the season London City Lionesses are having and the ruthless ambitions of owner Michelle Kang, the idea that the club could produce a season that delivers them collective success and individual success off the back of it feels less distant than it did just a few short months ago.

Against the champions, London City more than held their own, the opportunity to move level on points with their opponents and league leaders Chelsea an inviting incentive. Their threat was evident within 30 seconds, when Manchester City’s defender Rebecca Knaak was forced to turn Lucía Corrales’s cross wide of the far post just ahead of a waiting Isobel Goodwin.

Neither team has impressed defensively this season, each only managing to keep one clean sheet in the WSL, and it made for a thrilling encounter, the high lines and aggressiveness of both attacks delivering a showstopper.

Making her first WSL start for the home team, with Elene Lete hitherto preferred, Mary Earps made a huge statement with an impressive double save from a Knaak header to keep the game goalless going into the break.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Mary Earps dives at the feet of Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

It was Manchester City that broke the deadlock despite London City dominating and it was their most influential player that delivered. Hemp flicked the ball into the run of Shaw and with her first touch, she took it past Earps before switching the ball on to her right foot and firing home to become the first player to score in eight consecutive WSL starts.

A deserved equaliser arrived in the 72nd minute, when Fernández was at the near post to meet a corner and her assured header sent the ball looping in at the back post.

The celebrations were emphatic but they were very short-lived. This is a new, more resilient Manchester City, one that survived various scares last term to secure a second WSL title, and they reestablished their lead two minutes later, when Hemp stretched out a leg to poke in Mary Fowler’s cross from the right to secure the win.

That London City could feel aggrieved at having not taken something from the game was a testament to their performance and how quickly progress is being made. The home team had 23 shots to Manchester City’s seven and 52 touches in the opposition box to Man City’s 13, but critically, the visiting team were clinical when it mattered. Converting two of their three efforts on target and showing the edge needed to battle at the top.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick to stay in charge of Manchester United for Roma game
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for Tuesday’s Champions League game against Roma at Old Trafford despite Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Chelsea.

The defeat means United have not won in nine games and have made their poorest start to a season since 1988, but Carrick’s position is expected to be reviewed again during the international break after the next round of Premier League matches, in which United host Aston Villa next Sunday.

The 45-year-old came close to losing his job last Monday when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada met at the training ground to discuss his future. The director of football and the chief executive decided Carrick should be given a chance to turn form and results around.

Carrick’s side are in 17th with seven points, above the relegation zone only on goal difference.

There remains a view within the hierarchy that Carrick can still transform fortunes, with United’s travelling support still backing him at the end of the defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

After the game the head coach indicated that he expected to still be in position for the Roma game. He said: “We’ve got to move forward and win matches, it’s as simple as that.”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United’s captain, looks dejected after the 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Eddie Howe is Wilcox’s preferred candidate should Carrick be sacked, with contact between the parties understood to have been made. The former Newcastle ­manager is open to taking up the position, ­subject to negotiations. He would cost about £3m in compensation to Newcastle.

Julian Nagelsmann, the ­former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by ­Christopher ­Vivell, United’s director of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow ­German. The pair previously worked together at RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
Sports.content:
After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top.

The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project.

In terms of personnel, the most notable change was in the dugout where 48-year-old Peter Cklamovski replaced Karl Robinson, who was sacked after a desperate performance in the playoff final loss to Notts County. Cklamovski’s previous experience came working under Ange Postecoglou before becoming a head coach in his own right in Asia, most recently taking charge of the Malaysia national team. Such was his unknown status, Salford’s chief football adviser Paul Scholes had to Google the Australian before he was appointed.

Off the pitch, Salford reverted to wearing orange, the traditional club colour that was changed by the Class of ’92, who wanted the shirts to reflect their links to Manchester United. The fans voted for it, democracy in action where previously the owners knew best. Beckham has turned Inter Miami into a global brand worth more than £1bn, making pink a key part of its identity. Lionel Messi shirt sales helped the hue travel, with kids across the UK spotted with the famous No 10 on the back. Beckham selected the shade of orange – and the badge was redesigned – but whether Langstaff et al can have the same effect as Messi remains to be seen. “Not many others play in orange, so if you’re going to see that kit around Manchester, you would know it’s not United or City,” says Danny Shepherd of The Future Is Orange podcast.

Attracting new fans is the aim but Salford face competition from much bigger clubs in the region. Even with Manchester City in a crisis and United’s form spiralling, convincing locals to head down to the AIG Stadium is difficult. Cklamovski’s attractive style is a deliberate ploy but the Ammies have the fourth-worst average attendance in League Two. It is optimistic to think they can create a Championship fanbase, even with subsidised away travel.

View image in fullscreen The Salford badge was redesigned and the shirts reverted to a traditional orange. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Cklamovski is making a name for himself with the aggressive attacking football he learned under his mentor. He started with three defeats but since then the Australian has found a pragmatic approach, mixing his playing out from the back ideals with an openness to be more direct when required, which brought a change in fortunes.

“I’d be disappointed if we didn’t go up because of the strength in depth,” says Shepherd. “Last season we had certain linchpin players that if they weren’t available, then we had either a utility player, a youngster or someone whose quality is so much lower that it’s like falling off a cliff. I’m not a rose-tinted spectacles fan, I can’t see how this team cannot get promoted – I think we should win the league at a canter.”

The confidence was not fully apparent in the first half as Salford were sloppy and struggled to create chances, while defensively vulnerable against a resolute Exeter. Goalkeeper Will Norris was booked for rushing out of his area and fouling Sonny Cox, who got his own back by scoring the opener for a side on a fine run themselves, unbeaten in the previous five.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Peter Cklamovski has instilled a brand of football at Salford that he learned while working under Ange Postecoglou. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Salford only came to life after the disappointing Luke Molyneux was forced off through injury, replaced by Daniel Udoh in the 55th minute. Energy levels increased and were rewarded by Luke Garbutt’s leveller at the back post after Langstaff’s fine work on the right.

Salford were on top after that and got their reward from the unfamiliar source of former Exeter centre-back Aimson, who sent a shot into the top corner from 25 yards to keep the run going and show this team have character to battle back in difficult circumstances. “We’ve got to stay really focused and diligent,” Cklamovski says. “We’ve got a nice bit of momentum, but don’t look too far forward. Eight wins in a row or 11 unbeaten however you want to look at it, just don’t look back.” He need not worry, there are plenty of people above him looking to the future.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca rues ‘silly’ errors after Manchester City defeat against Brighton
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said “silly goals” and individual errors are costing Manchester City after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in Saturday’s 1-0 victory here. Ayari’s strike was made possible after Nunes, City’s right-back, missed Diego Gómez’s cross from the right, so the ball could come back across goal via Maxim De Cuyper.

The 2-1 loss at Aston Villa came from Gianluigi Donnarumma allowing Nicolas Jackson’s long-range winner to squeeze under his body.

“Sometimes it happens,” said Maresca. “Unfortunately, it is happening for our players, but it is part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse, understand what we can do better and try to move on.

“We are the second team in terms of scoring in the Premier League, but we are conceding silly goals that we can avoid and hopefully we can avoid in the next game.

“It is a very similar feeling we had after the Aston Villa game – unfortunately we created enough to get some points but we didn’t score. At the moment it is like this. We did enough to deserve something. We need to move on and try to win games. For sure we are not happy.”

While Maresca said he had not seen the free-kick awarded against Elliot Anderson to decide if this was fair, Brighton’s victory takes them to 19 points, two behind City, who are the leaders before Arsenal’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

Fabian Hürzeler was delighted his players had changed the feeling of Wednesday’s Carabao Cup penalty shootout loss to City. “Every morning you can wake up and decide if you’re disappointed by something you cannot change or set the tone,” he said. “Stand up and have the belief that you’ll have a different feeling. It was brutal [the cup defeat]. We promised ourselves that we won’t have the same feeling.

“We want to be satisfied. We created energy, positivity, the next day. You need this. We saw Saturday as an opportunity to come back stronger. This was the approach and how the players stuck together and built the connection through the four days is really impressive.”

Hürzeler was asked what is possible for Brighton this season. “The only thing we’re focused on is that we are in a big process, a process of analysing the game. Then try to prepare for Getafe [on Thursday], a big challenge.”

Sports.title: Zion Suzuki horror own goal haunts Aston Villa to hand Fulham a point
Sports.content:
Fulham helped cement Jamie Carragher’s argument that Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. No, they know how to grind out a point on a bad day and can go to Barcelona on Tuesday with some confidence.

Villa’s goalkeeper Zion Suzuki dropped Alex Iwobi’s corner over his own goalline to deny Unai Emery’s team a fifth win in six games after Nicolas Jackson’s eighth goal of the season had promised to lift a resurgent Villa back into the top third of the Premier League. Not even John McGinn’s missed penalty had looked set to deny them as they took control in the first period.

But while Villa were made to look below par by a Fulham side making it seven points from the last nine, the home supporters sang long and loud to make their manager know how much he is appreciated.

The Holte End had not waited long to voice their verdict on the spat between the former England international and the Villa chair.

Carragher had admitted that his words were “clumsy and wrong” after telling Villa fans “to shut the fuck up” as they reacted angrily to his claims that Emery should want to manage Manchester United if Michael Carrick were to be sacked after their long winless run. It seemed like a storm in a teacup to many until Nassef Sawiris issued a statement promising to initiate legal action. “As custodians of this great club, we cannot stand still while the F word is directed at Villa fans,” Sawiris said.

Notwithstanding this disappointing draw, it is beyond question that Emery has done an admirable job at Villa. Even after losing another tranche of top talent, with Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers and Emi Martínez heading up the exits last summer after winning the Europa League, the former Arsenal and PSG manager has resurrected the club’s fortunes yet again. They start seasons slowly – winning only two of their last 12 league games in August and September – but once he has cast his spell and integrated the new signings, Villa tend to get going; they had won eight of their previous 10 league games in October and November.

View image in fullscreen Zion Suzuki fumbles the ball into the net to gift Fulham their goal. Photograph: Manjit Narotra/ProSports/Shutterstock

It must be galling to qualify for the Champions League twice in three years and yet still have your best talents lured away. So the idea that United could, in Carragher’s eyes, come and click their fingers and expect Emery to be unable to resist their faded grandeur evidently stuck in the throats of Villa fans and chair alike.

Fulham’s second-half showing, in particular, merited a draw that followed their recent league wins over Hull and Coventry and kept them two points above the relegation zone in Álvaro Arbeloa’s first autumn in charge. Emery would never countenance it but perhaps Villa’s ultimate glamour trip, to Barcelona, on Tuesday before next Sunday’s visit to Old Trafford, of all places, overshadowed this game.

McGinn spurned his first penalty for the club (excluding shootouts), awarded after Sander Berge was belatedly adjudged to have handled Leon Goretzka’s header, when he thundered his spot-kick against the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson opens the scoring for Aston Villa in the first half. Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA

But while Fulham had plenty of the ball, Villa appeared content to threaten on the counterattack. Indeed, they took the lead in the 39th minute after Jackson was sent running down the inside-left channel by a perfect through ball from Johan Manzambi. The £65m striker weaved into the penalty area past Timothy Castagne and David Affengruber before slotting in his fifth goal in five Premier League games.

Fulham were much more dominant in the second half. “They were more aggressive than us in the first half,” Arbeloa admitted. “I told my players I know we are a team that wants to control the game through the ball. But this is the Premier League. If you want to win a game, you need to fight for every ball.” When Castagne headed on Alex Iwobi’s corner, both Gonzalo García and Shea Charles got a touch on the ball before it spooned up on to the roof of the net. Villa were riding their luck.

Fulham’s dominance paid off, however, in the most unexpected fashion midway through the second half. Suzuki, who has been lauded for his early-season form, had just saved a header from Iwobi when, from the Nigerian’s ensuing corner, under no pressure, he inexplicably dropped the ball just over the line. “It’s part of football,” Emery said. “I make mistakes as coach. The players are making every match mistakes … when it’s the keeper, those mistakes are more in focus. I prefer to speak about the saves he did today.”

Sports.title: Naderi breaks Aberdeen’s resistance as Rangers reach Premier Sports Cup final
Sports.content:
Ryan Naderi’s dramatic late strike broke down Aberdeen’s stubborn resistance to earn Rangers a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

Aberdeen restricted Rangers to one shot on target in a low quality first half, but Derek McInnes’s side picked up the pace after the break. Aberdeen survived relentless pressure at times but in the 83rd minute Naderi redirected a strike from James Penrice into the net for his eighth goal of the season to seal a 1-0 win at Hampden Park.

The 23-year-old Naderi later tried to share the glory, saying: “It feels amazing. I’m happy, of course, happy to be the one who scores the goals, but happy for the team. I think we deserved it. We believed we could score right up until the very end and we did, and I think it’s a deserved win.”

It was another close-range strike from Naderi and he joked about this proficiency from distance. The Germany-born Czechia international said: “I’ve tried to shoot twice today from outside of the box and it didn’t go well.

“So I went back inside the box. Maybe I should just stick to the easy ones! As I said, I’m just happy how it is right now and I’m going to try to stick to it.”

Rangers – who will face the winners of Sunday’s semi-final between Hearts and Hibernian in the final – went into the game unbeaten in 10 and firm favourites.

With five Aberdeen defenders missing through suspension or injury – Lewis Mayo, Mats Knoester, Dan Happe, Kristers Tobers and Chris Cadden – there was a makeshift element about their lineup, with a first start of the season for Nicky Devlin.

McInnes, the Rangers manager who won the trophy with Aberdeen in 2014, raised eyebrows by dropping midfielder Dan Neil, with left-back Tuur Rommens starting and Penrice moving into midfield, and Badredine Bouanani starting in place of Djeidi Gassama.

View image in fullscreen Ryan Naderi diverts James Prentice’s shot past Marius Müller. Photograph: Kirk O’Rourke/Rangers FC/Shutterstock

There was more readjustment for Aberdeen when Emmanuel Gyamfi injured himself trying to tackle Kim Min-su and was replaced by Stuart Armstrong.

In the 23rd minute, the Rangers defence parted and Nesta Guinness-Walker drove through the gap, forcing goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to save. Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet glanced a header wide of the goal before Naderi hooked an effort over the crossbar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Scottish Premiership roundup: Saints dedicate draw to dismissed Steward Show Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to the goalkeeper Toby Steward, who was dismissed in the 14th minute (pictured) after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty area. Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point. The substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair, who came on at the expense of Taylor Steven, also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh. Valakari, the St Johnstone manager, said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’ But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor, who I needed to take out straight away. “We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility. Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a sweeper-keeper for those long balls. In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.” Alfred Johansson admitted he was left to sweat as Motherwell broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren. Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth. Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players. He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games. It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all." Press Association Photograph: Andy Buchanan/Shutterstock Editorial Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Just before the break Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Müller parried a low drive from Bouanani to safety, then Naderi headed a cross from stand-in captain Nico Raskin just over before Kim slashed a drive wide.

As the game became stretched, Pandur saved a deflected Kevin Nesbit drive then Müller blocked a shot from Kim before Rangers striker Kevin Kelsy somehow managed to head a pinpoint delivery from Bouanani past a post from six yards.

Müller’s foot blocked another effort from Bouanani and beat away a Raskin volley as the Aberdeen box came under siege. On a rare break, Nesbit’s shot was deflected wide and from the corner the Aberdeen striker hooked over the bar.

Aberdeen finally succumbed when Bouanani knocked the ball back to Penrice and he fired towards goal, with Naderi stepping in to beat Müller from close range.

Sports.title: Man United handed Bruno Fernandes price tag warning ahead of predicted exit
Sports.content:
Tony Cascarino does not believe that any Premier League team would pay £60million for Bruno Fernandes.

Manchester United are currently in disarray having not won in nine games and are 17th in the table.

4 It was yet another game to forget for Man United Credit: Getty

After their latest defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, former Blues striker Cascarino and Shebahn Aherne discussed potential fees for the current Man United squad.

Cascarino used a benchmark fee of £60m, and he doesn't believe that a single player in Michael Carrick's team would command that fee.

And that even included Fernandes, who has been the only bright spark for a few years.

However, he is in his 30s now and has been in particularly poor form this year.

Speaking on Weekend Sports Breakfast with Aherne, Cascarino said: "How many Manchester United players do you think you would get £60million for?

"Let's just use that as a price tag. How many from Old Trafford would you buy for that?

"Carlos Baleba has just come for £70m, so it is a bit unfair to put him in.

"Would Bruno Fernandes go for £60m? You might from Saudi Arabia, but you wouldn't from another Premier League team - there is no way that would happen.

"I really don't think a Premier League club would pay it. He's 32, so would you pay £60m and put him on a huge wage?

"I would think absolutely not.

4 Fernandes has even been dropped this year Credit: AFP

4 Michael Carrick has been kept on as manager at Man United despite results getting worse Credit: AFP

"Has he been a great player for Man United? Yes, he has. He's had periods where he has dragged the club out of trouble with his goals and his assists."

Fernandes' future

This is very possibly the 32-year-old's final season as a Man United player with his contract due to expire in the summer.

The Portuguese international also found himself out of the team after calling out Carrick's tactics.

Como beat Man United 4-1 in the Champions League and following the match, Fernandes questioned the lack of pressing.

In the immediate aftermath, the Man United manager didn't say too much about it, but in the next game against Bournemouth, he left his captain on the bench for the entire game.

Carrick was then told he'd be staying on and reconciled with Fernandes and started him at Stamford Bridge only for him to miss an absolute sitter at 0-0.

4 Fernandes' form has been way off this year Credit: Getty

And Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda predicts he will leave the club.

He joined talkSPORT Breakfast and said: "In my personal opinion, I think it's coming to an end.

"And I really think that's the best for both because I think first of all, Manchester United must organise their own dressing room.

"Even for Bruno Fernandes, I think the best for both is to, let's say, break this relationship, find a solution, because I think that kind of organisation that Man United needs to make a step back, to make two steps forward, starts with cleaning the dressing room.

"I think that a player like Fernandes nowadays, it's better to not be there, even for him, because I think that Fernandes is in a team that is more established, fighting for big things.

"Even for him, it could be much better, because yesterday, for example, it is what it is, but Bruno Fernandes, the position that he had in the Ballon d'Or [27th], for example, it doesn't reflect the player that he is, the numbers that he has.

"And if he plays for another team, I'm sure that Bruno Fernandes easily can be in the top ten players of the world."

Sports.title: Billy Sharp makes surprise retirement U-turn to play one final game in FA Cup for former club
Sports.content:
Billy Sharp makes surprise retirement U-turn to play one final game in FA Cup for former club

Billy Sharp will return to football less than a month after announcing his retirement.

The 40-year-old will come back for one game only, having quit football on October 11, to help out former club Rushden & Diamonds.

2 Sharp scored 299 goals across his career - now he can make it 300 Credit: Alamy

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds, the phoenix club following Rushden & Diamonds demise in 2011, announced the signing of Sharp on Sunday.

The Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side reached the first round proper of the FA Cup for the first time.

They won five qualifying rounds to reach the first round and will take on Burton.

In a statement, the club said: "After 21 years away, AFC Rushden & Diamonds are excited to announce that Billy Sharp becomes a Diamond once again.

"Billy scored the first of 299 goals for Rushden & Diamonds back in 2005.

"The man who put the ball in the Cobblers' net, has 299 career goals spanning over 22 years.

"Featuring for RDFC, Sheffield United Doncaster Rovers, Southampton, & Scunthorpe to name a few!

"Billy comes in to help the club with James Clifton being suspended and we can’t wait to see him pull on the shirt one final time as we go to Burton Albion in the FA Cup 1st Round Proper for the first time ever in AFC Rushden & Diamonds history."

Billy Sharp retirement

Sharp scored 299 senior goals in an extensive playing career that saw him feature from League Two through to the Premier League.

This included three spells at Sheffield United, as well as successful stints at Scunthorpe, Doncaster and Nottingham Forest.

2 Sharp also had a brief stint in the MLS with LA Galaxy in 2023 Credit: Getty

His first taste of Premier League football came with Southampton in the 2012/13 season, before returning six years later with the Blades.

Sharp is also the Championship's record goalscorer having hit 130 in the second tier.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Sharp was asked if it was a difficult decision to make, and replied: "No. I've been planning it, I had plenty of time to think about it.

"I'm just really satisfied that I got a choice to retire and it's not been taken away from me by injury or something else. It's a big wrench to make that decision.

"I know I could have played on and scored goals, but I thought the time was right. I've just had a new addition to the family and time away with the family, which I've not really been able to have.

"It's always been football. Football has given me a lot of highs, a lot of great memories, and it was there for me when I lost a child. I'll be forever grateful and in debt to that.

"I've had a good career, scored a lot of goals, and I've got so many memories to take away from it."

Billy Sharp's career in numbers Sheffield United - 377 games, 129 goals, 42 assists

Doncaster Rovers - 198 games, 71 goals, 20 assists

Scunthorpe United - 94 games, 56 goals, 5 assists

Nottingham Forest - 40 games, 11 goals, 5 assists

Leeds United - 35 games, 5 goals, 1 assist

Southampton - 18 games, 10 goals, 3 assists

Rushden & Diamonds - 16 games, 9 goals, 1 assist

Hull City - 13 games, 0 goals, 0 assists

LA Galaxy - 12 games, 6 goals, 1 assist

Reading - 10 games, 2 goals, 0 assists Total: 814 games, 299 goals, 78 assists

Sharp had also joined Baller League team N5, led by former Arsenal and Germany goalkeeper Jens Lehmann.

The striker has also completed his coaching badges and may have one eye on management in the future.

Sports.title: Declan Rice to become Arsenal’s joint best paid player – but still earns less than Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Declan Rice to become Arsenal’s joint best paid player – but still earns less than Mikel Arteta

Mikel Arteta has hinted that a new long-term contract for Declan Rice is imminent.

Rice joined Arsenal in 2023 for £105m, but is currently in the final two years of his deal.



2 Rice has already played 169 times for Arsenal Credit: Getty

Talks started with the England international at the start of the year and there was always confidence he would extend.

Asked if he is expecting talks to be finalised soon, Arteta said: "Yeah.

"My feeling is that he is very happy here. Every conversation that I have with him, he wants to continue here for the long term.



"It will be a matter of time when we resolve that."

How much will Rice be paid?

Reports suggest Rice will be paid in the region of £350,000-a-week, a significant increase from the £240,000-a-week he gets currently.

This would put him on a level with Bukayo Saka as the best paid player at Arsenal.



Manager Arteta earns a basic salary of £20m-per-year, which equates to around £384,000-a-week.

The Gunners boss himself signed a lucrative long-term contract until 2030 in October.



Speaking on Weekend Sports Breakfast, journalist Jamie Jackson said: “It's obviously a great sort of re-signing, renewing of contract for Arsenal. He is kind of the fulcrum for the side.

“I think he's a heck of a player. He could probably score more goals if he asked me my opinion of where he could improve.”

2 Arteta, Saka and Rice will be on a combined £1m-a-week at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Declan Rice this season

Rice has started all eight of Arsenal's Premier League games this season.



That will become nine on Sunday as the Gunners travel to Anfield to face Liverpool.

Arteta's side can go top-of-the-table if they get at least a point in the 4.30pm kick-off.

"I think he's (Rice) been very consistent again," Arteta said.

"What we are demanding him to do, every year, is very difficult to maintain. He's doing it, big credit to him.

"Big players for big matches and we know the kind of performance we need from Dec and the rest of the boys to get away from there with three points."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick given two-match deadline before losing Man United job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has two more matches at Manchester United before he loses his job - then the circus will continue with another manager.

That is the view of talkSPORT's Henry Winter, who thinks the international break will prove the optimal time to cut the cord.

3 Carrick is set to be given more time as United head coach despite their winless run of nine matches Credit: Getty

Carrick appeared destined for the sack at Old Trafford after the club fell to a 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth last weekend.

However, talkSPORT revealed that the Man United board being split over whether to hire Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann played a part in the decision to keep him on for the time being.

That decision came under further scrutiny when the Red Devils were then beaten 2-0 by Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

It was a result that meant that Man United have now gone nine matches without a win for the first time since 1988.

Despite that latest setback, Carrick is expected to be in the dugout on Tuesday night against Roma, talkSPORT understands.

Football journalist Winter believes the stay of execution won't extend much beyond next week, with Man United hosting high-flying Aston Villa in their final match before the November international break.

Carrick predicted to lose his job in the break

Asked what Carrick does next to bounce back from the Chelsea defeat, Winter told Shaun on talkSPORT's Sunday Edition: "You go into the Roma game. You prepare for that.

"The irony of that is that it was probably one of his best ever performances as a Manchester United player [in the 7-1].

"He scored twice, and he was fantastic...And then he limps on into the Aston Villa game and probably loses his job in the international break.

3 Carrick has at least two more matches in charge at United, with a tough test against Roma next up Credit: Getty

"We know what international breaks are like in the rhythm of managers; if they're going through a difficult time, it gives the club opportunity and time to get someone in.

"And also you have the risk of if an incumbent manager is staying on during the international break, and there are dark clouds over his head - those players who go off on international break.

"You know what we're like [the media]. I would imagine the Portuguese journalists before they got Denmark and Wales and the Argentinian journalists before the Uruguayans and Costa Rica.

"They will be talking respectively to Bruno Fernandes, and to Lisandro Martinez, and say, 'What do you think of this Carrick character?'

"And of course, the sort of headlines emanating from those international camps, and other ones, are just a bit too much.

"So you'd imagine that at some point the club will make a decision on Michael Carrick, and then the whole circus will just continue with another manager until you sort out the ownership."

3 Carrick recalled Fernandes against Chelsea after clear-the-air talks Credit: Getty

Man United need to clear the squad out

The Red Devils were competitive at Stamford Bridge until Martinez was sent off at the start of the second half.

It is the latest negative talking point from a senior pro in the squad, with captain Bruno Fernandes also publicly criticising Carrick's tactics, resulting in him being dropped for last Sunday's loss to Bournemouth.

Winter added to talkSPORT: "That squad needs just a huge clear-out.

"And it's not Michael Carrick's fault that he started the season when he needed a left back and a striker and he was given three midfielders - two of whom probably are not up to it!

"[Carlos] Baleba, I haven't got a problem with, although he got caught out. It's not Carrick's fault that Amad Diallo didn't put those chances away.

"It's not Michael Carrick's fault that Lisandro Martinez behaved the way he did.

"It's not Michael Carrick's fault that three experienced players allowed Morgan Rogers to fly straight through the middle of them.

"So look, you can get rid of the coach, but you're not getting rid of the overall problem."

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League star to join Sheffield Wednesday backroom team as new manager announced
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star to join Sheffield Wednesday backroom team as new manager announced

Sheffield Wednesday have confirmed the appointment of Dave Challinor as their new manager.

It follows the sacking of Henrik Pedersen by the League One club.

2 Challinor is the new Sheffield Wednesday manager Credit: Getty



Challinor will be at Hillsborough on Sunday for their league game with Blackpool.

In a statement, the club said: "Sheffield Wednesday Football Club can confirm that an agreement was reached last night for Dave Challinor to become the club's new First-Team Manager.

"The 51-year-old will be in attendance at today's fixture against Blackpool at Hillsborough.

"The club looks forward to formally introducing Dave to supporters on Monday, when further details of the appointment will be announced."



Challinor's backroom team

Former Crystal Palace, QPR and Stoke defender Clint Hill is expected to join Challinor at Wednesday.

The Sheffield Star reports Hill was one of the first people the club spoke to as talks accelerated.



The 48-year-old was part of Challinor's backroom team at Stockport from 2021 until this summer.

Challinor's record

The 51-year-old left Stockport at the end of last season after losing in the League One play-off final to Bolton.



He had got them promoted from the National League and League Two previously.

Challinor has also had successful spells at AFC Fylde and Hartlepool.

2 Hill (left) is set to join Challinor's staff Credit: Getty

Sheffield Wednesday this season

The Owls currently sit ninth in League One following their relegation from the Championship.

The club ended last season bottom of the second tier on zero points after being deducted 18 points over the course of the campaign.



Wednesday can climb up to near the play-off places with a win over Blackpool on Sunday.

Should they win their two games in hand, the club will be pushing for automatic promotion.

Following their clash with Blackpool, they travel to Oldham in the first round of the FA Cup next Sunday.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho addresses Trent Alexander-Arnold exit rumours amid Premier League transfer links
Sports.content:
Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho has admitted that Trent Alexander-Arnold's lack of playing time makes him 'sad'.

The Special One made a frank statement on the England star's future in Spain amid reports of a move back to the Premier League.



3 The ex-Liverpool defender has been left as an unused substitute on six occasions under Mourinho this season so far Credit: Getty

Trent has endured a torrid time at Los Blancos since he left boyhood club, Liverpool, for a nominal fee at the end of his contract in 2025.

A mixture of injury issues and the form of Dani Carvajal meant the 28-year-old made just 14 LaLiga starts in his first campaign in Spain.

Mourinho's arrival this summer further dampened his prospects, with the Portuguese immediately signing Denzel Dumfries at right-back.



The pair have now both found themselves languishing on the Madrid bench in recent weeks, with Federico Valverde preferred in defence.

Trent has started just three LaLiga games under Mourinho this term, and played just a minute in the El Clasico triumph over Barcelona.



His lack of game time has sparked rumours that Madrid's No.12 could look to leave the club, with a return to England the most natural fit.

However, Mourinho has poured cold water on the prospect of the 36-cap Three Lions star requesting a move away from Spain's capital.



Mourinho dismisses Trent transfer exit

"To begin with, it hurts me," Mourinho explained in his most recent pre-match press conference when asked about Trent's situation.

"I don't like giving bad feelings to players; I prefer them to feel good. When you build a squad with two players per position and end up playing a third, it's not something I appreciate.

"But there are things more important than these feelings, things that matter more for the team at a given moment.

3 Alexander-Arnold has been tipped to stay and fight for his position at Real Madrid despite struggling for regular starts Credit: Getty



"I felt we needed to change our midfield and play Fede in that position," Mourinho continued on his preferred right-back.

"It was a decision made for the team, not based on individual players."

"Trent and Dumfries accepted my explanations well," Mourinho continued.

"They understood that this choice was made in the interest of the collective and was not aimed at anyone.



"Against Barcelona, circumstances meant that Dumfries played and Trent also had a few minutes."

“And I don’t think either of them is going to ask to leave.

3 The dream move to Real Madrid hasn't quite worked out for Alexander-Arnold Credit: Getty

“The demands of the season, with so many games and these ‘gifts,’ accumulated yellow cards, fatigue, the occasional injury… ultimately, everyone will play.

“I don’t think we’ll have that kind of situation.”

Mourinho also offered Trent a potential lifeline by revealing that Valverde will be rested for Madrid's clash with Racing Santander.



The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Manchester United boss insisted that one of Trent or Dumfries will step up on Sunday instead.

Sports.title: Harry Kane makes rare admission on performance in first game since winning Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Harry Kane makes rare admission on performance in first game since winning Ballon d’Or

Harry Kane offered a candid assessment of his own performance in Bayern Munich's eventful 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund.

The newly-crowned Ballon d'Or winner missed a penalty as his side twice threw away a lead in a dramatic Der Klassiker stalemate.

3 Kane presented the Ballon d'Or to the Bayern fans ahead of kick-off Credit: Getty

It was Kane's first appearance since lifting the Golden Ball on Monday, having been an unused sub in a 6-1 win over Magdeburg in midweek.

However, the England captain became the first player in 14 years to miss a penalty in the Der Klassiker between Bayern and Dortmund.

Harry Kane reacts to 'strange night' for Bundesliga leaders

The former Tottenham striker could not hide his frustration at full-time, having endured a rare off day at the Allianz Arena.

"Today probably wasn't my best performance or the team's best performance, but that's just life," Kane told Bulinews in the post-match mixed zone.

"It's part of being a striker and a footballer.

"I could have been out there playing for another hour today, and the ball wouldn't hit the back of the net.

"You have to take that on the chin sometimes."

Kane also reflected on the mood inside the Bayern dressing room, with both Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry suffering injuries.

The Bavarians are already without boss Vincent Kompany, who was only recently discharged from hospital after his terrifying collapse at the club's training ground.

3 Kane became the first player since Robben in 2012 to miss a penalty during Der Klassiker between Bayern and Dortmund Credit: Getty

Kane continued: "It was a strange night all round. We have to see how the injuries are. A couple didn't look so good.

He added: "We're at that stage of the season where we have that many games coming up.

"We have to think about using the squad a lot [rotation], and there's no doubt we will use the squad.

"For Atlético [Madrid], I'll be ready to go. It's an important game for us.

"We're going to a really tough place away from home, so we're going to need everyone to step up."

Kane, who has already scored 10 goals in 13 appearances for Bayern across all competitions this season, did at least register an assist for Dayot Upamecano's goal that restored his side's advantage after Serhou Guirassy cancelled out Konrad Laimer's strike.

3 Kane had a helping hand in one of Bayern's goals, but they could not hold onto their lead and had to settle for a draw in the derby Credit: Getty

The 33-year-old was powerless to prevent Dortmund from hitting back a second time, though, with Fabio Silva rescuing a draw late on.

It means that the two teams are level on 18 points with five wins and three draws, but Bayern lead the Bundesliga on goal difference.

Sports.title: 'My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate': Bradley Lowery's mum issues heartbreaking statement to condemn 'cruel' Coventry fan who used her late son's photo to taunt Sunderland fans
Sports.content:
Bradley Lowery's mum has released a heartbreaking statement after a Coventry fan appeared to use his photograph to taunt Sunderland supporters. The deplorable behaviour came during the Premier League clash between the two sides on Saturday, which the Sky Blues won 3-1. A video on social media showed a supporter holding up a picture of Bradley - who tragically died from a rare form of childhood cancer at the age of six in 2017 - smiling in the direction of Sunderland fans, with the individual pointing at it and seen smirking at the same time. And, in a statement on Sunday morning after the behaviour of the Coventry fan went viral, Bradley's mum Gemma shared a heartbreaking message. 'My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate,' she wrote. 'Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile. 'I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt. A Coventry fan appeared to use a photograph of Bradley Lowery to taunt Sunderland fans A fan held up a photo of Bradley, the Sunderland fan who tragically passed away aged six from a rare form of childhood cancer, and was seen smirking and pointing 'We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. 'I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.' Gemma continued: 'What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope. 'Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away. 'So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours.' In response to the video Coventry released a statement, which read: 'Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland. 'The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.' Bradley was previously used by a fan as a taunt back in 2023 when Sheffield Wednesday supporter Dale Houghton was seen holding up a picture of him at a match against Sunderland and laughing. Houghton was subsequently handed a 12-week suspended prison sentence and ordered to do 200 hours unpaid work. Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, and formed a touching relationship with then Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe Bradley pictured with his mum Gemma at his sixth birthday party back in May 2017 Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, before he tragically passed away aged just six in 2017. The Bradley Lowery Foundation was set up in his honour, with the charity aiming to help families who are fundraising for treatment or equipment that is not readily available or covered by the NHS, while it also supports research into various childhood cancers, including neuroblastoma. Bradley, who was diagnosed with neuroblastoma when he was just 18 months old, also built up a touching relationship with Jermain Defoe, who later called him his 'best mate'. Defoe played for Sunderland at the time, and speaking in 2023, he said: 'He will always be in my heart, for the rest of my life. There's not a day that goes past where I don't wake up and think about little Bradley, because his love is genuine.'
