Sports.title: Hirakawa surprised by call-up to replace Ocon but disappointed by qualifying result | Formula 1
Sports.content:
New Haas driver Ryo Hirakawa admitted he was astonished Haas called him up to replace Esteban Ocon this weekend.

The World Endurance Champion drove Ocon’s car in first practice, then handed it back to him for the second session. Haas then took the unexpected decision, which they have not offered any explanation for, to drop Ocon for the rest of the event and hand his seat to Hirakawa.

“Obviously it was a very big surprise this morning, but I’m always here to be a reserve driver,” said Hirakawa. “This is a role I was always ready for, but always dreaming about it.

“Then today, the dream came true: Qualifying today and race tomorrow. So these five hours passed so fast, I had so much to prepare and the team helped a lot for myself so really thanks to the team.”

Hirakawa set the 19th fastest time in final practice, half a second slower than team mate Oliver Bearman. That gap grew to 0.875 seconds in Q1, where Bearman was the only driver to progress, but Hirakawa believes he could have delivered a better lap time.

“Today the main focus was to go through Q1, which was a shame for me. I had traffic in the last push lap, so it was [big] shame.

“But everything went well. I just need to focus for tomorrow, for the race. I’m very excited for that.”

Sports.title: Sheeraz Expects Canelo Payday After Limping Past Zachenhuber
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz is openly campaigning for an unearned lottery ticket against Canelo Alvarez, and boxing fans are expected to pretend this makes sense.

Fans online already assume Turki Alalshikh will force this matchup. That speaks volumes about the current matchmaking environment. People expect what they think the money wants instead of the fights worth watching. Canelo has genuine options available. A rematch with Terence Crawford makes sense, while Jaron Ennis, Dmitry Bivol, Lester Martinez, or Osleys Iglesias would each offer far more entertainment.

Sheeraz, in contrast, is the ideal safe business fight. He gives the Riyadh Season brass an easy UK marketing angle, brings a recognizable name to British television, and holds zero real threat of upsetting the apple cart. As Simon Zachenhuber showed, Sheeraz is upright, gets uncomfortable when pressed, lacks defensive subtlety, and struggles to impose his height when someone refuses to fold early.

Against Canelo, Sheeraz would stand right in range, get timed coming in, and walk straight into counters without the ringcraft to survive it. Picking him is about protecting the brand and cashing a check, not testing greatness.

“Why not, bro? Why not test myself against the best,” said Sheeraz to DAZN Boxing when asked yesterday why he wants to fight Canelo. “I’m in this game to be the best, and put myself in there with someone with the likes of Canelo. It’s stuff you can dream of. Every day, I wake up, training harder and harder. It’s starting to become more of a reality. So, now it’s like, let me get in there and let me do my thing.”

Sheeraz did himself no favors during his recent majority decision win against Simon Zachenhuber. The German walked through his shots, pressed him constantly, and exposed his discomfort under fire. Nothing in that performance signaled that Sheeraz belongs in the ring with the face of boxing.

His brief title run did not validate him either. Picking up a vacant WBO belt by blowing out Alem Begic in two rounds proved very little. Begic was 39 with a paper record built on obscure opposition. Sheeraz then vacated rather than face Janibek Alimkhanuly, citing low money and an opponent returning from a failed test. He had every right to walk away, but walking away did not prove he is elite.

The refusal to fight Iglesias makes Sheeraz even harder to sell. Canelo openly suggested Hamzah face the dangerous Cuban to earn the shot. Sheeraz rejected the idea, pointing out that Edgar Berlanga and Jaime Munguia never had to pass such an audition. Canelo might have double standards, but whining about Berlanga does not elevate Hamzah’s resume.

Testing yourself against the best is what you do after you run through actual contenders, not after edging Simon Zachenhuber on a majority decision or blasting out Alem Begic.

If Sheeraz genuinely wanted to “test himself against the best” to prepare for Canelo, Osleys Iglesias was standing right there. Canelo offered him the exact blueprint: beat the Cuban southpaw, prove you belong at the elite tier, and bring real credibility to the table.

Saying “It’s stuff you can dream of” gives the game away. It is a dream because it represents the ultimate lottery ticket: a massive purse, global visibility, and zero downside if he loses to an all-time great. Every fringe contender wakes up training hard with that exact dream.

Wanting the biggest purse in the sport is understandable from a business perspective. Pretending that ambition alone makes you a worthy challenger is the part fans are tired of seeing. If everyone who “wakes up dreaming of Canelo” got the call, the sport would be nothing but exhibition paydays. Until Sheeraz takes on a legitimate threat who can punch back, talking about testing himself just sounds like someone angling for a retirement check.

My sources tell me chances are uncomfortably high, easily hovering around 65% to 75% that Canelo fights Hamzah next. Everything coming out of Riyadh points to Hamzah Sheeraz being the preferred target for that spot: Sheeraz sat ringside in Riyadh, gave pre-fight interviews to DAZN building up the matchup, and openly positioned himself as next in line.

That is standard operating procedure when organizers are preparing the public for an announcement. From the promotional side, Sheeraz checks the exact commercial boxes Turki Alalshikh looks for. He provides a British draw to anchor UK pay-per-view buys, brings a Middle Eastern connection based out of Dubai, and comes without the brutal negotiating headaches that accompany figures like Dmitry Bivol or Terence Crawford.

For Canelo, the risk calculus makes Sheeraz almost irresistible. After working through twelve rounds with Christian Mbilli, taking on an upright target who does not use angles or elite lateral footwork is a safe day at the office. Canelo avoids the nightmare styles of Osleys Iglesias or Jaron Ennis while pocketing another massive purse.

The only real hurdles that could derail it are: Crawford agreeing to unretire for the massive bag that a rematch would command. If Crawford says yes, every other fight gets pushed aside immediately. A sudden pivot to a mandatory unification, such as Osleys Iglesias holding the IBF belt or the winner of Janibek Alimkhanuly against Jacob Bank for the vacant WBO strap, if organizers decide they want all the belts consolidated again. Lester Martinez, who holds the WBC interim belt and was also sitting ringside, is being enforced as a mandatory obligation.

As such, unless Crawford signs on the dotted line or public ridicule forces a change in direction, all arrows point toward Sheeraz getting the nod. It is safe matchmaking dressed up as an international event.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Talks Mayweather While His Team Pursues Teofimo
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia says Floyd Mayweather needs to 

“We’ve seen Ryan Garcia say on Twitter that he wants to fight on February 6th, whether it’s against Floyd Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez. I was told that Mayweather wasn’t even in discussion for the next fight,” said Mike Coppinger to DAZN Boxing. “Of course, Mayweather is almost 50 years old now. It’s kind of a pipe dream. It would be a massive event, especially if it was later in the year. First, they’re working on finalizing a fight between Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez, a welterweight title unification. I think it’s one of the biggest fights in all of boxing. Teofimo just regained a title fight in Rolly Romero. I want to see it.”

Teofimo brings plenty of credibility without dragging Mayweather into the promotion. He presents an active, dangerous test with quick hands, explosive pop, elite counter striking. Garcia always carries dynamite in his left hook, though overcommitting against someone as sharp as Lopez creates immediate trouble.

That title bout stands on its own merit. Taking down Lopez proves infinitely more in today’s landscape than defeating an exhibition headliner pushing fifty, regardless of casual fan buzz. As Claudia Trejo noted, Garcia commands attention whenever he speaks. That massive platform works wonders, yet chasing a ghost can drown out the legitimate challenge right in front of him.

Setting a February date proves Garcia wants to compete this winter. It definitely does not prove Mayweather is scrambling to meet a deadline. With Lopez occupying the real negotiating table, Garcia’s final warning sounds like pure noise.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Calls For Terence Crawford Rematch After Win
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez made his priority clear right after taking down Christian Mbilli in Riyadh to grab back the WBC super middleweight strap: he wants another shot at Terence Crawford.

In his post-fight interview, Canelo didn’t hide his intentions when asked about coaxing Crawford out of retirement.

“Hopefully, yes. Hopefully, yes. We would honestly love to have that rematch, like I’ve told you. If not, we’ll keep moving forward with our career, but hopefully that fight can happen,” Canelo said.

The desire is there. The evidence of meaningful improvement is harder to find. Beating Mbilli restores Canelo’s position as a champion, but defeating a pressure fighter does not demonstrate that he would fare better against Crawford’s movement, timing, and ability to control distance.

Whether the Mexican star cares about the potential of losing again is unclear. Assuming Turki is on board with financing a second fight, the money Canelo would get would make it worthwhile.

The appetite from fans for a sequel is lukewarm at best, and for good reason. The first bout settled whatever competitive debate existed. Crawford put on a clinic in ring generalship, using distance, a sharp jab, lateral movement, and timely ties inside to neutralize Canelo. While purists could appreciate Crawford’s discipline, it was a pedestrian viewing experience for the casual paying crowd.

Fans remember twelve rounds of Canelo plodding forward, swinging at air, unable to cut off the ring, while Crawford played keep-away and banked rounds on the outside. Rematches of fights like that rarely produce fireworks; they usually produce a carbon copy.

Boxing fans would far rather see matchups that guarantee genuine action and modern divisional relevance: A unification clash with Osleys Iglesias gives hardcore fans an intriguing, high-risk clash against a dangerous, prime southpaw puncher holding the missing IBF strap.

Even a bout against Dmitry Bivol at light heavyweight would hold more competitive curiosity than watching Crawford stick and move his way to another lopsided decision.

The only real driver behind a Crawford rematch is pure business. Turki Alalshikh has the deep pockets to bankroll a massive spectacle, and both fighters stand to collect generational checks. The promotional build would lean on celebrity hype and pageantry, but inside the ring, the paying audience knows exactly what it would look like: twelve more rounds of perimeter defense and frustration.

Sports.title: Alvarez victorious over Mbilli, captures WBC super middleweight title
Sports.content:
Canelo Álvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title with a twelve-round unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli (29-1-1, 24 KOs) on Saturday at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Canelo’s cleaner counters and defensive work earned him scores of 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in the DAZN PPV main event.

Returning from a thirteen-month absence following his loss to Terence Crawford, Álvarez landed in bursts while Mbilli pressed forward without consistently connecting cleanly.

Mbilli had success when he sustained his attacks, but too often backed away after throwing, allowing Álvarez time to choose his counters. Canelo’s jab, hooks and uppercuts supplied the more accurate work, although Mbilli’s activity kept several rounds competitive.

In the eighth, referee Hector Afu deducted a point from Mbilli following an illegal punch. Álvarez had repeatedly drawn the referee’s attention to Mbilli’s fouls before the penalty.

Mbilli continued pressing late but could not produce the breakthrough he needed. Álvarez finished effectively in the final two rounds, securing the decision without either fighter scoring a knockdown.

WBA super middleweight champion Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) had a much harder evening than the scorecards suggested against Russian southpaw Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs). Munguía retained his title by unanimous decision, winning 116-112 and 117-111 twice after twelve competitive rounds.

Their sixth round produced furious action, with both fighters hurt and Munguía in serious danger before recovering. The Mexican’s combinations and greater output helped him through the later rounds, but Zon remained dangerous until the finish.

Munguía’s defensive lapses made this an uncomfortable first defense against an opponent making his first twelve-round appearance.

Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO featherweight title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón. The ringside doctor stopped the scheduled twelve-round contest at 1:22 because of a severe cut over Blandón’s eye.

Espinoza controlled the action with his jab and pressure. The medical intervention brought an abrupt ending before the challenger’s corner could attempt further treatment between rounds.

Carl Jammes Martin (29-0, 21 KOs) overcame a seventh-round knockdown to take the WBC Silver featherweight title from David Picasso (33-2-1, 18 KOs) by split decision over ten rounds.

Martin bloodied Picasso’s nose with a left hand in the third. Picasso answered in the seventh with a left hook that dropped the Filipino southpaw, who rose quickly and continued.

Martin’s strong final round helped him secure scores of 95-94 and 96-93, while the third judge favored Picasso 95-94.

Super featherweight Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) stopped Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) at 2:27 of the second round. The Japanese southpaw scored two knockdowns in the second before a follow-up attack prompted the referee to stop the scheduled ten-round bout.

Bek Nurmaganbet (17-0, 15 KOs) knocked out Marcos Vázquez Rodríguez (21-4-1, 10 KOs) at 2:57 of the opening round in their scheduled ten-round contest. Nurmaganbet scored an initial knockdown with approximately a minute remaining, then finished the Mexican southpaw with a combination that sent him onto his back.

Brayan León (13-0, 9 KOs) earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Hector Aguirre (7-1, 3 KOs) in a lively super middleweight contest. León landed the heavier punches early, but Aguirre rallied and kept the fight competitive.

Both men landed well in the closing rounds before León received scores of 77-75 and 78-74 twice.

Emiliano Rojo (22-0, 9 KOs) stopped Flavius Biea (24-4, 12 KOs) in the fourth round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Rojo’s pressure and body punching wore down the Romanian veteran, bringing the stoppage midway through the fourth.

Sultan Almohammed (6-0, 4 KOs) defeated Erick Jahir Urvina Villegas (5-3-3, 1 KO) by unanimous decision over six rounds. The eighteen-year-old scored a final-round knockdown with a left hand to the chin and won by scores of 60-54 and 59-55 twice.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Defeats Christian Mbilli by Unanimous Decision to Reclaim WBC Title
Sports.content:
Canelo Álvarez (64-3-2) reclaimed the WBC super middleweight title by making Christian Mbilli miss and punishing his approaches, winning a unanimous decision after twelve rounds on Saturday. Returning from thirteen months out following his defeat to Terence Crawford, Canelo showed that pressure alone was not enough to overwhelm him.

The judges scored it 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110, with Boxing News 24 scoring it 116-111. Mbilli (29-1-1) supplied the greater activity in stretches, but Canelo’s cleaner counters, jab and defensive work gave him the stronger scoring punches across enough rounds to secure the victory.

Canelo established that difference early. Mbilli came forward with energy and tried to force a fast pace, only to find that much of his offense struck the guard or missed. Canelo answered selectively, catching the champion as he entered rather than trying to match every burst with an equally long combination.

The opening three rounds favored Canelo’s accuracy on our card. His jab helped him judge the distance, while his counters discouraged Mbilli from attacking without caution. The champion was working hard, but the effort did not consistently produce clean connections.

Mbilli improved in the fourth, landing more frequently and forcing Canelo into a largely defensive role. That was the approach he needed to sustain: make Canelo respond to several attacks rather than give him time to select a single counter. When Mbilli kept the work coming, the rounds became considerably harder to separate.

The sixth provided another productive spell for the champion. Canelo spent time backing up and near the ropes, answering with occasional body shots and counters while Mbilli supplied the steadier offense. Those passages kept the fight competitive and showed why Canelo could not afford to rely entirely on isolated punches.

Canelo responded in the seventh with one of his better rounds. A stiff jab interrupted Mbilli’s output, and a sharp right uppercut caught him coming forward. Canelo also mixed in body work, giving the champion more to consider before launching his next attack.

The eighth brought a costly point deduction against Mbilli from referee Hector Afu. Canelo’s cleaner work earned him the round on our card, making it 10-8 after the penalty. That gave the challenger additional breathing room without either fighter having scored a knockdown.

Mbilli continued competing rather than allowing the deduction to end his effort. His activity narrowly earned him the ninth and tenth on our card, as Canelo left enough gaps between attacks for the champion to collect points. Canelo remained accurate, but accuracy still needed sufficient output to win those rounds.

The closing two rounds settled matters. Canelo beat Mbilli to openings in the eleventh and finished behind his jab and counters in the twelfth. Mbilli could not generate the sustained late attack needed to threaten a reversal, and Canelo reached the final bell without a serious scare.

This was a successful return built on skills that survived the layoff: timing, punch selection and the ability to defend while remaining close enough to answer. Mbilli made him work and earned rounds through persistence, but never consistently solved the difference between getting Canelo to the ropes and landing effectively once he had him there.

Canelo did not deliver a stoppage, extending his run of distance fights, but he earned the belt with the more precise boxing. Mbilli brought the pressure expected of him; Canelo repeatedly supplied the better answer.

Sports.title: Canelo vs Mbilli Live Results: Round-by-Round Updates and DAZN Coverage
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) retained his WBA super middleweight title with a unanimous decision over Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs), but looked alarmingly poor in a fight closer than the scores suggested. The judges returned cards of 117-111, 116-112 and 117-111, margins that flattered the champion after a difficult twelve rounds.

Zon repeatedly found openings for his southpaw power shots, exposing Munguía’s loose defense and hurting him badly during a furious sixth round. Munguía survived that crisis and answered with volume and combinations, but never produced the commanding performance expected against such an inexperienced challenger.

The referee also appeared to miss two potential knockdowns against Munguía, allowing him to escape counts that could have materially affected the scoring. A clear rabbit punch from Munguía went without a point deduction, another officiating failure that favored the champion. Munguía left with the belt, but his defensive mistakes and reliance on outworking Zon made this an unsettling defense rather than a reassuring victory.

Featherweight champion Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón (21-7, 14 KOs) after a severe cut over the challenger’s eye forced a medical stoppage.

Espinoza controlled the early action with his jab and reach, keeping Blandón under pressure. The Nicaraguan struggled to get past the champion’s long punches and establish an attack of his own. The cut worsened enough for the ringside doctor to intervene, ending the scheduled twelve-round contest.

Blandón had accepted the fight on roughly a week’s notice after Lorenzo Parra was ruled out, and the gap in preparation accompanied a substantial difference in class. Espinoza was comfortably in charge, although the medical ending denied him the chance to produce a more decisive finish with his punches. It was a straightforward retention for the champion, but a brief and unsatisfying title fight against a replacement challenger.

Super featherweight Reito Tsutsumi (6-0, 5 KOs) overwhelmed Raymundo Rojas García (16-3, 11 KOs) for a second-round TKO in their scheduled ten-round bout. The Japanese southpaw took charge early, using his speed to land clean combinations before Rojas could establish himself.

Rojas struggled to cope with the quicker, more polished prospect and could not slow his attack. Tsutsumi kept pressing, turning his technical advantage into damaging offense rather than allowing the Mexican time to recover.

The second-round stoppage completed a one-sided performance and gave Tsutsumi his fifth consecutive knockout victory. Rojas brought regional experience and respectable punching power, but neither was enough to bridge the difference in speed and technique. Tsutsumi looked ready for a sterner test after another opponent failed to take him beyond the early rounds.

Carl Jammes Martin (29-0) upset David Picasso (33-2-1, 18 KOs) by split decision over ten rounds to claim the WBC Silver featherweight title. The Filipino southpaw started quickly, using his speed and cleaner power shots to prevent the taller favorite from settling.

Picasso had substantial height and reach advantages but too often allowed Martin to dictate the pace rather than keeping him outside. Martin’s busier work and heavier-looking punches gave him the stronger argument in rounds where neither fighter sustained control.

Picasso had his successes in a competitive fight, but his quieter stretches left openings for Martin to seize the initiative. Two judges favored the unbeaten challenger, rewarding a performance built on activity and effective aggression against a more established opponent. Moving up in weight, Martin earned a significant victory while Picasso paid for failing to make his physical advantages count.

Super featherweight Sultan Almohammed (6-0) scored a sixth-round knockdown on his way to a unanimous decision over Erick Jahir Urvina Villegas after six rounds. The 18-year-old Saudi prospect dictated the action with persistent pressure, making the Mexican fight at his pace.

Almohammed maintained his intensity throughout, but Urvina Villegas proved tougher to finish than some of the teenager’s earlier opponents. The Mexican kept battling despite being outworked, forcing the heavy favorite to go the distance.

Almohammed closed strongly, putting Urvina Villegas down in the final round to underline his superiority. The knockdown capped a clear victory, even if the prospect could not produce another early stoppage. Six rounds against an opponent who kept competing gave Almohammed useful work beyond the quick finishes that had marked his early career.

Super middleweight Bek Nurmaganbet (17-0, 15 KOs) demolished Marcos Vázquez Rodríguez (21-4-1, 10 KOs) with a first-round knockout, ending their scheduled ten-round fight at 2:57. The unbeaten Kazakh attacked early with heavy, accurate punches, giving the Mexican veteran little opportunity to settle.

Nurmaganbet scored two knockdowns as his southpaw power proved too much for the 37-year-old. The violent finish immediately drew Knockout of the Year talk from DAZN.

Vázquez Rodríguez’s experience offered little protection once Nurmaganbet began landing, and he was overwhelmed before the opening round was over. This was a destructive performance, although beating an older opponent coming off a defeat leaves tougher tests ahead. Nurmaganbet supplied the kind of emphatic finish expected from a heavy favorite and delivered one of the early undercard’s biggest moments.

Emiliano Rojo stopped Flavius Biea at 1:37 of the fourth round, securing Team Mexico’s first victory of the night in their super middleweight bout. The 20-year-old controlled the middleweight bout with steady pressure, walking down his Romanian opponent and making him work at Rojo’s pace. Biea (24-4, 12 KOs) struggled to halt the younger fighter’s advance as Rojo’s activity gradually wore him down.

Rojo (22-0, 9 KOs) looked comfortable taking the initiative against the more experienced veteran, keeping the pressure on until the referee intervened. It was an effective performance, although Biea’s recent stoppage defeats limit how much can be read into the result. The 20-year-old Rojo did what a heavy favorite needed to do, finishing an opponent whose career was already heading downhill.

Super middleweight prospect Brayan León (13-0, 9 KOs) defeated Hector Aguirre by an eight-round unanimous decision, but the unbeaten Cuban had to work for it. Aguirre pressed León and forced him into a tough, competitive fight that exposed some flaws in the favored prospect.

León started rounds well, only to let his work rate drop and allow Aguirre to back him up. Those lapses gave the Mexican opportunities to keep the action close rather than letting León take control.

Aguirre lacked the punching power to make those stretches more costly, but he pushed León through the full eight rounds before suffering his first professional defeat.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Survives Sixth Round Scare to Outpoint Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía (47-2, 35 KOs) retained his WBA super middleweight title against Nikita Zon (12-1-1, 10 KOs), but his dreadful defense and a dangerous sixth round made the unanimous decision far less comfortable than the scorecards suggested. The champion won by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 117-111 after twelve rounds that exposed how easily he can still be hurt.

Zon arrived with limited experience and no previous twelve-round fights, yet repeatedly found Munguía with effective southpaw power shots. The Mexican’s volume and combinations helped him collect rounds, but they did not conceal the damage coming back. This was supposed to be a favorable title defense; instead, Munguía spent portions of it fighting to keep the challenger from taking over.

The sixth round brought the clearest danger. Zon hurt Munguía badly and pressed an attack that threatened to turn a difficult evening into another stoppage defeat. Munguía deserves credit for surviving and responding, but the crisis came against an opponent taking an enormous jump in competition.

His recovery mattered. Munguía resumed throwing combinations and used his activity to rebuild his case over the later rounds. Zon could land the more troubling punches without consistently matching the champion’s output, giving Munguía a route to winning rounds even when his defensive mistakes were the most memorable feature.

That distinction helps explain the decision without making the wide margins persuasive. Munguía’s busy spells counted, but Zon’s successes were too significant for this to resemble a routine defense. The challenger was dangerous enough to punish openings that Munguía should have been closing well before the championship rounds.

The officiating also deserved scrutiny. Two sequences in which Munguía appeared to go down were not ruled knockdowns, allowing him to avoid counts and the potential scoring consequences. Those were important moments in a contest where the official margins already seemed generous to the champion.

Munguía also escaped a point deduction for a clear rabbit punch. That foul warranted stronger action, particularly in a physical fight where the challenger was already having to overcome a substantial experience disadvantage. Taken together, the missed potential knockdowns and unpunished foul made the referee’s performance part of the story.

Zon did not need to win every round to expose the shortcomings in Munguía’s work. He found opportunities to land hard while the champion was attacking, showing the cost of throwing combinations without adequately protecting the return. Munguía could produce more punches and still emerge from a sequence looking like the more vulnerable fighter.

The concern carries added weight because Munguía has already suffered a knockout loss to Bruno Surace. Surviving Zon’s best attack prevented a repeat result, but it did not demonstrate that the underlying defensive weaknesses have been corrected. An inexperienced challenger was still able to bring him close to disaster.

For Zon, the defeat supplied evidence that his power could trouble a world champion over a distance he had never previously attempted. He fell short on the cards, but made a much stronger case for himself than the pre-fight expectations suggested.

Munguía kept his belt through persistence, offensive volume and the ability to recover when badly hurt. Those qualities earned him something on a poor night, but they cannot keep substituting for reliable defense. Against a more accomplished finisher, the openings Zon found could carry a much heavier price.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza Stops Ricardo Blandon on Cuts in Riyadh Under Three Rounds
Sports.content:
Rafael Espinoza (29-0, 25 KOs) retained his WBO featherweight title with a third-round TKO over Ricardo Blandón (21-7, 14 KOs), but a severe cut ended the fight before it could become much of a contest. The champion was comfortably ahead when the ringside doctor intervened on Saturday’s Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli undercard in Riyadh.

Blandón accepted the opportunity on roughly a week’s notice after mandatory challenger Lorenzo Parra was ruled out. He faced a difficult task against Espinoza, and the opening rounds offered little indication that he could overcome the difference in technique. The Mexican established his jab, applied pressure, and made the replacement challenger work to get within punching distance.

Espinoza’s length gave him control of the approach. Blandón needed to get past the jab before he could make his own power useful, but he struggled to do that consistently. The champion could initiate the action from farther out, leaving the Nicaraguan trying to close ground while dealing with incoming punches.

That combination of reach and pressure made Espinoza difficult to dislodge. He did not have to surrender the initiative to use his physical advantages, and Blandón never established enough offense to make him reconsider his approach. For the brief time they fought, the champion dictated the terms.

The cut became the decisive factor in the third round. Its severity prompted the doctor to stop the contest, producing a TKO rather than allowing the scheduled twelve-round bout to continue. This was a medical ending, with the condition of Blandón’s eye determining the finish rather than a knockdown or a referee intervention during an unanswered attack.

That distinction matters when judging the performance. Espinoza was winning clearly, but the fight ended before he could demonstrate how thoroughly he might break down the challenger. The result rewarded his early control without providing the more complete finish that his pressure appeared capable of producing.

For Blandón, the short preparation and sudden ending made this a frustrating world-title opportunity. He arrived with four consecutive victories and respectable punching power, but neither translated into sustained success against the champion. Once the cut became too serious, there was no opportunity to attempt a recovery over the remaining rounds.

Espinoza had been out of action since stopping Arnold Khegai in November 2025. Returning with a successful defense keeps his championship run moving, although fewer than three completed rounds offered limited work after that absence. Blandón could not extend him enough to reveal much about his longer-distance sharpness.

The original opponent change also reduced what Espinoza could gain from the night. Beating a replacement challenger was necessary to protect his position, but it was unlikely to carry the significance of a successful mandatory defense against Parra. The abrupt medical stoppage narrowed that opportunity further.

Espinoza remains a difficult proposition at featherweight because his unusual height comes with an attacking style that prevents opponents from simply waiting outside. Blandón experienced that difficulty immediately. The champion kept his belt with little trouble, but a stronger opponent and a fuller contest are needed to give his next defense greater substance.

Having a world champion like Espinoza share the ring with a replacement drafted on seven days notice made for grim viewing. You could tell within ninety seconds Blandon had neither the footwork nor the size to deal with a six foot one featherweight, let alone mount meaningful offense.

Blandon was essentially a sacrifice brought in to salvage television time once Lorenzo Parra fell out. When the doctor stepped in to halt it over that eye cut, it almost felt like an act of mercy rather than a dramatic championship conclusion. Nobody gained anything from it. Espinoza gets a three round workout that told us nothing new, Blandon collects a paycheck after taking punishment, and the audience gets robbed of a genuine title contest.

Ghana News.title: People want constitutional reforms; our politics is not delivering the development promised – Dr Asante
Ghana News.content:
The Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships at the Ghana Center for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), Dr Kojo Pumpuni Asante, says there is a growing demand among Ghanaians for constitutional reforms.

He argues that the country’s current political system has failed to deliver the level of development citizens were promised.

Speaking on JoyNews’ The Law, in a discussion on constitutional reform and efforts to bridge Ghana’s political divide, Dr Asante said people from all walks of life increasingly recognise the need to strengthen the country’s governance system.

“I think what is clear if you go around the country is that people want change. Our politics is not delivering the development promise that we want,” he said on Sunday, November 1.

According to him, the demand for change cuts across different sections of society, including young people, civil society organisations and professionals.

“Everybody, it doesn't matter their background,” he said, noting that youth groups associated with the constitutional reform process were actively engaging students across the country.

Dr Asante said even young people in secondary schools have expressed concerns about the current state of the country’s governance and political system.

“If you even listen to people in secondary schools, they know that what we have is not good,” he stated.

He, however, acknowledged that Ghana’s current constitutional system has served the country for more than three decades, but said there was now a rare opportunity to strengthen it to better meet the country’s development needs.

“We have at least—it has served us well for over three decades. I think we have a rare opportunity to strengthen it so that it can continue to serve us well,” he said.

With Ghana set to mark 70 years of independence next year, Dr Asante said successfully advancing the constitutional reform process would be a fitting milestone for the country.

“Given that next year will be 70 years of independence, I think it would be a befitting birthday present if we're able to get it past this time around,” he added.

His comments come as the Citizens’ Platform for Constitutional Reform intensifies efforts to mobilise public support and encourage citizen participation in the constitutional reform process.

Dr Asante explained that the platform, which was launched in November 2025, was established to mobilise citizens to support what he described as a credible constitutional reform process and outcome.

He said the platform currently brings together more than 100 civil society organisations, as well as professional groups, including the Trades Union Congress (TUC) and the Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association.

The platform also has a 25-member steering committee chaired by Dr Akosua Darkwa of the Network for Women's Rights in Ghana (NETRIGHT).

According to Dr Asante, the group has been actively educating citizens about the constitutional reform process to prepare them to play a meaningful role.

He said the platform is also helping citizens understand and assess the recommendations of the Constitutional Review Committee (CRC), the government's position paper and the views of citizens on the proposals.

Dr Asante stressed that the opportunity for constitutional reform should not be wasted on superficial changes.

“Citizens of all walks of life want to see change and that's why I really think that if we want to do this, we should do it well and not just paper over the cracks,” he said.

Beirut airport in Lebanon



The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has confirmed the arrest of a Syrian national at the Rafic Hariri International Airport in Beirut, Lebanon, after he allegedly attempted to transport approximately 40 kilogrammes of suspected cocaine from Ghana.

The suspect was arrested on Saturday, October 31, 2026, following his arrival from Accra, Ghana, with the suspected narcotic substance concealed in two pieces of luggage.

Drugs seized by the Customs in Beirut's International Airport on Oct. 30, 2026. (Credit: Lebanese Customs)



In a statement issued on November 1, 2026, NACOC said it was working to identify and arrest the suspect's accomplices in Ghana as part of ongoing operations to dismantle the criminal network behind the shipment.

The Commission explained that the arrest followed a coordinated controlled delivery operation involving close collaboration between Ghanaian and Lebanese drug law enforcement authorities.

According to NACOC, the joint operation was designed to identify and apprehend targets at both ends of the drug supply chain while gathering intelligence to dismantle the wider transnational criminal syndicate responsible for the shipment.

The Commission said the successful operation highlights the importance of international cooperation and intelligence-sharing in the fight against drug trafficking.

It further reaffirmed Ghana's commitment, alongside Lebanon, to disrupting international drug trafficking networks through cross-border law enforcement collaboration.

Mfantsipim School has honoured distinguished alumni, members of staff and corporate partners at its 150th anniversary Awards and Fundraising Dinner, held on Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Executive Chairman of KGL Group, Alex Apau Dadey, received two honours — the Partner of Impact Award and a special category award recognising his contributions to Mfantsipim.

The live auction featured artworks, a limited release of 10 custom anniversary Caveman Watches and a Collector's Edition of the school's 150th Anniversary Anthology.

The evening also featured performances by Ghanaian artistes Sefa and Efya.

Its Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships, Dr Kojo Pumpuni Asante, believes the anniversary presents an opportunity for the country to strengthen its constitutional framework and address longstanding weaknesses in its governance system.

Speaking on JoyNews’ The Law, Dr Asante said Ghana had a rare opportunity to improve the 1992 Constitution, which has guided the country for more than three decades.

“And given that next year, 70 years, will be 70 years of independence, I think it will be a befitting birthday present if we're able to get it past this time now,” he said on Sunday, November 1.

He argued that citizens from different backgrounds were increasingly demanding changes to the country's political and governance arrangements because the current system was not delivering the development outcomes they expected.

Dr Asante said the growing interest in constitutional reform was not limited to civil society organisations, adding that young people were also expressing concerns about the country's governance system.

He disclosed that CDD-Ghana had established youth platforms that were engaging secondary school students across the country to encourage their participation in discussions about constitutional reform.

According to him, the broad interest in reform explains why more than 100 civil society leaders and organisations have come together under the Citizens Platform for Constitutional Reform.

“I think what is clear, if you go around the country, is that people want change. Our politics is not delivering the development promise that we want,” he said.

He added that the country should use the current constitutional review process to make substantive changes rather than overlook fundamental weaknesses.

“We have, at least, it has served us well for over three decades. I think we have a rare opportunity to strengthen it so that it can continue to serve us well,” he said.

Dr Asante stressed that the process must be approached carefully to ensure that the concerns of citizens are adequately addressed.

“Citizens of all walks of life want to see change. And that's why I really think that if we want to do this, we should do it well. And not just step over the cracks,” he added.

The Citizens Platform for Constitutional Reform brings together civil society organisations and other stakeholders seeking to broaden public participation in discussions about changes to Ghana's constitutional and governance arrangements.

Ghana News.title: Climate diplomacy meets frontline reality: AGN opens COP31 strategy session amid urgent El Niño warnings
Ghana News.content:
The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) has opened a crucial two-day strategy meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, to prepare for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).

The urgency of their negotiations is underscored by alarming real-world climate advisories emerging across the African continent.

Convening from November 1 to 2, the negotiating body seeks to unify Africa's voice ahead of global climate talks, a task rendered vital by newly confirmed meteorological data indicating severe climate shocks ahead.

Concurrently, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has issued an urgent advisory confirming that a very strong El Niño event is developing in the Pacific Ocean and will heavily influence West African weather into the first half of 2027.

The convergence of high-level climate diplomacy in Türkiye and frontline weather advisories in Ghana highlights an imperative message for COP31: international climate governance must deliver concrete, actionable outcomes that build resilience and safeguard vulnerable communities against devastating climate impacts.

The AGN plays a central role in coordinating the positions of African nations and representing the continent’s common interests within the United Nations climate process.

The strategy meeting in Antalya brings negotiators together to consolidate preparations, strengthen continental coordination, and ensure a unified stance at COP31 and subsequent international forums.

Opening the session, AGN Chair Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah stressed that unity, cooperation, and collective commitment are essential to elevating Africa’s voice on the global stage. He commended members for their steadfast dedication despite demanding schedules and competing professional responsibilities.

"The spirit of teamwork demonstrated by members will be crucial in ensuring a coordinated approach to the negotiations and securing outcomes that reflect Africa’s priorities and development needs," emphasized Dr. Amoah, urging negotiators to maintain their shared sense of purpose.

The Antalya consultations aim to reinforce the group’s collective climate diplomacy and build institutional capacity to secure international agreements focused on adaptation funding, developmental equity, and robust support for climate-vulnerable populations.

The Looming Climate Shock: GMet Confirms Intensifying El Niño

While diplomatic strategies take shape in Türkiye, operational advisories from West Africa illustrate the escalating environmental pressures facing African nations.

In an official advisory issued on October 29, 2026, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) confirmed that a very strong El Niño event is intensifying in the Pacific Ocean.

Joint observations from GMet and leading international climate centers—including the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), the International Research Institute for Climate and Society (IRI), and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)—indicate that the event will peak between now and January 2027 before gradually weakening through the first half of 2027.

Historical experience demonstrates Ghana’s high vulnerability to El Niño-induced rainfall variability. Previous very strong events in 1982/83, 1997/98, and 2015/16, as well as the moderate event of 2023/24, severely impacted key economic and social sectors across the country:

Agricultural Production: Severe rainfall deficits disrupted planting cycles, reduced crop yields, and threatened food security.

Water Resources and Hydroelectric Power: Extended dry spells depleted reservoir levels, constraining water availability and hydroelectric power generation.

Public Health: Extended heat and dry dust transport created environmental conditions conducive to disease outbreaks.

The GMet advisory for 2027 underscores that the consequences of extreme weather fall most heavily on vulnerable populations. Protecting these communities requires translating meteorological forecasts into targeted mitigation measures across key sectors, including health, water resources, the agricultural sector and food security.

The parallel developments in Antalya and West Africa illustrate why global climate negotiations cannot take place in a vacuum.

As AGN negotiators work to shape Africa's strategic stance ahead of COP31, the realities on the ground in Ghana demonstrate that climate policy must ultimately serve to shield vulnerable communities from environmental disaster.

By coupling strong, unified diplomatic advocacy with robust local disaster preparedness, African nations can better protect lives, safeguard food and energy systems, and build enduring resilience against an increasingly volatile climate.

Ghana News.title: UBIDS charts path to growth with academic wins despite transition challenges
Ghana News.content:
The University of Business and Integrated Development Studies (UBIDS) is recording significant academic gains as it navigates the challenges of its early years of autonomy.

During a parliamentary oversight visit by the Education Committee, the university highlighted its progress and resilience despite the difficulties associated with transitioning to full independence.

The Vice-Chairman of the Committee, Joseph Kwame Kumah, who led the delegation, commended the university's efforts, particularly after it had to independently repackage 177 academic programmes when its former parent university declined to process their accreditation.

The Vice-Chancellor of UBIDS, Prof. Emmanuel Kanchebe Derbile, disclosed that management had secured approval from the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to recruit new assistant lecturers. The move follows the loss of 55 key staff members to the University for Development Studies (UDS) during the transition.

Dr Fred Kyei Asamoah, Member of Parliament for Offinso North, also examined the university's strategic plans, including its vision to establish a medical school by 2027, and commended some of its flagship initiatives.

However, he raised questions about the sustainability of the university's operating model, particularly the disparity between its weekend master's and regular student populations. The university has 1,898 weekend master's students compared with 356 regular students, prompting management to outline clearer plans for ensuring the institution's long-term viability.

Infrastructure constraints

On infrastructure, Prof. Derbile disclosed that a government debt of GH¢114 million relating to land acquisition had slowed campus development.

He said a new 600-bed facility would accommodate only about six per cent of the university's 10,000-student population, underscoring the need for targeted support to help newly established universities meet their infrastructure requirements.

Despite the constraints, UBIDS continues to register academic achievements. Its School of Law recorded a notable success, with 27 of its 47 graduates passing their professional entrance examinations at the first attempt.

Promoting gender inclusion

The university is also taking steps to address gender disparities in higher education.

Female enrolment declines from 52 per cent at the diploma level to just 15 per cent at the PhD level, a trend the university is seeking to reverse through targeted interventions.

As part of these efforts, it has established a new Centre for Gender Diversity and Social Inclusion to mentor female scholars and promote greater participation in advanced academic study.

Another flagship initiative is the Practical Training Programme (PTP), directed by Prof. Stanley K. Dary. The programme deploys students into local communities to undertake advocacy and skills training, an approach commended by the parliamentary committee during its visit.

Management is appealing for special financial dispensation for newly established universities to help them overcome transitional difficulties, consolidate their gains and establish a sustainable foundation for future growth.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
