World.title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
World.content:
Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted in German cities over the cost of living.

Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who were targeting emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.

Thousands joined largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day. They were organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.

The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.

On Sunday, Germany's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told Bild newspaper that overnight police had prevented "violence like that seen in Paris" in recent weeks and called for "harsh punishments" for rioters and looters.

Overnight, a large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.

Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.

Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".

She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."

World.title: Judge dismisses Trump's lawsuit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein birthday book
World.content:
A US judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's $10bn (Â£7.4bn) lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal, ruling the suit was "grasping at straws".

Trump had sued the media outlet's parent company Dow Jones and its leader Rupert Murdoch last year after it reported on a letter allegedly written by Trump to disgraced financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein as part of a birthday book in 2003, before Epstein was charged with sex crimes.

Trump has denied writing or signing the letter, which included suggestive language and a drawing of the outline of a woman's body.

Judge Darrin Gayles threw out the case, finding the suit runs counter to the First Amendment, which protects freedom of the press.

Gayles had already once dismissed the defamation lawsuit, which sought $20 billion in damages. Trump's team refiled the suit seeking $10 billion, and this time, the judge threw out the case "with prejudice," meaning the suit cannot be filed again.

The news outlet's story about Epstein's 50th birthday book, external - and the letter with Trump's name - came as the Trump administration battled intense bipartisan criticism over the summer for its handling of Epstein documents.

Trump had said the newspaper had slandered him and violated libel laws in publishing the article.

In his 20-page ruling, Gayles noted the paper's "thoughtful and detailed âinvestigation" that led to the story and said the lawsuit was "grasping at âstraws" to "manufacture flaws" in their work.

World.title: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
World.content:
Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi for a rally demanding the resignation of India's chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.

Organised by the opposition INDIA bloc and led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress party, the protest drew many of the alliance's most prominent leaders in a show of strength against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

Protesters waved flags and chanted "Save the vote, save the country" and "Vote thief, give up power".

It was the latest in a series of protests over electoral roll revision that the opposition says has removed eligible voters to benefit the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP and the Election Commission deny the allegations.

The crowds gathered at Ramlila Maidan, a sprawling ground in central Delhi known for hosting major political and cultural events. Some protesters sang and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs, while others waited beneath a large canopy in the colours of the Indian flag to hear opposition leaders speak.

Gandhi and several senior opposition leaders arrived at the venue in an open jeep, travelling through crowds of cheering supporters.

The event was also attended by Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, alongside leaders of regional parties such as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti, Supriya Sule and Tejashwi Yadav.

Addressing the crowds, Rahul Gandhi said those gathered had sent a message to Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

"This is not the voice of a single political party or of politicians. It is the voice of India's youth, women, farmers and workers," he said.

"We will not allow democracy to be destroyed in India. We will not allow the constitution to be destroyed."

Other opposition leaders echoed Gandhi's criticism of the Election Commission. Congress president Kharge said the alliance would continue its campaign until Kumar resigned, while Banerjee pledged to keep fighting against what she described as threats to democracy.

Speaking to reporters in Delhi on Sunday, senior BJP leader and federal minister JP Nadda accused the opposition of trying to create unrest and destabilise the government under the guise of defending democracy.

He described the rally as a "calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy - in the name of democracy".

World.title: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied front-line city
World.content:
Warning: This story contains graphic content.

Olha has one word to describe what life has been like in the front-line city of Oleshky over the past few years: "Horror".

Disembarking alongside her from a coach in the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv with their immediate family and dog, her husband Viacheslav put it this way: "We came back from hell."

The couple were among hundreds of residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city who crossed into northern Ukraine via Belarus on Saturday, many reuniting with loved ones they had not seen for years.

Oleshky, seized by Russia during the first few days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River and on the other side by Russian forces.

Olha and Viacheslav had lived there with their son and daughter, both in their 30s. Even as the shelling around them intensified, they feared that trying to escape could be even more dangerous, with routes mined and subject to drone attack.

As supplies dwindled, the couple said they made an attempt to find food by crossing through minefields earlier this month. "People were stepping on mines, dying and being maimed, all just to survive," Olha told the BBC.

Those who were too afraid to go out in the city had resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive.

"We saw that the situation wasn't getting any better, so we realised we had to get out," Olha said.

World.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
World.content:
There were raw emotional scenes as people evacuated from the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed from Belarus into the Ukrainian region of Chernihiv.

Families cried as they reunited with relatives they had not seen for years, with two sisters running and crying out as they embraced their father.

Some elderly residents were so weak they were carried on stretchers. They had been trapped in the frontline city without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for her efforts in brokering a local ceasefire that paved the way for their evacuation on Friday.

Upon their arrival, Dasha and Anya Palii sprinted across the tarmac screaming towards the bus carrying their father Mykhailo.

Their cries and their tears captured the sheer relief of three years of desperate worry, fearing they would never see him again.

Their mother Zhanna clasped Mykhailo's face and stroked his forehead again and again, as if checking he was the same man she had left behind. He promised her, finally, they will now get married.

Tetiana and Volodymyr, an older couple carrying their cat, told the BBC they no longer have a home, after it was burned down in the first year of the war. They have been living in the abandoned house of a neighbour.

They said they instantly took the decision to leave but feared their journey could be disrupted. Now they have to work out where to go next and how to rebuild their lives.

World.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
World.content:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) assets stolen in a hack on Thursday.

The remaining 10% may take longer to source in the required amounts, the company added.

Binance has consistently pledged to cover 100% of the losses from what is suspected to be crypto's biggest hack on record and said it has set aside more than $6.34bn in company funds to do so.

"Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users," the company said in a statement on Saturday.

In an update on Sunday, Binance said withdrawals had been restored on several of its networks, after they were suspended following the hack.

It previously said withdrawals would be resumed in phases.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the attack.

The FBI said it had observed hackers converting stolen assets into a type of cryptocurrency called Ethereum and that it is expected that the assets will then be converted again using decentralised finance and instant swap services.

Two analytics firms previously told the BBC they had robust intelligence pointing to North Korean state-backed hacking unit the Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor - which was specifically named by the FBI - as the likely culprits.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday night, US President Donald Trump said, external the US is still unsure who the culprits are.

"We're learning about it. We don't know if it's North Korea - but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it," he said.

Binance said it had replenished the stolen assets using various funds and its own corporate treasury.

All holdings of the cryptocurrencies bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether are covered, along with seven other widely-traded crypto assets, the company said.

The hack is believed to be the largest in history, eclipsing the record of a $1.5bn heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025 - for which the FBI also said North Korea was responsible.

North Korea has always denied involvement in these attacks.

World.title: How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán
World.content:
Mobilisation of voters, and the role of election monitors, played a big role in the opposition victory in both countries.

Last weekend, the DE civic action group in Hungary sent 70 election monitors to Serbia, to work with students' movement representatives, visiting polling stations in the northern Serbian province of Vojvodina.

During the summer, even before the election was called, they held workshops to share their experience and methods from the Hungarian election with the Serbian students.

A key technique was to identify "infected" polling districts in advance - places where the surprisingly high number of votes for the governing party at previous elections suggested that voter intimidation or "chain voting" techniques were used.

"From around 16:00 on election day, we noticed groups of masked hooligans - VuÄiÄ supporters - gathering near voting stations," PÃ©ter Klemm, a student activist from Subotica, told the BBC. "So we sent mobile teams, and started filming everything."

Combined with the "stationary" monitors already in place, 20 to 30 volunteers at each threatened polling station acted as a strong deterrent, he believes, and prevented intimidation or fraud.

OrbÃ¡n in Hungary, VuÄiÄ in Serbia, both looked invincible. Both were powerful leaders, in office for 16 and 14 years, who had taken over state institutions and established business empires overlapping the two countries.

Orban chose cheese, VuÄiÄ meat, when they sat down to a quick lunch of traditional burek pastries at a small, popular town centre bakery in Subotica almost a year ago.

They continued to a local winery, to talk about oil and other business deals - the planned Hungarian purchase of a controlling stake in Serbia's NIS oil company. The two nationalist leaders found much in common, in business and politics, not least their friendship with Vladimir Putin in Russia and Chinese President Xi Jinping, and their strong support for Milorad Dodik, the separatist leader of the Bosnian Serbs.

A high-speed railway between Belgrade and Budapest is being built with Chinese finance and know-how.

World.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
World.content:
A federal judge has ordered the federal government to stop threatening local and state election officials with criminal charges over their role in processing election ballots.

The California judge ruled that the Department of Justice (DoJ) must stop demanding that local and state election officials set aside or not process certain ballots that the Trump administration alleges may come from non-citizens.

The ruling comes days before the midterm elections, which will determine which political party controls the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.

Trump criticised the ruling on Saturday, writing,"Why would they reject fixing Election Fraud?"

In California earlier this month, the justice department sent letters to the secretary of state and Los Angeles County Registrar demanding they set aside the ballots of 20,000 registered voters whom the Trump administration "believe" are "likely" non-citizens, according to court documents.

About a week later, armed officials from the Department of Homeland Security delivered letters to county officials and employees across California threatening criminal charges if they didn't sequester those ballots.

But the groups said they could not comply with those demands because they must follow election procedures required by state and federal law. A judge weighed in and tossed the demand, writing it would "wreak havoc" in the election.

Around the same time, the justice department reportedly began a criminal investigation into county election officials, issuing federal grand jury subpoenas.

Civil rights groups and unions representing election workers filed a legal complaint, accusing the justice department of interfering in their duty to administer the election. Judge Trina Thompson ordered the administration to halt their actions.

"Although Defendants claim that their actions are designed to halt unlawful voting by noncitizens, their actions are likely to have the effect of interfering with election administration and disenfranchising lawful voters," Judge Thompson wrote.

The Trump administration sent a similar letter about alleged non-citizen voters to Washington state and demanded that the secretary of state there cease processing the ballots, according to Thompson's order.

The manoeuvres are part of a yearslong campaign by Trump and his administration to fight alleged voter fraud that they believe is widespread, despite research showing that it is extremely rare.

Ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, the president has cast doubt on the security of the vote - alleging "rampant" cheating in postal voting and non-citizens voting. The president also offered a $1m (Â£750,000) reward to people who report cases of voter fraud in the US which lead to a conviction.

Studies, however, suggest actual cases are extremely rare. BBC Verify reported that the Heritage Foundation's database identified 24 cases of non-citizens being convicted for voting between 2005 and 2025.

In his post on Saturday, Trump said criticised recent rulings against his administration pertaining to allegations of possible election fraud and vowed to continue fighting for "Election Integrity".

World.title: CSOs urge judiciary to avoid another Imo-style embarrassment in Uzodimma’s Senate case
World.content:
A coalition of Nigerian civil society organisations (CSOs) has urged the judiciary to use the ongoing court case involving Governor Hope Uzodimma to restore public confidence in the courts.

The coalition said Uzodimma had claimed he won the Imo West senatorial race through Option A4, while the APC’s national leadership stated in a submission to the Federal High Court that he had emerged through a consensus arrangement. Describing the accounts as conflicting, the group alleged that the process was fraudulent.

The coalition also cited the controversial 2020 Supreme Court judgment that declared Uzodimma the winner of the Imo State governorship election, displacing Emeka Ihedioha. The ruling drew widespread criticism. Uzodimma is now involved in another legal dispute, this time with former governor, Rochas Okorocha. According to the coalition, the case relates to an earlier ruling in which a judge reportedly said that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) had fraudulently declared Uzodimma the winner instead of Okorocha.

The group said previous disputes over Imo State’s governorship had seriously damaged the judiciary’s reputation. It also referred to reports that several Nigerian judges had been denied U.S. visas.

The statement was issued in Bauchi, Bauchi State. It was signed by Job Samuel Danfulani of the Centre for Public Integrity, John Samuel Nangi of Nigeria Integrity Watch, and Mohammed Ibrahim Sumaila of the Northern Council of Nigeria. Other signatories were Abdullahi Salisu of the Nigeria Ethnic Nationality Forum and Hassana Mohammed of the Foundation for Democracy in Africa.

Citing human rights lawyer Chidi Odinkalu, the statement alleged that Uzodimma’s early career included working as a driver and associate of Maurice Ibekwe, a former member of the House of Representatives. Ibekwe faced high-profile fraud allegations, including an alleged scam involving hundreds of thousands of dollars and foreign nationals. He died in Kirikiri Prison in 2004 while standing trial before the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

The coalition said the fallout from the Imo governorship ruling had embarrassed the Supreme Court. It also alleged that justices involved in the case were denied U.S. visas despite holding valid travel documents. Former Cross River State Governor Donald Duke referred to the reported visa denials in his memoir and at a book launch in February 2023.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Former Cross River State Governor Donald Duke mocked the Supreme Court justices who delivered the 2020 Imo State governorship election judgment, revealing that they were denied U S visas. The justices that gave that judgment cannot go to the United States today because they have been denied visas,” Mr Duke said at the launch.

He said the justices had planned to travel to the United States for a legal conference but were denied visas, while their aides were granted them.

“They wanted to go on a retreat. Their aides were given visas, but they were not. How much disgrace can we take as a nation before we say enough is enough?” Mr Duke said.

The coalition warned that Uzodimma must not be allowed to further damage the judiciary’s reputation, saying the current case presents an important opportunity for the courts to restore public confidence.

The group also called on security agencies to investigate reports circulating in the Southeast that Uzodimma is positioning himself to become Nigeria’s first Igbo president. The coalition said it had no objection to his presidential ambition, but argued that the means by which he intends to pursue it should be established. It said the claims should not be dismissed, given Uzodimma’s rise to the governorship through the courts, and urged that his political manoeuvres not be underestimated.

The coalition recalled that Deji Adeyanju and the late Ariyo-Dare, acting through the Coalition in Defence of Nigerian Democracy and Constitution, had petitioned the United States to impose visa restrictions on Supreme Court justices. It said it hoped the judiciary would not repeat past mistakes.

The temple of justice must stand up to any fraudulent attempt by anyone to smuggle himself into 11th senate

The coalition also commended Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, for his unwavering integrity, stating that more judges of his caliber are needed in the judiciary. Despite alleged pressure and lobbying, Justice Egwuatu resisted temptation and upheld justice. For his steadfastness, he deserves both commendation and a national award.

World.title: Freedom advocates urge Nigeria to grant Africans visa-free entry
World.content:
Freedom advocacy groups, including civil society actors, and media practitioners, have urged Nigeria to grant citizens of African Union member states visa-free entry.

They argued that Nigeria’s restrictive visa policy hurts its economy and continental influence, and called for easier travel to boost tourism, investment and trade.

They made the call at the Conference of Freedom Advocates (CFA) 2026 in Abuja on Saturday. Liberalist Centre organised the event in partnership with the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), BudgIT and 3rd Eye TV, with funding from Atlas Network.

Johnson Sanni, chief operating officer of Liberalist Centre, said the conference, themed “ADVANCE”, aimed to promote liberty, innovation and citizen-led leadership.

He stressed the need to protect individual rights, uphold the rule of law and allow citizens to pursue opportunities and shape their destinies.

Call for a visa-free Nigeria

During a panel session titled “The Case for a Visa-free Nigeria”, apeakers warned that Nigeria’s restrictive visa policy undermines its participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

The discussion featured Abdullah Tijani, journalist and executive director of The Liberalist; Chike Donald, executive director of Simplefix Nigeria; and Tolulope Gbenro, president of Grow with D Oracle Empowerment Foundation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

They questioned the use of visas as a source of government revenue. In their view, business travel, conferences and other economic activities could generate greater benefits when people move more freely.

They cited the Henley Passport Index to illustrate the imbalance in international travel access. The July 2026 edition ranked Nigeria’s passport 90th among 199 passports. It also showed that Nigerian passport holders could access 44 destinations without obtaining a visa in advance.

Figures on Nigeria’s visa openness also showed that far fewer nationalities can enter the country without prior visas than the number of destinations Nigerians can access through similar arrangements abroad.

The speakers identified tourism, investment and trade as sectors that could benefit from easier movement across borders. They noted that tourism accounts for only about three per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product.

They urged Nigeria to prioritise African countries before extending visa-free or visa-on-arrival access more widely. They advocated reciprocal arrangements among African countries, citing Kenya and Rwanda as examples of countries that had taken steps to ease entry for other Africans.

Nigeria, they argued, had been slow to reciprocate and had tightened entry restrictions for some nationalities, including South Africans.

They also challenged the security argument for strict visa restrictions. According to them, terrorism, banditry and kidnapping stem largely from porous land borders and local recruitment, not visitors arriving through international airports in Lagos and Abuja.

To address security concerns, they recommended modern screening systems, including biometric checks and advance passenger information, at major entry points. They maintained that visa restrictions should not serve as Nigeria’s main security measure.

“Openness begets openness,” they argued, adding that countries that admit more visitors freely are better positioned to secure easier travel access for their own citizens.

Concerns over technology and the justice system

Apart from the call for visa-free entry, speakers examined how technology dependence, weaknesses in the justice system and government policies affect freedom and development.

Speaking on artificial intelligence and human freedom in Africa, Dipo Ige, a lawyer and team lead at LawDigits, urged African countries to develop technologies that address local needs. He challenged them to move beyond copying global AI trends and identify problems in health, agriculture and education that technology could solve.

He argued that AI should serve African interests rather than deepen dependence on foreign technologies.

He stressed: “Our constraints should shape our strategy, not stop our ambition.”

On Nigeria’s justice system, Festus Ogun, managing partner at FOLEGAL, questioned whether the courts still serve ordinary citizens.

Speaking on “What to Do with Our Rule of Law”, he argued that the system treats poor and wealthy Nigerians differently.

Mr Ogun questioned whether the judiciary remained the “last hope of the common man” or had become the “lost hope of the common man”. He argued that ordinary citizens struggle to obtain justice, making Nigeria’s system a “judicial system” rather than a justice system.

He identified repeated adjournments, judges’ absence and prolonged proceedings as obstacles that leave litigants frustrated, even when they eventually win their cases. He called for reforms to address systemic problems within the judiciary.

Government accountability and economic freedom also featured in the discussions.

During a session titled “Beyond Good Intentions: Why Freedom Must Shape Nigeria’s Next Generation of Reforms”, moderated by Oluwabukola Adimula, Programmes Associate at African Liberty, participants questioned the numerous taxes and charges imposed on Nigerians, including bank card maintenance fees, and how governments spend the revenue.

Panelists Bayonle Fesobi, Director of Research at Ominira Initiative, and Chike Donald, Executive Director of Simplefix Nigeria, criticised successive governments for recycling policies without addressing previous failures.

They described taxation as “theft” when citizens receive little in return. They also called for stronger monitoring and evaluation of government policies to prevent administrations from abandoning programmes without assessing their outcomes.

At a fireside civic panel titled “What Would You Advance? Changing Perspectives From Citizen Frustration to Sustainable Solutions”, Leonard Ogunweide, founder of Face of Liberty International, moderated the discussion.

Hashimu Adamu, Chairperson of the AU-EU Youth Voices Lab Youth Advisory Board and Executive Lead of Voices & Data for Policy and Development Initiative, Tolulope Gbenro and Khadijat Akewushola, a Public Policy and Governance Specialist at the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), urged citizens to hold all three tiers of government accountable.

They encouraged Nigerians to identify community problems, engage relevant public institutions and mobilise others to develop solutions. They also challenged young people to take responsibility for social change rather than postpone their contributions.

ALSO READ: Togo removes visa requirement for African nationals

At a session titled “The Price and Promise of Freedom in a Changing Africa”, Abinye Briggs, Victor Ndeche, Head of Operations at Glass Institute, and Joy Una, a public affairs and policy professional, examined how economic hardship and weak public institutions restrict individual freedom.

They identified poor infrastructure, unreliable electricity, weak healthcare and low purchasing power as barriers to economic activity and business growth.

Drawing on examples from other countries, they highlighted social support systems such as free public education, childcare assistance, food support and transport benefits. They argued that these measures ease the burden of basic needs and give people greater opportunities to pursue their ambitions.

The speakers also called on governments to improve living conditions, given their control over financial and human resources. They stressed that citizens must participate in governance beyond seeking political office or joining protests.

Participants share lessons from the event

In interviews with PREMIUM TIMES, participants highlighted lessons from the conference and how they planned to apply them.

Zaka Peter, Chief Executive Officer of Lifted Initiative, said a breakout session on tracking public funds, facilitated by BudgIT at the conference, taught him how to monitor government spending and hold officials accountable for projects they fail to deliver.

The conference also encouraged him to speak up about social issues despite his previous fear of public speaking.

“One of the motivations I got here is that whether you speak or you don’t speak, you are still going to die. So, speak for the next generation,” he said.

He promised to share the knowledge with other young Nigerians through his organisation and social media platforms.

Also, Chenka Sunday, a UNICEF Global Youth Advisor and U-Reporter, said the conference strengthened her understanding of the right to access public information.

“The generality of what I’m taking home is that I can question the government because it is my right,” she said.

She said a breakout session on freedom of information, facilitated by CJID, taught her how to submit information requests. It also provided guidance on the appropriate officials and institutions to approach. The session encouraged her to exercise her right more actively and demand answers from public institutions.

World.title: Joint naval, army forces kill 34 insurgents in Lake Chad region
World.content:
Operatives of the Nigerian Navy Marines and Nigerian Army have conducted “intelligence-driven” offensives against terrorists ravaging the troubled Lake Chad region, killing at least 34.

Naval spokesperson, Abiodun Folrunsho, disclosed this in a statement on Saturday, saying the operations were conducted between 28 and 30 October.

The operatives, stationed at the Naval Base Lake Chad, launched the offensives in collaboration with operatives of Army 403 Amphibious Brigade, a tactical unit operating under Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east.

On 28 October, a total of 28 terrorists suspected to be members of Boko Haram were killed “in action,” Mr Folorunsho said.

During the subsequent offensive launched on 30 October, the operatives, according to the naval spokesperson, killed an additional six terrorists at their enclave identified as Dumba.

“The casualty figures remain subject to further verification as operational assessments continue,” he said.

Mr Folorunsho did not specify whether the joint offensives were conducted on war boats or on the ground. However, one blurry picture of a slain terrorist suggests that the battle was fought on the ground.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Boko Haram and its rival Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) are entrenched in Lake islands, often launching attacks on security and civilian targets, while occasionally fighting themselves on boats. Videos of their infighting, especially on water, have gone viral at different times

Because they exploit the vast waters of Lake Chad and the maze of islands to tax local fishermen while evading military raids, regional security forces fighting this protracted war under the umbrella of the Multi-National Joint Task Force (MNJTF) have integrated naval and riverine patrols to strip the insurgents of their sanctuary.

ALSO READ: NAF strikes ISWAP leadership cell in Lake Chad region

With the escalating geopolitical and structural challenges rocking MNJTF, observers say naval and riverine patrols have significantly reduced, shifting major responsibilities to Nigerian forces, which continue to deploy air and naval assets.

Mr Folorunsho said the marines, since their recent deployment to Lake Chad Bay, “served as a force multiplier under Operation Hadin Kai, strengthening the conduct of offensive operations against terrorist elements. “

“Their operational contributions have enhanced the capacity to target terrorist enclaves, disrupt hostile activities and deny Boko Haram terrorists freedom of action within the Lake Chad area,” he added. “These efforts continue to support the degradation of terrorist capabilities and advance ongoing operations to restore peace and stability in the North-east.”

World.title: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduces new wife
World.content:
The senior pastor of Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, introduced his new wife, Mo Jasyme, to his congregation.

The pastor introduced Ms Jasyme during Sunday’s church service in Ilupeju, Lagos, confirming his new marriage following the collapse of his previous union with Oluwakemi Banjoko.

Mr Odukoya married Ms Banjoko in London in March 2013, and they have two children.

His new wife, Ms Jasyme, also previously married British-Nigerian record producer Mosadoluwa Adegboye, known as itsMOSA.

A designer and creative entrepreneur, Ms Jasyme collaborated with her former husband on various creative ventures over the years.

The circumstances surrounding her divorce from Mr Adegboye, including when the marriage ended, remain unclear.

“Search and found”

The unveiling followed a social media post that Mr Odukoya shared on Saturday, triggering speculation about his marital status.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The actor-turned-pastor posted a close-up image of two hands on Facebook.

One belonged to a woman who wore long green nails and a prominent diamond engagement ring, while the other showed his hand with a diamond-studded wedding band.

He accompanied the photograph with the caption, “To a new beginning.”

Speaking during the service, Mr Odukoya said he had done many things alone since taking up pastoral duties, a situation he noted contradicted the biblical teaching that it was not good for man to be alone.

He subsequently described Ms Jasyme as the missing rib he had searched for and found as he stood beside her on the altar.

He said: “The Bible says it’s not good to be alone. He said, I will find somebody suitable. Described as when Adam saw, he said, this is the flesh of my flesh. Bone of my bone: my left and right ribs. So, I was looking and searching. And I found. There are what we call Kairos moments. You say Kairos moments, when the Kairos moments.

“I’m sure some of you saw the post. Somebody, some people say, is it artwork? Is it, is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, no, no, it’s my wife. Let me introduce to you. For the first time, Pastor Mrs Odukoya. And your first lady, and my wife. Let me be a gentleman. Pastor Mrs Odukoya. Please bring out my wife, please.”

After Mr Odukoya introduced her to the congregation, Ms Jasyme expressed her delight at being in the church.

“Good morning, family. It’s my pleasure and honour to be here and stand alongside my husband. The senior pastor of the Fountain of Life Church.”

Father’s blessing

After presenting his wife, Mr Odukoya called on Tunde Bakare, the founder of Citadel Global Community Church (CGCC), to bless their union.

The cleric walked to the altar with his wife, Olayide, and offered prayers for the newlyweds.

He prayed that God would strengthen their marriage and make their household a centre for kingdom activities.

“In the name of Jesus. Father, we bless you in the name of the Lord for this day. We are not here to sweep anything under the carpet. All things must be done decently and in order. We give you glory and praise because you have begun a good work and you perfect it in the life of your son and his wife, in the mighty name of Jesus. Lord, when you show up, you don’t take sides.

“You take over. We ask that you take over the Fountain of Life Church from this day forward. Let it expand. Let it grow. I bless you in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Your union will be a power union. Your family and household will be the centre of kingdom activities. What you abandon now is bound in heaven. What is set loose on earth is set loose in heaven”, he said.

Mr Bakare also prayed that their home would grow stronger each day and become a model for others to emulate rather than a cautionary tale.

“This home is built on the foundation of peace and stability and love of God. Nothing will desecrate it. Nothing will dismantle it. It will rise stronger and stronger daily, and it will become an example to follow, not a mistake to avoid.

“In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, in Jesus mighty name, we pray. When Jesus Christ rose from the dead.”

World.title: BON Awards 2026: Love and New Notes, The Herd, Colours of Fire lead nominations
World.content:
Love and New Notes has emerged as the biggest contender at the 2026 Best of Nollywood (BON) Awards, securing nine nominations, while The Herd follows closely with eight.

The nominations list, released by the organisers ahead of this year’s ceremony in Enugu, also features several other productions competing across acting, directing, technical and major film categories.

Four films, The Creek, Aba Blues, Colours of Fire and Efunroye: The Unicorn, secured seven nominations each, while Asurf Oluseyi’s 3 Cold Dishes received six.

Behind the Scenes and Agesinkole (King of Thieves) 2 earned five nominations apiece.

The nominations place several of Nollywood’s established actors and emerging talents in contention for this year’s awards, with competition particularly strong in the leading acting categories.

In the Best Actor category, Bucci Franklin earned a nomination for his performance in The Creek, alongside Kanayo O. Kanayo for Grandpa Must Obey, Jide Kene Achufusi for Aba Blues, Timini Egbuson for Love and New Notes, Uzor Arukwe for Colours of Fire and Wale Ojo for 3 Cold Dishes.

The Best Actress category features Scarlet Gomez for Behind the Scenes, Osas Ighodaro for Colours of Fire and 3 Cold Dishes, Mercy Aigbe for Everything Is New Again, Sharon Ooja for Ordinary People and Nse Ikpe-Etim for Devil Is a Liar.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ighodaro’s double nomination makes her a notable contender in the category.

The supporting acting categories also feature a mix of familiar faces. Eniola Badmus, Destiny Etiko, Damilola Oni, Nancy Isime, Linda Ejiofor-Suleiman and Bisola Aiyeola are nominated for Best Supporting Actress.

For Best Supporting Actor, the nominees include Akeem Ogara, Mike Ezuruonye, Kelechi Udegbe, Jide Awobona, Prince Nelson Enwerem, Abba Ali Zaky and Ibrahim Suleiman.

Competition across major categories

The Director of the Year category features six nominees, including Toka McBaror for The Creek, Jack’enneth Opukeme for Aba Blues, Kayode Kasum for Love and New Notes, Bayo Tijani and Abbey Lanre for Efunroye: The Unicorn, Asurf Oluseyi for 3 Cold Dishes and Daniel Etim Effiong for The Herd.

The six films also feature in the Movie of the Year category, making it a closely contested race among the productions that dominated the nominations.

In the Best Screenplay category, The Herd, The Creek, 3 Cold Dishes, The Covenant, Love and New Notes and Si Olorun (A Letter to God) are in contention.

Other categories recognise achievements in cinematography, editing, production design, costume, sound, soundtrack, makeup and special effects.

The awards also include categories for Best Indigenous Film, Best Social Message, Best Short Film and Best Documentary, reflecting the range of productions considered for this year’s edition.

Among the documentary nominees are Marked and The Rhythm of Ancestors: Yoruba Bata, while Scratch, The Covenant and Ordinary People will compete for Best Series.

The Best Child Actor category features five nominees, including Royal Aziomaku for Alechen(u), Daniel Adeshina for Irin Ajo, Fiyin Asenuga for Grandpa Must Obey, Nnamani Chibuike Wisdom for The 9th and Tonye Tam Azorbo for Ek(e)mini.

The Best Child Actress category has six nominees, including Fisayo ‘Abebi’ Amodemaja, Michelle Onamade, Marcella Aipoh, Iremide Adeshina, Okorie Emmanuella and Future Lolo Lamai.

Enugu to host 2026 edition

The 2026 edition of the BON Awards will be held in Enugu, bringing filmmakers, actors and other industry stakeholders to the southeastern state for the annual celebration of Nigerian cinema.

The nominations span commercial productions, indigenous-language films, short films, documentaries and television series, highlighting the range of projects competing for recognition this year.

The BON Awards, which celebrate achievements in Nigeria’s film industry, will announce this year’s winners at the ceremony in Enugu.

World.title: Tinubu’s pledge on electricity must be considered in full context- APC Campaign Council
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council says President Bola Tinubu will present his scorecard on the power sector and explain any shortcomings in fulfilling his 2023 electricity campaign promises as he seeks re-election in 2027.

The campaign council said the president remained committed to his pledge to end estimated billing and improve electricity supply, but acknowledged that resolving Nigeria’s longstanding power sector challenges remained unfinished business.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, urged Nigerians to consider the full context of Mr Tinubu’s campaign promise, arguing that some recent public commentary had reproduced his remarks without including his qualification that he would provide adequate reasons for any failure to deliver.

At a meeting with members of the Organised Private Sector in Lagos ahead of the 2023 general elections, Mr Tinubu had promised to end estimated billing and ensure stable electricity supply.

“Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore,” he had said.

He added that if he failed to fulfil the promise, Nigerians should not vote for him in a second-term election unless he provided adequate reasons for his inability to deliver.

Mr Alake said a fair assessment of the pledge should consider the complete statement alongside the administration’s record since assuming office in May 2023.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He listed the signing of the Electricity Act 2023, the Presidential Metering Initiative, the settlement of legacy debts and investments in transmission infrastructure among the administration’s interventions in the sector.

According to him, Mr Tinubu signed the Electricity Act on 9 June 2023, less than two weeks after assuming office, effectively allowing state governments to participate in electricity generation, distribution and transmission.

He said Lagos, Enugu, Abia, Ekiti, Oyo, Kaduna and Niger states had begun taking advantage of the legislation by establishing their own electricity regulatory agencies and attracting private investment.

The spokesperson also said the administration inherited more than N6 trillion in legacy debts accumulated between 2015 and 2025 and introduced a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified obligations to 21 electricity generation and gas companies.

He said the first two tranches of the programme had raised more than N1.2 trillion towards settling the debts.

On metering, Mr Alake said the Presidential Metering Initiative was established to address a gap of more than seven million meters, adding that over 1.5 million customers had been metered under the programme in the last three years.

He also cited the Rural Electrification Agency’s efforts to connect universities, hospitals and rural communities to solar power.

The administration, he said, had unveiled plans to modernise the Osogbo Grid Control Centre, which was built more than 60 years ago, and construct an East-West super grid.

Mr Alake further disclosed that the Federal Executive Council approved the first batch of five Transmission Company of Nigeria substations for upgrading in December 2024, with the projects expected to be completed and commissioned before the end of the administration’s first term.

READ ALSO: Benue residents groan as JED disconnects electricity after attack on staff

He said the council approved another batch of projects in June 2026, involving the construction of eight new substations and the upgrading of four existing ones.

According to him, the projects require specialised equipment with long procurement and delivery timelines, making immediate completion unrealistic.

On electricity tariffs, Mr Alake said the administration had aligned tariffs more closely with costs to improve liquidity in the electricity market while introducing service bands to balance the financial needs of distribution companies with affordability for consumers.

He said the government was also putting measures in place to protect low-income households while investments in substations and grid expansion continued.

The spokesperson cited recent investments by Geregu Power Plc in new power transformers to improve operations at its Geregu 1 Power Plant as evidence that the administration’s interventions were beginning to encourage fresh investments in the sector.

He also said Mr Tinubu had reviewed the Presidential Power Initiative inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari and signed an acceleration agreement with German partners in December 2023 to fast-track projects aimed at improving the national transmission grid.

“Fixing the electricity market and power sector is ongoing work,” Mr Alake said.

He maintained that the president had not abandoned his electricity pledge and would present his administration’s achievements and outstanding challenges to Nigerians as he seeks a second term.

World.title: Katsina govt denies violence link to Radda’s campaign rally
World.content:
The Katsina State Government has attributed violence in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to a disagreement over a Maulud procession, denying reports linking the incident to Governor Dikko Radda’s campaign rally.

Two vehicles were reportedly burnt and several people injured during the disturbance.

In a statement on Saturday, the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Ibrahim Kaula Mohammed, said participants in the religious procession disagreed with security personnel over designated routes, causing confusion along a public street.

He said the incident had no connection with the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally in Faskari.

Two vehicles reportedly burnt

LEADERSHIP newspaper reported that suspected hoodlums burnt two vehicles, including one belonging to the Musa Adamu Network (MAN), a political association. Several people were reportedly injured, while shops were damaged.

Nura Yandaki, chairman of the association’s caucus, told the newspaper that he was travelling with 11 other members to the governor’s rally when the disturbance occurred.

He said trouble began around a Maulud procession before suspected hoodlums attacked passing vehicles.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Yandaki said members of his delegation escaped unharmed, but their vehicle was destroyed.

An unnamed local government official also told LEADERSHIP that two vehicles were burnt and several people injured while residents and political supporters awaited the governor’s arrival.

The official said security personnel later restored order.

The government’s statement did not address the reported attacks on vehicles carrying people travelling to the rally.

Governor passed through Yankara — Govt

Mr Mohammed said Governor Radda passed safely through Yankara on his way to Faskari.

The governor visited the district head’s palace and inspected renovation works at the local government secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally.

The government called on security agencies to investigate the violence and establish what happened.

It also urged media organisations and social media users to verify information before publication and appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified reports.

World.title: NDLEA arrests two Europe-based Nigerians with 200 wraps of cocaine
World.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested two Nigerians living in Europe after they allegedly swallowed 200 wraps of cocaine weighing 3.46kg while attempting to board a flight from Abuja to Paris, France.

The suspects, Aliocus Godian Odife and Sam Blackborn, were arrested on Wednesday, 28 October, during passenger clearance for an Air France flight at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.

The NDLEA spokesperson, Femi Babafemi, said in a statement on Sunday that a body scan revealed foreign objects in the stomachs of the two men, who were travelling on flight AF 832.

Mr Odife, who works in a factory in France, had arrived in Nigeria on 21 October for a short holiday. According to NDLEA, he admitted swallowing 110 wraps of cocaine, which he later excreted under observation. The wraps weighed 1.901 kg, the NDLEA said.

His co-traveller, Mr Blackborn, was also found to have swallowed cocaine. The NDLEA said he admitted ingesting 90 wraps, weighing 1.559kg, which he subsequently excreted.

The NDLEA stated that laboratory tests confirmed that all 200 wraps recovered from the men contained cocaine.

The arrest brings back to mind a similar incident in May 2024, when the agency arrested a 48-year-old businessman at the Abuja airport as he prepared to board a flight to Paris. A body scan revealed that he had swallowed 111 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.603 kilogrammes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In January 2025, another businessman arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, underwent surgery after some of the 81 cocaine pellets he had swallowed became stuck in his stomach.

The latest arrests were part of a series of operations in which the NDLEA seized drugs and arrested suspects in several states.

In Lagos, operatives intercepted two vehicles on Sunday, 25 October, following intelligence about the movement of skunk, a potent strain of cannabis, from Lagos Island to the mainland.

They recovered 537kg of the substance from a white Volkswagen LT 28 bus along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja. Another team intercepted a brown J5 bus along the Gbagada-Oshodi Expressway the same day and seized 439 kilogrammes.

In Oyo State, two men, Oguntona Nasiru, 46, and Soji Balogun, 47, were arrested on Thursday, 29 October, while allegedly loading 554 kilogrammes of skunk into a Volvo truck along Idere Road, Igboora.

The operation followed an earlier seizure of 309.5kg of cannabis, popularly known as Ghanaian Loud, allegedly linked to a drug dealer identified as Omo Oba, who escaped arrest on 25 October.

In Kano State, operatives raided a location in the Tsamiya area of Gezawa on Monday, 26 October, recovering 247,500 tablets of diazepam weighing 57.7 kilogrammes and 100,000 tablets of Exol-5 weighing 38.7kg.

Two days later, officers arrested Ziya’ulhaq Abdullahi, 35, and Garba Muhammed, 52, in the Dorayi area with 19,250 tablets of tramadol 225mg.

In Kaduna State, NDLEA operatives arrested a woman, Aisha Isah, with 266 rounds of live AK-47 ammunition at a toll gate along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway.

Another suspect, Ifeanyi Egwolonwu, 68, was arrested at Gwargwaje, Zaria, along the Zaria-Kano Expressway, with 2,770 ampoules of pentazocine injection, 100 ampoules of diazepam injection, 11,000 tablets of diazepam and 4,500 tablets of Exol-5.

In a separate raid in the Tashan Banke area, officers arrested seven suspects, including Faisal Adamu, and recovered 178.85 kilogrammes of cannabis, alongside quantities of diazepam, tramadol, Exol-5 and pregabalin.

In Ondo State, operatives raided cannabis farms in Ijare Forest on Sunday, 25 October, arresting four suspects, including Bassey Okon, 24; Abraham Edet, 20; and Oto Udo, 24. They recovered 16 bags of processed cannabis weighing 180kg.

In Edo State, NDLEA operatives, working with soldiers, raided Eko Camp in Ilushi, Esan South-East Local Government Area, on Wednesday, 28 October. They destroyed a cannabis plantation covering 1.646 hectares, with an estimated yield of 4,115.53kg.

A 50-year-old woman, Christiana Uboi, was arrested at the camp with 301kg of processed cannabis. Officers also recovered another 176 kilogrammes during the operation.

In Sokoto State, operatives of the NDLEA Zone 7 Command arrested a 68-year-old man, Ibrahim Ayuba, with 236.6 kilogrammes of skunk on Saturday, 31 October.

The agency said its commands also held drug awareness campaigns in schools, places of worship, workplaces and communities under its War Against Drug Abuse initiative.

Among the schools visited were Obawole Grammar School II in Ojodu, Lagos; Nsukka High School in Enugu State; Government Technical College, Dorayi Babba Rijiyar Zaki, in Kano State; and Ajagbe Comprehensive High School in Iperu, Ogun State.

The NDLEA chairman, Buba Marwa, commended the officers involved in the operations, particularly those who arrested the two cocaine couriers in Abuja.

He warned Nigerians living abroad against using their foreign residence as cover for drug trafficking, saying officers at the country’s entry and exit points remained vigilant.

Mr Marwa urged NDLEA personnel to sustain their operations against drug trafficking and continue public awareness campaigns to discourage drug use.

Between 2021 and 2025, the agency arrested 77,792 suspected drug offenders, secured 14,225 convictions and seized more than 14.8 million kilogrammes of illicit drugs, according to figures released by the NDLEA.

World.title: FG launches USSD service to help Nigerians access loans without internet [How to apply]
World.content:
The Federal Government has launched a new USSD-based credit service, SPARK, designed to help Nigerians access loans and build formal credit histories using basic mobile phones.

The product, introduced by the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP), targets Nigerians, particularly first-time borrowers who have limited or no credit history.

Interested Nigerians can dial *347*333# on their mobile phones to access the service without requiring a smartphone or internet connection.

According to CREDICORP, SPARK is designed to simplify access to consumer credit while helping beneficiaries establish repayment records that could improve their credit profiles and open up further financial opportunities.

“By establishing repayment records through responsible borrowing, beneficiaries can progressively improve their credit profiles and create pathways to greater financial opportunities,” the corporation said.

It added that the product is expected to become more widely available to Nigerians before the end of 2026.

Why FG introduced SPARK

The product was unveiled at CREDICORP’s ‘CREDICORP for All’ showcase in Aba, Abia State, where the corporation highlighted affordable credit opportunities for more than 1,000 residents.

The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit could support businesses and improve livelihoods.

Activities included credit-access demonstrations for market women and traders, presentations on the YouthCred initiative for young Nigerians, and the showcasing of credit-backed tricycles for transport operators.

The event also featured locally assembled tricycles made available on credit through CREDICORP’s Securing Consumer Access for Local Enterprises (S.C.A.L.E.) initiative.

CREDICORP Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Uzoma Nwagba, said the initiative was designed to make consumer credit accessible beyond traditional financial institutions.

“Consumer credit should not be a privilege reserved for a few. It should be an opportunity available to every working Nigerian,” he said.

He added, “Today in Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, we are demonstrating what that means in practical terms: credit for market women, a financial head start for young people, productive assets for transport operators, and with SPARK, a simple way for Nigerians to begin building their credit histories. This is how we make credit work for the people.”

Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, chief principal to Abia State Governor Alex Otti, said the state government was creating an environment where responsible consumer credit and enterprise could thrive.

“Under Governor Alex Otti’s leadership, Abia State is putting the conditions in place for businesses to grow, investments to flourish and responsible credit to reach more of our people,” Mba-Uzoukwu said, representing the governor at the event.

“By strengthening the enabling environment for enterprise, we are making it easier for initiatives such as CREDICORP to support traders, young people and hardworking families across the state.”

Similarly, Armstrong Ume Takang, Managing Director of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI) and a CREDICORP board member, said the showcase demonstrated how Federal Government policies could translate into economic opportunities for Nigerians.

“Through CREDICORP, we are seeing how well-structured public investment can stimulate enterprise, support local manufacturers and deliver measurable economic impact directly to citizens,” Takang said.

CREDICORP said it had facilitated more than N53.5bn in consumer credit for over 351,000 Nigerians since commencing operations, with women accounting for approximately 59 per cent of beneficiaries.

World.title: FBI says North Korea behind $6 billion crypto theft from Binance
World.content:
Binance said Sunday that it had resumed withdrawals after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for.

Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack, which is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist, caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday.

The company has offered reassurances it will cover the losses from the attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of what was stolen.

Binance suspended user withdrawals after the attack but said they would be resumed in phases, the first of which began on Sunday.

“First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals,” the exchange posted on X .

The US law enforcement agency accused North Korea of being behind the hack in a statement on Saturday, confirming earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a Pyongyang-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was responsible.

TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year.

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the statement said.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralized finance and instant swap services.

It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.”

US President Donald Trump cast doubt on the North Korea’s involvement in the hack.

“I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida late Saturday.

The president often reflects with pride on summits he held with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his first term.

Binance has said that it was preparing to gradually resume withdrawals, starting at between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday.

“We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” it said.

– ‘Cover the financial impact’ –

Binance said Saturday it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack.

“Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X.

It said it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of the stolen funds, while the remaining 10 percent of tokens are “less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts.”

The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

Bitcoin plunged nearly five percent after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly six percent and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 percent.

The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea — which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programs — to find illicit means to capture revenue.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for “The Interview,” a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
