World.title: PDP, NDC members defect to APC as ‘Tinubu Must Stay’ spreads to Jigawa
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Some members of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP and the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC have defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress APC in Jigawa State.

They announced their defection in Garun Gabas Ward of Malam Madori Local Government Area at the inauguration of a grassroots campaign office for President Bola Tinubu, led by the Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi.

Abdullahi and the Malam Madori APC leadership received the defectors who credited their decision to what they described as development interventions and improvements in their communities.

They also singled out projects facilitated through NITDA, saying these had deepened their confidence in the administration’s development agenda.

The event which was organised by the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly called the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, saw the llarge crowd of APC chieftains, community leaders, women, youths and other supporters chanting “Tinubu Must Stay” along the streets.

Abdullahi, who is Chairman of the TMS Board of Trustees and National Coordinator, said the movement was taking its message to the grassroots ahead of the 2027 general elections and Tinubu’s anticipated re-election bid.

“The essence of creating the TMS Movement is to go down to the grassroots level to enlighten citizens on President Tinubu’s reforms. He made it clear when he assumed office that economic diversification and inclusivity in attaining national prosperity are paramount to his reform agenda,” he said.

He said the administration’s interventions in education, agriculture, food security, national security, digital literacy and healthcare were designed to stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods.

Abdullahi cited South Korea, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Malaysia as countries whose experience showed the importance of sustained economic reforms and policy continuity. According to him, Nigeria needs consistent implementation of development policies to compete favourably with emerging economies.

“On this note, I implore the people to come out en masse and ensure a landslide victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027,” he told the gathering.

The TMS National Coordinator also announced plans to empower another 200 women in Garun Gabas Ward. He said this would follow an earlier programme in Hadejia, where beneficiaries received financial assistance, sewing machines, bakery equipment, agricultural inputs and other support for small businesses.

He said the movement would keep prioritising women, youths, children and persons with disabilities through economic empowerment, educational assistance and community development.

The APC Chairman in Malam Madori Local Government Area, Alhaji Tanko Ahmad, commended Abdullahi for facilitating digital infrastructure projects that have widened educational opportunities for young people.

He highlighted the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Development Centre at Government Secondary School, Garun Gabas, which he described as a significant boost to digital literacy.

Ahmad pledged continued support for the TMS initiative and assured that party structures in the area would intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections.

The TMS Convener in Garun Gabas, Engineer Hashim Suleiman, described the turnout as evidence of growing grassroots acceptance of the movement.

He expressed confidence in the administration’s economic direction, citing developments in the financial and petroleum sectors as signs of improving prospects for investment and growth. He urged beneficiaries of the empowerment programmes to use the assistance productively to build sustainable businesses.

“As you know, the movement started some weeks ago. We started from the UK, launched it in Abuja, and now we are here at the community ward level. This is just the beginning, as more grassroots engagements are expected,” he said.

END

World.title: Nigeria woos Russian investors, seeks local currency trade settlement at Moscow summit
World.content:
‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye

‎By Boluwaji Obahopo

‎

‎Nigeria has called for a shift in its relations with Russia from political commitments to practical economic cooperation, urging Russian investors to explore opportunities in the country’s energy, solid minerals, agriculture, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and digital sectors.

‎

‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call while delivering Nigeria’s statement at the Third Russia-Africa Summit at the Grand Kremlin Palace, where he also advocated stronger trade and financial arrangements, including independent local currency settlement mechanisms between both countries.

‎

‎Enikanolaiye, who led Nigeria’s delegation to the summit, said the future of Africa- Russia relations must be measured by tangible economic outcomes, stressing the need to translate longstanding diplomatic ties into investments, technology transfer and development partnerships.

‎

‎He said Nigeria was particularly interested in strengthening cross-border payment arrangements with Russia through mutually agreed systems, alongside improved banking channels and financial infrastructure to facilitate trade and investment.

‎

‎The minister, who conveyed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s greetings to Russian President Vladimir Putin and the African Union Chairman, President Evariste Ndayishimiye of Burundi, said the private sector must play a greater role in driving the partnership.

‎

‎He urged Russia to collaborate with African countries on commercially viable infrastructure projects covering railways, ports, energy, telecommunications, transport and logistics, noting that such investments would strengthen regional connectivity and support the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

‎

‎On the digital economy, Enikanolaiye warned against Africa becoming merely a consumer of imported technology, calling for expanded cooperation in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, software development, digital infrastructure and joint research.

‎

‎He said such partnerships should prioritise technology transfer, capacity building and the development of indigenous technological capabilities across the continent.

‎

‎The minister also identified agriculture and food security as critical areas for cooperation, urging Russia to support African countries in expanding domestic food production, fertiliser availability, irrigation, mechanisation, agricultural research, storage and agro-processing.

‎

‎According to him, recent disruptions to global supply chains have exposed the vulnerability of food systems, making it imperative for African countries to strengthen domestic production and retain more value from their agricultural resources.

‎

‎On security, Enikanolaiye reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to peace and stability in Africa, identifying terrorism, violent extremism, transnational organised crime, arms trafficking, piracy and cybercrime as threats requiring coordinated regional and international responses.

‎

‎He, however, stressed that such partnerships must be anchored on African ownership and African-led solutions, with external cooperation strengthening existing regional mechanisms, including the African Union and ECOWAS.

‎

‎The minister further reiterated Nigeria’s commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, non-interference and the peaceful settlement of disputes, while calling for reforms of the United Nations Security Council and international financial architecture to guarantee Africa’s rightful representation.

‎

‎On the outcome of the summit, Enikanolaiye said Nigeria supported the adoption of a focused Africa-Russia Action Plan for 2027–2029, with clear priorities, financing arrangements and monitoring mechanisms to ensure that agreements translated into measurable results.

‎

‎He specifically invited Russian businesses to take advantage of Nigeria’s position as Africa’s largest market and a strategic gateway to West Africa and the AfCFTA, highlighting opportunities in energy, including renewable and nuclear technology, solid minerals, agriculture, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, defence and digital services.

‎

‎The minister also said the summit had reinforced the longstanding friendly relations between Nigeria and Russia, recalling Moscow’s historic support for Nigeria’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity dating back to the Soviet era.

‎

‎Speaking at the plenary session, Putin described Russia and Africa as natural allies in building a just multipolar world order, reaffirming his country’s commitment to sovereign equality, expanded diplomatic engagement, security cooperation and greater African representation in global institutions.

‎

‎Similarly, Ndayishimiye stressed that Africa would not exchange one form of subordination for another, insisting that the continent’s international partnerships must respect its independence and development priorities.

‎

‎He said the 2027–2029 Action Plan would provide an opportunity to address infrastructure deficits through technology transfer and skills development, while moving Africa from dependence on external assistance towards greater economic independence.

‎

‎The AU chairman also identified water security as a major priority of the continental body’s 2026 agenda.

‎

‎These was contained in a statement on Sunday by the Minister’s Special Assistant on Media and Public Communication, Mr. Richard Elesho

World.title: Betta Edu courts 500 C’River women, sets 1.5m vote target for Tinubu
World.content:
Former Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Betta Edu, has set a target of 1.5 million votes from Cross River for President Bola Tinubu, come 2027 general elections.

Edu, Co-Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mobilisation Directorate, made the declaration on Sunday in Calabar, during an empowerment programme that benefited about 500 market women, petty traders and artisans.

She said the initiative organised at the instance of the First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, was designed to improve women’s economic livelihood, and strengthen grassroots mobilisation.

She said the beneficiaries received N50,000 each, alongside business and household equipment, including deep freezers, blenders, and toasters.

According to her, the intervention targets petty traders whose businesses are constrained by inadequate capital.

“Some of them are selling trays that have just N5,000 worth of things on them, while some of them have trays with just N10,000 worth of items on them.

“So we are giving these sets of petty traders N50,000 each so that they can expand that their business, build on it, so things can get better for them and their children,” she said.

Edu urged residents of the state to support Tinubu, Gov. Bassey Otu and other APC candidates as the party was banking on grassroots women’s mobilisation to strengthen its electoral fortunes in the state.

She expressed confidence that the state would deliver more than 1.5 million votes for the ruling party, adding that the directorate was establishing support structures for women across the country.

She disclosed that the empowerment programme would be extended to other parts of Cross River, with Abi Local Government Area scheduled to benefit in November or December, while the northern senatorial district would be reached in January.

The former minister also highlighted some Federal Government interventions, including the student loan scheme and free maternal healthcare, as measures aimed at improving the welfare of Nigerians.

As part of the mobilisation activities, she led members of the directorate on a visit to the General Hospital, Calabar, where they interacted with patients, pregnant women and children receiving treatment and offered financial and emotional support.

She said the hospital outreach was undertaken at the instance of the First Lady ahead of the APC rally scheduled to hold in Calabar on Monday.

Edu also cited subsidised dialysis services and free maternal healthcare as interventions aimed at improving healthcare access and reducing maternal mortality.

One of the beneficiaries, Esther Bassey, a widow from Odukpani Local Government Area, expressed appreciation for the support, saying previous empowerment programmes had helped her cater for her three children.

Bassey pledged her support for the APC in 2027, saying she and her family would vote for the party

World.title: ‎2027: Promote peace, policies, not personal attacks – PDP tells supporters
World.content:
PDP FLAGS

By Muhammad Inuwa Dutse

‎

‎The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Jigawa State has urged its social media supporters to promote peaceful political engagement, issue-based campaigns and policy discussions rather than engage in insults and personal attacks ahead of the 2027 general elections.

‎

‎The party’s governorship candidate, Mustapha Sule Lamido, made the call during a meeting with PDP social media users and political commentators in the state.

‎

‎Lamido urged the supporters to use their platforms responsibly by promoting the party’s programmes, policies and candidates through constructive engagement.

‎

‎He stressed that political campaigns should be driven by ideas and policies capable of winning public confidence, rather than abusive language and personal attacks.

‎

‎”Political campaigns should focus on issues, policies and programmes that can convince the electorate, not insults or attacks on individuals,” Lamido said.

‎

‎According to him, the meeting was organised to sensitise youths on the importance of responsible political communication and their role in promoting the party ahead of the 2027 elections.

‎

‎He further disclosed that the party had completed arrangements to commence its campaign activities across Jigawa State.

‎

‎Lamido reaffirmed the PDP’s commitment to conducting peaceful and orderly campaign tours across the state, without violence or unnecessary provocation.

‎

‎”We are committed to peaceful campaigns across Jigawa State, and we urge our supporters to avoid anything that could create tension or disrupt public peace,” he said.

‎

‎The governorship candidate also expressed appreciation to the people of Jigawa State for their continued support for the PDP, urging them to sustain their confidence in the party.

World.title: Delta HOSTCOM clarifies position on DESOPADEC publication
World.content:
….Urges workers, management to await court ruling on 30% payment dispute

By Chiamaka Ekwuwe

WARRI — The Delta State chapter of the Host Communities of Nigeria Producing Oil and Gas (HOSTCOM) has clarified that a publication criticising Governor Sheriff Oborevwori over the operations and funding of the Delta State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (DESOPADEC) does not represent its official position.

In a statement signed by its Chairman, Chief Comrade Sunday Ndidi Enujeke, and Secretary, High Comrade Joseph Lamienghan, the organisation said it had not adopted or endorsed the publication titled, “Oborevwori’s DESOPADEC Betrayal: Oil Communities Starved While Derivation Billions Vanish,” authored by Swill Mavua.

The publication had expressed concerns about DESOPADEC’s funding and the development of oil-producing communities, while urging residents to vote against Oborevwori and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections.

However, Delta HOSTCOM said the views and political recommendations contained in the article should be regarded as those of its author and not attributed to the state chapter.

The organisation explained that its recognised leadership comprised Enujeke as chairman and Lamienghan as secretary, adding that official positions issued in its name should reflect the decisions of its leadership.

It urged media organisations, government institutions, political parties, oil and gas industry stakeholders, community leaders and the public to take note of its clarification.

DESOPADEC payment dispute

On the dispute concerning the 30 per cent payment to DESOPADEC workers, the organisation appealed to the workers and management to maintain peace and allow the court to determine the matter.

It stressed the importance of respecting the judicial process while awaiting the final ruling.

Delta HOSTCOM also expressed support for the objectives of Governor Oborevwori’s MORE Agenda, which stands for Meaningful Development, Opportunities for All, Realistic Reforms and Enhanced Peace and Security.

The organisation said sustained engagement between the state government and host communities was important to addressing developmental challenges, improving living conditions and promoting peace in oil-producing areas.

It added, however, that its position on the agenda should not be interpreted as an endorsement of every government policy or a dismissal of concerns relating to DESOPADEC’s statutory responsibilities.

According to the statement, issues concerning the commission’s funding, project execution, statutory obligations and workers’ welfare require constructive engagement with relevant authorities.

It said environmental justice, infrastructure development, transparency, accountability and improved welfare remained important to the development of oil-producing communities.

HOSTCOM outlines endorsement process

The organisation said it would continue to engage its constituent communities through town hall meetings before taking decisions on political endorsements.

It explained that such consultations would provide an opportunity for members to discuss issues affecting their communities and collectively determine their position.

The leadership said: “HOSTCOM does not involve itself in campaigns. What we do is organise town hall meetings, which will kick-start soon. At the grand finale, that is when we normally endorse credible candidates, who must be delivered by the oil-producing communities across the 21 local government areas.”

Delta HOSTCOM called for unity among oil-producing communities and reiterated its commitment to engaging government authorities and other stakeholders on matters affecting their welfare.

It maintained that the disputed publication was not an official statement or political position of the Delta State chapter.

World.title: Nigerians, other foreign graduates to get shorter UK work visa from 2027
World.content:
The United Kingdom, UK has announced plans to retain its two-year post-study work visa for international students graduating from selected universities, partially reversing an earlier decision to reduce the duration of the scheme.

Under the revised policy, graduates of universities with strong immigration compliance records and employment outcomes will continue to qualify for the two-year Graduate visa, while other international graduates will receive 18 months from January 2027.

The UK government disclosed the change in its 2026 Budget, although it has yet to publish the list of qualifying universities or explain how institutions will be assessed.

The policy introduces a two-tier system in which the university attended by an international student could determine how long they can remain in Britain after completing their studies.

“The government will also increase the duration of the Graduate visa to two years for graduates from high compliance universities where there are strong labour market outcomes,” the Budget document said.

The change comes after the government announced plans to reduce the standard Graduate visa from two years to 18 months for bachelor’s and master’s degree holders, effective January 1, 2027. Doctoral graduates will continue to qualify for three years.

The development could affect thousands of African students, particularly Nigerians, who constitute a significant proportion of Britain’s international student population and rely on post-study employment opportunities to gain work experience and recover the cost of their education.

Nigeria was the UK’s third-largest source of sponsored international students in the year ending June 2026, with 26,060 sponsored study visas issued to Nigerian main applicants, behind China and India.

Nigerian nationals also recorded 20,604 approvals under the Graduate route during the period, making them the third-largest nationality group to benefit from the scheme.

The Graduate visa allows eligible international students to work or search for employment in Britain without requiring immediate employer sponsorship. However, the visa cannot be extended, and graduates seeking to remain longer must switch to another

eligible immigration route, such as the Skilled Worker visa.

Students graduating before the end of 2026 can still apply for the existing two-year Graduate visa, while the reduced 18-month duration will apply to applications submitted from January 1, 2027.

hile maintaining opportunities for international graduates and professionals considered valuable to the country’s labour market.

Vanguard News

World.title: Adesina, Sanusi, Otti, Others to Lead African Prosperity Talks in Abuja
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Dr Akinwumi Adesina; Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II; and Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, are among prominent African leaders expected in Abuja on November 3 to explore practical strategies for building a prosperous, resilient and inclusive African economy.

The second edition of the Oxford Global Think Tank (OGTT) Leadership Conference will bring together influential figures from government, business, technology, finance and civil society to examine leadership choices, institutional reforms, technological innovations and investment opportunities needed to translate Africa’s enormous potential into sustainable economic prosperity.

Adesina, who is also Executive Chairman of the Global Africa Investment Summit, will deliver the keynote address, while Sanusi and Founder of ANAP Foundation, Atedo Peterside, will co-chair the conference.

The conference, themed ‘Leadership for a Prosperous Future,’ is expected to address critical challenges confronting the continent, including the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), changing global power dynamics, demographic shifts and evolving economic realities.

Other prominent personalities expected include Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani; Minister of Women Affairs, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim; Executive Vice-President of Afreximbank, Dr Kanayo Awani; Director-General of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Dr Emomotimi Agama; and Chief Executive Officer of Flutterwave, Gbenga Agboola.

A statement by the Conference Media Adviser, Comrade Chris Isiguzo, said discussions would centre on three pillars — resilience, innovation and dynamism — with participants exploring ways to strengthen African institutions, mobilise capital, improve productivity and expand economic opportunities.

A special highlight will be the conference’s focus on AI, featuring the launch of an AI report and an AI Virtual Centre, as well as an exhibition showcasing emerging technologies and their potential to transform Africa’s development.

The organisers said the gathering would move beyond broad aspirations to identify practical actions and partnerships capable of strengthening institutions, deepening productive capacity and promoting inclusive economic growth.

“Africa’s future will be shaped by the quality of leadership and the choices its institutions and leaders make today,” the organisers said.

The conference, hosted by the Oxford Global Think Tank, founded by Ms Arunma Oteh, is slated to hold at the Congress Hall, Transcorp Hilton Hotel, Abuja, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., followed by a cocktail reception.

The Oxford Global Think Tank is an independent, non-governmental and non-partisan organisation that promotes research and dialogue on development and supports public and private sector leaders in exploring policy ideas and strengthening institutions.

World.title: Tinubu’s Trans-Sahara Superhighway’ll Transform Northern Economy, Strengthen Security, Says Yilwatda
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the ongoing reconstruction of the Akwanga-Jos section of the Trans-Sahara Superhighway as a landmark infrastructure project that will transform economic activities, improve security and deepen national integration across Nigeria.

Yilwatda stated this during an inspection tour of the project, where he expressed satisfaction with the pace of work and commended the commitment of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration to delivering critical road infrastructure across the country.

The APC national chairman said the project represented one of the most significant federal investments in the region in decades, noting that the corridor had suffered years of neglect despite its strategic importance to socio-economic development in the North-central and North-east regions.

According to him, the reconstruction forms part of the larger Trans-Sahara Superhighway corridor stretching from Calabar through Ebonyi, Enugu, Benue, Abuja and Jos, before extending to Gombe, Biu and Maiduguri, linking several geopolitical zones and creating a seamless transport network across the country.

He said the highway, which spans more than 1,400 kilometres, would serve as a catalyst for trade, investment and national cohesion by connecting communities, markets and businesses across the South-south, South-east, North-central and North-east regions.

Yilwatda noted that the Akwanga-Jos road, originally constructed around 1972, had not witnessed major rehabilitation for more than five decades, with successive interventions limited largely to palliative repairs and patchwork.

“For over five decades, since the days of the late Joseph Gomwalk around 1972, this corridor witnessed only piecemeal patching. Communities along the Nasarawa-Plateau axis rarely saw federal capital projects running into even N10 billion. Today, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has committed hundreds of billions of naira to build an infrastructure asset designed to endure for over a century,” he said.

He explained that the project was being executed using rigid concrete pavement technology to ensure durability and reduce maintenance requirements, adding that the road was designed to serve future generations.

“We are targeting a lifespan of over 100 years before there will be a need to consider maintaining or repairing it again. That is how you build a lasting legacy,” he stated.

The APC chairman further disclosed that the highway would incorporate modern security architecture, including intelligent surveillance systems, continuous lighting, dedicated police outposts and emergency trauma centres aimed at safeguarding commuters and communities along the route.

According to him, the 24-hour surveillance cameras would assist security agencies in monitoring vehicular movements, tracking criminal activities and ensuring rapid response to emergencies.

“This is not just a road; this is connecting communities. This is connecting customers, connecting markets, connecting people and improving security,” he said.

Yilwatda maintained that the project embodied the ideals of President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, adding that visible infrastructure development across the country was evidence that the administration was translating campaign promises into tangible results.

He also described the administration’s infrastructure drive as a major political asset for the ruling APC ahead of the 2027 general election, arguing that Nigerians would ultimately judge the government by projects delivered and impacts felt in their daily lives.

Earlier, the project’s Equipment Coordinator and Public Relations Officer, Mr. James Baba, said construction activities had intensified following the mobilisation of heavy equipment to the Jos axis in line with directives from the Federal Ministry of Works.

Baba disclosed that work was progressing simultaneously from both the Akwanga and Jos ends of the highway, while test-running of the rigid concrete pavement had already commenced.

According to him, about 400 metres of rigid pavement have so far been completed, with contractors targeting 10 kilometres of earthwork before Christmas and an additional 30 kilometres expected to be delivered next year.

“Our target this year is to cover about 10 kilometres of earthwork before Christmas,” he said, expressing confidence that the project would be executed in line with approved specifications and the highest quality standards.

He explained that the adoption of cement concrete pavement in place of conventional asphalt followed the Federal Ministry of Works’ specifications and was intended to guarantee long-term durability of the highway.

World.title: VivaJets Steps Up Francophone Africa Expansion, Grows Fleet to Eight
World.content:
Pan-African business aviation firm, VivaJets, has restated its expansion drive into Francophone Africa as it grows its fleet and strengthens connectivity for businesses, investors and institutions across the continent.

The company was a partner and participant at the fifth UK-West and Central Francophone Africa Trade and Investment Forum (WCAF V) that held in Conakry, Guinea in October.

Themed ‘From Cooperation to Transformation: Building the Future of Development in Africa,’ WCAF V brought together government representatives, institutional stakeholders, businesses and international partners to explore trade, investment and economic opportunities across Francophone West and Central Africa.

The engagement followed VivaJets’ recent participation at the Africa Energy Week (AEW) in Cape Town, where it met stakeholders across the continent’s energy sector.

Chief Executive Officer of VivaJets, Erika Achum, said Francophone Africa presents a key opportunity to deepen regional connectivity.

“Francophone Africa represents an important opportunity to deepen regional connectivity and support the movement of people, ideas and investment across the continent,” Achum said.

“Our participation at WCAF V was about building meaningful relationships with government and institutional stakeholders, as well as international partners who share a commitment to Africa’s economic development. As VivaJets continues to grow, we want to be a trusted aviation partner to the businesses and institutions helping shape the continent’s future,” she added.

VivaJets’ participation at the forum comes amid rapid growth for the company. Just over a year after receiving its Air Operator Certificate (AOC), the firm has expanded its fleet to eight aircraft.

The company has also secured two rounds of credit investment from London-based TLG Capital to support its expansion and advance its mission of improving connectivity through private aviation.

Chief Operating Officer of VivaJets, Tejumade Salami, said the expansion goes beyond fleet size.

“Our expansion is about more than growing the number of aircraft in our fleet. It is about building the operational strength, service capability and partnerships needed to connect businesses and people across diverse African markets.

“Our participation at WCAF V gives us an opportunity to listen to stakeholders, understand the realities of the region and explore how VivaJets can support their connectivity needs as our operations continue to scale,” Salami stated.

Head of Growth and Innovation at VivaJets, Basil Agbor, said the forum provided a platform to understand regional markets and build partnerships.

“Expanding into new markets starts with understanding the people, businesses and institutions that operate within them. WCAF V created an important space for those conversations, allowing us to engage with stakeholders who are actively shaping investment and development across Francophone Africa.

“Our focus is on translating these relationships into practical opportunities for connectivity, collaboration and long-term value. We believe innovation in African aviation must be grounded in a clear understanding of the markets we serve and the challenges our clients need us to solve,” Agbor said.

World.title: C’ River: We’ve Reduced Domestic Debt by N70bn, Governor Otu
World.content:
‎* IGR hit N46.3bn in 2024

‎Cross River State Governor, Senator Bassey Otu, Saturday, presented his administration’s record of debt reduction, asset recovery, infrastructure renewal and public service reforms as evidence of progress under the People First Agenda, declaring that a second term would propel the state from economic recovery to wealth creation and shared prosperity.

‎

‎Otu made the declaration in Calabar, while inaugurating the Cross River State All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for the 2027 general election.

He charged party leaders and campaign officials to take the administration’s achievements to the electorate, insisting that continuity was essential to consolidating the foundations already laid for sustainable development.

‎

‎Reflecting on the circumstances surrounding his assumption of office in May 2023, the governor recalled that the state was grappling with insecurity, a demoralised public service and underutilised public assets.

“We did not promise all things in one year, but we covenanted to stop the bleeding, clear the ground, recover the losses and restore abandonments,” he said, describing the administration’s first phase as one of recovery and restoration.

‎

‎On fiscal management, Otu disclosed that his government had reduced the inherited domestic debt of more than N204 billion by over N70 billion without taking fresh loans, bringing the outstanding debt to approximately N132.3 billion as of March 2026.

He also disclosed that internally generated revenue increased from N21.1 billion in 2022 to N46.3 billion in 2024.

“Every debt retired is freedom for our children and house-cleaning for fresh fiscal air,” he said, adding that improved revenue and financial discipline would strengthen investment in public services.

‎

‎The governor identified the recovery of strategic public assets as another major achievement, citing the reclamation of Tinapa from the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON), the recovery of nearly N1 billion from Etung Cocoa Estates and other public assets, and ongoing efforts to reclaim the state’s oil wells and secure its interests in the Bakassi axis and proposed Deep Seaport.

He also highlighted improvements in security, the lifting of the employment embargo, the restoration of more than 3,000 local government workers to the payroll and the payment of the first tranche of gratuities after nearly two decades. “The government is not just concrete — it is the people,” he said.

‎

‎On infrastructure and economic revitalisation, Otu cited the reconstruction of the Obudu Cargo Airport runway, the revival of the Teachers Continuous Training Institute in Biase, the transformation of Akamkpa College into the University of Entrepreneurship and the concessioning of the Garment Factory and Obudu Ranch through public-private partnerships.

He also pointed to road construction and rehabilitation, increased and expanded Cally Air fleet and operations, as well as the growing economic impact of Carnival Calabar. “Continuity is an attitude of maturity,” he said, arguing that completing inherited projects and sustaining viable investments were critical to the state’s progress.

‎

‎Otu also highlighted agriculture and digital transformation as key drivers of future growth, noting investments in cocoa, rice, potatoes, palm fruits and cassava to strengthen food security and rural livelihoods.

He said more than 200 kilometres of fibre infrastructure had been deployed across Calabar, over 600 residents had received ICT training, and digital platforms were improving revenue collection and public service delivery.

He further cited Cross River’s selection by the World Bank GovTech Team for its 2026 AI in Governance and Public Administration Bootcamp in Seoul, South Korea, as international recognition of the state’s technological advancement.

‎

‎Outlining his second-term priorities, the governor pledged to turn recovered assets into productive enterprises, complete major infrastructure projects, expand youth and agricultural enterprise programmes, establish industrial parks across the three senatorial districts and improve workers’ welfare.

Urging the campaign council to engage voters across the state’s 18 local government areas and 196 wards with facts and decorum, he said: “You do not change a farmer who has cleared the farm just when it is time to plant. You do not abandon a builder who has laid the foundation when it is time to raise the roof.”

He formally inaugurated the council, declaring that the campaign must be fought not for an individual, but for the future of Cross River and its people.

World.title: ADC Chides Governor Alia Over Performance in Office
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Benue State for the 2027 general elections, Rt. Hon. Herman Hembe, has declared that Governor Hyacinth Alia is no longer electable, calling on the people of Benue State to reject him at the polls. He maintained that the governor has not performed well enough to deserve a second term in office.

Hembe made this declaration in Oju, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area, during the campaign flag-off ceremony for the ADC Benue South Senatorial candidate, Dr. David Olofu.

Addressing thousands of party faithful drawn from all nine local government areas in Zone C, Hembe said that, in all his years of political experience, he had never encountered a governor who could look his people in the eyes and tell them a lie without hesitation.

He expressed concern over what he described as the unfair distribution of the state’s financial resources, alleging that about ₦1.1 trillion accrued to Benue State over the last three years.

According to Hembe, Governor Alia stated that Zone B received ₦317 billion, representing 91 per cent, while Zone A received ₦17 billion (5 per cent) and Zone C received what he described as an insulting ₦8 billion (2 per cent).

Hembe questioned the basis for the alleged disparity in resource allocation, asking why Zone B would receive such a significant share while Zone C was left with so little.

He maintained that an ADC-led government would not practise sectional governance, stressing that development should promote unity, fairness and equal opportunities across the state.

“Even with the allocation said to have gone to Zone C, where can we point to and say that the two per cent has been invested?” he asked.

Hembe further accused Governor Alia of creating political crises rather than providing effective leadership. He alleged that the governor had lost the confidence of members of his own party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), and questioned why the people of Benue State should continue to trust a governor whose party members no longer have confidence in him.

“If his own party members do not trust him, why should the people of Benue State trust him again?” Hembe asked.

He also congratulated ADC candidates from Zone C, expressing confidence in the party’s growing acceptance across the zone and encouraging the candidates to remain committed to their respective campaigns.

Earlier, the ADC State Chairman, Rt. Hon. Samson Okwu, formally presented the party’s flags to candidates contesting various positions in Zone C. He charged them to work diligently towards securing victory for the party at all levels.

Okwu also welcomed thousands of defectors into the ADC and urged them to remain committed to the progress and success of the party.

In his remarks, the ADC Benue South Senatorial candidate, Dr. David Olofu, thanked the people of Zone C for embracing the ADC, describing it as a viable political platform capable of bringing meaningful change to the zone and Benue State at large.

He pledged to serve as the voice of the people and provide the effective representation they had long been denied.

World.title: NCDC Confirms Negative Ebola Tests in 2 Suspected Adamawa Cases
World.content:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) says two suspected Ebola Virus Disease cases identified in Yola, Adamawa, have tested negative following two rounds of laboratory testing.

Dr Jide ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‍‌‍‍‍‌​⁠⁠‌​Idris, NCDC Director-General, disclosed this in a statement on Saturday, saying the agency was working with the Adamawa Government to investigate the reported cases.

Idris said the report was received by the Adamawa Public Health Emergency Operations Centre in the early hours of Oct. 30, following the identification of two individuals with symptoms suggestive of Ebola.

He explained that the individuals were immediately isolated, while samples were collected and appropriate public health measures initiated to determine the cause of their illnesses.

The NCDC director-general said laboratory results from two rounds of testing were negative for Ebola, confirming that there was currently no laboratory-confirmed case in Adamawa.

He commended the Adamawa Commissioner for Health and his team for their proactive response, assuring that the NCDC would continue to provide technical support to strengthen the state’s response operations.

Idris also clarified that the previously confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory, remained Nigeria’s only laboratory-confirmed Ebola case.

He urged Nigerians to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information or speculation, advising the public to rely on official government and public health communication channels.

The NCDC boss described Ebola as a serious infectious disease requiring prompt detection, appropriate clinical management and effective infection prevention and control measures.

He advised anyone experiencing symptoms such as fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding to seek immediate medical attention.

Idris stressed that people experiencing such symptoms, particularly after possible exposure, should inform healthcare workers about relevant travel or contact history.

He also cautioned against self-medication, urging individuals to follow professional medical advice and guidance from public health authorities.

According to him, the NCDC, Adamawa Government and other relevant stakeholders will continue to monitore the situation and provide updates as verified information becomes available.

He reaffirmed the commitment of public health authorities to protecting Nigerians through early detection, evidence-based interventions, transparent communication and coordinated national response efforts. (NAN)

World.title: INEC Forecloses Changing 2027 Election Timetable, Says Polls Can’t Be Shifted
World.content:
*To release final voters’ register December 15*Warns against attacks on officials, corps members

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has ruled out any adjustment to the timetable for the 2027 general election without lawful justification, declaring that the polls must hold as scheduled.

This comes as he warned against attacks on electoral officials, including National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members, during next year’s elections, saying perpetrators would face the full weight of the law.



Speaking yesterday in Port Harcourt, Rivers State capital, during an interactive meeting with INEC staff from the six South-south states to assess the commission’s preparedness for the forthcoming elections, Amupitan maintained that the commission would adhere strictly to its statutory obligations, stressing that the election timetable was fixed and would not be altered without lawful justification.

Amupitan also said the commission was addressing submissions of claims for corrections to the voters’ register ahead of the release of the final voters’ register scheduled for December 15.



“Our statutory timeline is fixed. We will not change anything. The election must be held as scheduled,” he said.

The INEC chairman also announced that Rivers State would receive particular attention in the commission’s preparations, given its position as the state with the highest number of registered voters in the South-south.



According to figures released by the commission, Rivers has 3,736,434 registered voters, followed by Delta with 3,525,988; Edo, 2,865,263; Akwa Ibom, 2,566,198; Cross River, 1,928,978; and Bayelsa, 1,200,691.

The six states have a combined 15,823,550 registered voters.

Amupitan said Rivers’ electoral significance placed additional responsibility on INEC officials to ensure no eligible voter would be denied the opportunity to exercise their franchise.



“With the 3,736,434 registered voters for Rivers State, the state leads the South-south. As a result, the commission will pay closer attention to what happens in Rivers State. It is your duty to ensure that no voter is disenfranchised because of operational failures,” he said.

On the voters’ register, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had published the register online and at designated locations for public scrutiny, adding that the commission had received more than 5,000 claims for corrections, including names and dates of birth, as well as over 600 objections.



He said the commission was addressing the submissions ahead of the release of the final voters’ register scheduled for December 15.

The INEC chairman explained that although he had initially considered revalidating the entire voters’ register after assuming office, he abandoned the proposal because he feared the exercise would come too close to the general election.



Amupitan expressed confidence in INEC’s capacity to deliver peaceful, transparent and credible elections, citing lessons from recent off-cycle governorship elections, particularly the Osun State governorship poll.

He described the Osun election as encouraging, noting that it recorded the highest voter turnout in the history of off-cycle elections in the state and earned positive assessments despite earlier security concerns.



“Osun State elections gave us the confidence that we can achieve this despite the noise. It is good that we had a series of those elections before the general elections because we learn lessons from every election,” he said.

He added that the commission would build on the experiences gained from the off-cycle elections to strengthen its preparations for 2027.

“We will conduct elections that will move the nation forward and not an election that will bring it down,” he assured.



On security, Amupitan said INEC was collaborating with relevant security agencies, including the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services (DSS), to guarantee the safety of voters, electoral personnel, ad hoc staff and election materials.

He stressed that Nigerians must be able to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and exercise their franchise without fear of intimidation or violence.



“We want every part of Nigeria to be calm during the elections so that people can come out to vote. We will not tell them to take their PVCs and then will not guarantee their safety,” he said.

The INEC chairman also dismissed suggestions that Artificial Intelligence (AI) or computer algorithms could determine the outcome of the 2027 elections, insisting that Nigerian voters would remain in charge of electoral decisions.



“It is the people of Nigeria that will decide the outcome of the elections and not AI or any algorithms,” he declared.

He, however, acknowledged the growing cybersecurity threats associated with emerging technologies, saying the commission was exploring ways to deploy technology to better protect its digital infrastructure against possible attacks.



Amupitan urged INEC personnel across the South-South to remain professional and committed, emphasising that the credibility of the 2027 elections would ultimately depend on the conduct of officials at polling units and other field locations.

He warned against attacks on electoral officials, including NYSC members, during next year’s elections, stressing that perpetrators will face the full weight of the law.



Amupitan said the commission was strengthening its operational plans to ensure the safety of election personnel, voters and materials, particularly in areas exposed to security threats.

“Anyone who threatens or harms INEC officials, including National Youth Service Corps members deployed for election duties, will face the full weight of the law,” he warned.



The INEC chairman also cautioned electoral officers against partisanship, negligence, absenteeism and financial misconduct, stressing that such violations would attract disciplinary action.

Amupitan said the readiness assessment was designed to identify operational weaknesses and address logistical challenges before the elections.

World.title: Two New Suspected Ebola Cases in North East Test Negative, Says NCDC
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

Barely five days after the first imported case of Ebola virus disease was evacuated to Switzerland, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has confirmed that two new suspected cases of the disease tested negative in the North East state of Adamawa.

The NCDC had earlier yesterday reported that two suspected cases were identified in the North-east, and that they were isolated, with contact identification and laboratory testing ongoing.



However, in an update released last night, NCDC Director-General, Dr. Jide Idris, said the cases, which were identified in Yola, Adamawa State, had returned negative after two rounds of testing.

“Samples were collected for laboratory testing to establish the cause of the illness. Fortunately, the samples turned out negative for EBV after two rounds of testing,” Idris said.



He clarified that there was no laboratory-confirmed EVD case in Adamawa State, adding that the index case previously confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) remained the only confirmed case in Nigeria.

While commending the Adamawa State Government for its proactive response, Idris urged the public to remain calm, avoid sharing unverified information and continue to practise good hand hygiene and enhanced sanitation.



He assured that NCDC would continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as verified information becomes available.

NCDC had initially said it identified two suspected cases of the disease in the North-east geopolitical zone.

The agency, which did not disclose the particular state, added that laboratory testing was being conducted to determine whether the individuals had contracted the disease.



“Two suspected cases of Ebola disease have been identified in Nigeria’s North-east region. Both individuals have been isolated, contact identification and listing are ongoing, and laboratory testing is being conducted.

“Being classified as suspected cases does not mean they are confirmed Ebola cases; confirmation is subject to laboratory results,” the statement read.



The NCDC, however, cautioned that being classified as suspected cases did not mean the individuals had tested positive for Ebola, stressing that confirmation would depend on laboratory results.

The agency urged Nigerians to maintain good hand hygiene, practise enhanced sanitation, and follow guidance from public health authorities.



It said it would provide further updates as verified information became available.

The development came less than two weeks after the federal government confirmed Nigeria’s first imported case of the virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, on October 20, 2026.

The patient, a woman who had travelled from Uganda to Nigeria, tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain and was subsequently isolated and treated by Nigerian health workers.



Announcing the first case of the disease, the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Ali Pate, had stated that the infected woman had travelled to Nigeria from Uganda and developed symptoms on October 7 before seeking medical attention at a private hospital in Abuja on October 11.



After confirmation, health authorities initially identified 44 contacts of the patient, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers, and people who might have travelled with her.

The number later rose to 53, and health authorities placed the contacts under surveillance.

The patient was subsequently evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 alongside her husband, who had remained asymptomatic.



The World Health Organisation (WHO) said Nigeria would need to complete a 42-day monitoring period before it could be declared free of Ebola, comprising 21 days of monitoring for identified contacts and another 21 days in line with established protocols.

The federal government had announced a payment of N100,000 weekly to each contact of the confirmed case to encourage compliance with quarantine directives and prevent possible community transmission.

World.title: Don’t bother calling SASSA; they’re planning not to answer
World.content:
Will SASSA beneficiaries get help if they call the agency? Image: Pexels

In its annual performance plan, the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has made a shocking revelation.

The revelation?

It wants to stop answering up to 800 000 calls.



SASSA won’t be answering calls anymore

The agency wants to update its systems. Phone calls are the first thing to go.

In its 2026/2027 Annual Report, SASSA outlines its targets to improve customer experience.

To reach that target, it wants to improve the turnaround time for resolving customer enquiries.

Unfortunately, for customers, to “improve turnaround time,” the agency plans to reduce the number of calls it answers.

In 2024-2025, the agency answered 4.8 million calls.

But by March next year, it wants to drop that number to 4.2 million, which means it will answer 600 000 fewer calls.



The plan doesn’t end there.

Every year until 2029, the agency wants to answer fewer calls, until it reaches 4 million calls a year.

The aim is for 70% of customers to complete an after-call survey. Yet it doesn’t mention how many callers should be satisfied with the service they receive.

If their history is an indicator, callers will be dissatisfied.

The agency’s customer experience is getting worse

In 2023-2024, the agency resolved 97% of enquiries in 5 days.

By 2025, that dropped to 94% of enquiries resolved in 5 days.

SASSA also plans to become less efficient at processing Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant applications.

Between 2022 and 2024, the agency processed 100% of SRD grant applications.

Yet it intends to process 95% of applications this year as SRD grant applications rise.

The agency also hasn’t maintained on-time payments for SRD grants. As of June 2026, it had only paid 89% of the grants it approved.

SASSA wants to Go Digital

All of these so-called improvements come down to SASSA’s desire to digitise.

The agency wants to replace customer care workers with AI-powered chatbots.

However, even in its plan, SASSA admits that beneficiaries may not be able to adopt these solutions because they lack digital literacy.

Many SASSA beneficiaries live in rural communities or in homes where there isn’t internet access.

These beneficiaries rely on calling the agency instead of travelling long distances to get help.

But if SASSA doesn’t want to prioritise their calls, how will they get help?

World.title: Sundowns coach says it was a dark night for SA football
World.content:
Sundowns delivered a dazzlying performance to dislodge Orlando Pirates from the top of the league.

However, Cardoso’s post-match reaction centred on what he believed were questionable officiating decisions against Betway Premiership giants.

MAMELODI SUNDOWNS SLAMS OFFICIALS

The Portuguese coach made his frustration clear during his interview with SuperSport TV. He suggested that his team had not received the respect it deserved.



“Today, is a day of a lot of emotions. I will make my best efforts to shut up and not speak too much. I think it’s another dark night for South Africa, but let people think whatever, there’s people that will sleep in a bed for sure,” Cardoso told SuperSport TV.

“Honest people that work hard, even here today you should go look at the penalties that was taken from Sundowns. I don’t want to speak too much, but whoever has conscious today should before go to sleep pray a little bit and think a little bit more together,” he added.

DURBAN CITY PUT TO THE SWORD

On the pitch, Sundowns had enough quality to overcome Eric Tinkler’s Durban City side, with Thabang Matuludi enjoying an outstanding evening.



The full-back scored twice, while Iqraam Rayners and Antonio Van Wyk also found the back of the net to complete a comfortable victory over the Citizens.

“Look, my team deserves everything but the same respect for Durban City today, our boys put the intensity, we profit obvious from freshness as we have a chance to change a lot of players from the previous match.

“Congratulations for both teams, obviously a big result for us, it’s obvious important to have a happy game with goals, congratulations for the fans, for this stadium, the management of this stadium, to have such quality of this pitch.



The result puts Sundowns back at the summit, just one point ahead of Pirates, setting up another potentially tight title battle.

Cardoso believes the way the competition is unfolding could produce a similar finish to last season.

“Look, if the league is played like we saw today, there won’t be a lot of story, we’ll have a league like last year,” Cardoso said.

World.title: WATCH: Jacob Zuma returns to campaign trail after hospitalisation
World.content:
Former President Jacob Zuma has made his first in-person public appearance since being hospitalised in Pietermaritzburg in October.

Zuma attended the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party’s final election rally at Princess Magogo Stadium in KwaMashu on Sunday, 1 November, ahead of the local government elections on Wednesday, 4 November.

JACOB ZUMA RETURNS TO CAMPAIGN TRAIL

Ahead of the rally, the MK Party confirmed that Zuma would attend and deliver the keynote address.



The 84-year-old party leader was admitted to Netcare St Anne’s Hospital in Pietermaritzburg on 6 October after falling ill while addressing a campaign event in uMsinga, northern KwaZulu-Natal.

The party later confirmed that Zuma had been discharged on 17 October after spending 11 days in hospital. According to the party, his medical team had identified fatigue and recommended a period of rest under medical supervision.

His hospitalisation kept him away from the campaign trail during a crucial period for the party as he also missed a mini-rally in uMgababa on 18 October.



However, Zuma broke his silence on Friday, 30 October, in a video message shared on the party’s social media platforms.

In his address, he thanked those who had wished him well and urged South Africans to vote for the MK Party in the upcoming elections.

Jacob Zuma also expressed confidence in the party’s chances, saying it was ready to take over municipalities.

World.title: Ncikazi details big Orlando Pirates decision
World.content:
Mandla Ncikazi has returned home to KwaZulu Natal after a five-year chapter with Orlando Pirates. He is back as a head coach at Golden Arrows, since leaving in 2021.

NCIKAZI EXPLAINS ORLANDO PIRATES EXIT

According Ncikazi, his new responsibility is an opportunity to test himself again. He says he is relishing the opportunity to work with the raw talent at Arrows.

“I thought with gratitude, where I’m coming from, I think I achieved everything as a coach. I’m grateful to the big institution and all the memories,” Ncikazi told journalists.



The experienced coach revealed that his decision was influenced by the opportunity to return to a club where he previously enjoyed considerable success.

“I thank the supporters for sharing such memories with them. Then your next phase, after you have won everything, now as a coach, maybe [go for] a different challenge,” he added.

“Let me go back, work with young players, challenge myself. “I don’t want to retire as a coach, not having the stress that I have today. I thought it was an opportunity for me when Arrows gave me the opportunity. I said the club is still very close to my heart.



Ncikazi also reflected on his previous achievements at Golden Arrows, where he believes he helped take the club to new heights.

“The highest position that Arrows ever achieved was in my presence. We broke almost lots of records, maybe that crave was still there.”

GOLDEN ARROWS COACH FACES IMMEDIATE CHALLENGE

However, Ncikazi has little time to settle into his new role. Golden Arrows have a demanding fixture schedule, leaving limited opportunities to work on the tactical and technical improvements he wants to introduce.



He acknowledged that the circumstances are different from his first spell at the club, when he had more time to implement his ideas.

“Now we have a challenge right now. At the time when I started, I had the time. Right now, there’s not too much time. We have another game on Tuesday.

“So we want to train certain aspects, but we are playing games. But that’s the responsibility of a coach,” the former Orlando Pirates tactician concluded.

World.title: Kick off time for Springboks vs Italy this Saturday
World.content:
The last time the Springboks took to the field, Rassie Erasmus’s team suffered a shock defeat to Australia, and so they will be desperate to get back down to business as they get set to kick off a series of November Tests.

Heading into the resumption of the Nations Championship, the Springboks currently lead the Southern Hemisphere standings on points’ difference, tied on 15 points with New Zealand.

There are four more fixtures to come this November as South Africa will line up against Italy (7 November), France (13 November), and Ireland (21 November) before the Finals Weekend in London (27-29 November).



This Saturday’s encounter against Italy will kick off at 13:40 (SA time), and Ireland’s Cross will be the man in the middle in Turin this Saturday, 7 November.

“Italy may be ranked 11th in the world at this stage, but they are a quality team who have tested us to the limit at times, so we will not be fooled by the standings,” Erasmus commented.

“They will be playing at home in front of a passionate crowd, and they’ll be desperate to work their way into a good position for the remainder of the competition, so we will certainly not underestimate them.”

World.title: Water supply interruption for parts of Durban: Here’s where
World.content:
Parts of Durban have been affected by water supply interruptions for around two weeks. Image: canva

Parts of Durban are facing ongoing water supply interruptions, with residents and businesses in several Pinetown South and surrounding areas affected.

The eThekwini Municipality said the interruptions are the result of water supply curtailments by bulk water supplier uMngeni-uThukela Water at the Durban Heights Water Treatment Works.

The curtailments have reduced water flows through the Southern Aqueduct, affecting water levels at the Northdene and Shallcross reservoirs.



The municipality said the situation has persisted for approximately two weeks and continues to affect water availability across the impacted supply zones.

No restoration timeframe yet

The Pinetown South reservoir system depends entirely on the Shallcross Reservoir for its water supply. However, continued depletion of water levels at Shallcross has placed the system under severe strain.

The Washington Heights and Intake reservoirs are currently empty, eThekwini Municipality said, and there is currently no confirmed timeframe for the restoration of normal water supplies.

Pumping operations will resume once water levels at Shallcross Reservoir have stabilised and improved, provided there are adequate inflows from the Southern Aqueduct.

The municipality said it is monitoring the situation and implementing measures to reduce the impact on affected communities.

Water tankers have been arranged to provide interim relief to affected communities while the municipality works to restore water availability.



Durban Areas affected

The affected areas include:

Supply system Areas affected N-Pump Station Klaarwater, Phumphele, St Wendolins, parts of Nsizwaqkazi, Savannah Park Phases 1 and 2, Wiltshire Factories Washington Heights Reservoir Klaarwater, Nsizwaqkazi, Regency Park, Latana, Hlanganisa, Gwala Road, Sarjoo Road Intake Reservoir Demat, Progress Road, Mawelewele, Intake Road, Luganda, parts of Nagina Township, Khoseleni, Sthundu Hills, Dambuza, parts of Bell Tower Road, parts of Grasmere Road, Mpongo Road

Residents in the affected areas should prepare for continued interruptions until water levels at Shallcross Reservoir recover and sufficient flows return through the Southern Aqueduct.

World.title: Durban on high alert as severe thunderstorms set to hit
World.content:
Durban residents have been warned to take precautions as severe thunderstorms, heavy downpours, hail and lightning are expected across eThekwini.

The eThekwini Municipality has placed its disaster management and emergency services teams on high alert following a Yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms issued by the South African Weather Service.

The warning is valid from 12:00 until 23:59 on Sunday, 1 November 2026.



Emergency teams on standby

The municipality said its teams are closely monitoring areas that are particularly vulnerable to severe weather, including low-lying communities and informal settlements.

Resources have been placed on standby to respond to incidents including flooding, damage to infrastructure, fallen trees blocking roads and other weather-related emergencies

Disaster Management Director Vincent Ngubane urged residents to take the warning seriously.

“Our teams are closely monitoring areas prone to weather-related incidents, and resources are on standby to respond swiftly wherever they are needed. We urge residents to take the warning seriously and put their safety first,” said Ngubane.

What Durban residents should do

Residents living in flood-prone areas are urged to move valuables to a location above the expected flood level. People living in rural areas should move livestock to higher ground where possible.

The municipality is also advising residents to stay indoors during the severe weather where possible.



Motorists should reduce their speed and maintain a safe following distance, particularly during heavy rain when visibility and road conditions can deteriorate quickly.

Residents are also warned not to attempt to cross flooded roads, rivers or swollen streams.

Anyone who becomes trapped in a vehicle during flooding should leave the vehicle and move to higher ground, provided it is safe to do so.

Residents are encouraged to monitor the City’s official communication platforms for further weather and emergency updates.

Anyone who needs emergency assistance can contact the eThekwini Disaster Management Centre on 031 361 0000.

Residents in vulnerable areas should take the necessary precautions before conditions deteriorate and avoid unnecessary travel during the warning period.

World.title: IEC explains vote-counting process ahead of local government elections
World.content:
Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Sy Mamabolo says votes in the 2026 local government elections will be counted at the voting stations where they were cast to prevent possible interference during transportation.

Mamabolo explained the process as South Africans prepare to head to the polls on Wednesday, 4 November.

IEC CLARIFIES VOTE-COUNTING PROCESS

Earlier this week, Mamabolo told Newzroom Afrika that ballots would be counted at the voting stations, eliminating the need to transport them and potentially exposing them to interference.



“As soon as the voting station closes, it will be converted into a counting station. Party agents will observe the counting process, as well as observers as they may be. Just as a matter of interest, the Commission has accredited over 100 observer organisations.

“Upon the conclusion of counting, a result slip will then be generated and party agents will be expected to sign that result slip as confirmation that the votes attributed to their party, candidate or independent candidate are correct,” the IEC CEO explained.

COMMISSION INTRODUCES NEW MEASURES TO PROMOTE TRANSPARENCY

Mamabolo said one of the new measures that the IEC has introduced for the 2026 local government elections would allow political parties and their agents to photograph result slips before they leave voting stations.

This would ensure that parties have photographic copies of the results recorded at each voting station.

“The presiding officer will also have to announce the outcome of the count at that voting station, so that members of the community in the affected voting district are aware of the outcome.

“The result slip will then be taken to the local capturing site, where it will be captured on the double-capture system on the results system and thereafter audited by independent auditors, who will compare the result slip against what is captured on the results system,” he added.

World.title: People still believe that SA can do better - Hlabisa
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - 'If you are tired of empty promises, choose the IFP.'

That's the message from party leader Velenkosini Hlabisa.

Hlabisa closed the IFP election campaign in Ulundi, ahead of Wednesday's elections.

"‘They are tired of failed service deliveries, of dry taps, broken roads, unreliable electricity, uncollected refuse, dark streets and municipal offices that do not respond, tired of seeing the country moving backwards.

"Through our campaign we had something profound and encouraging. Beneath the anger and disappointment, there’s hope. People have not stopped believing that SA can do better, asking for a government that works, leadership that serves and a future that children can look forward to and inherit."

World.title: 'We've heard very clearly' - ANC president tells EC supporters
World.content:
MDANTSANE - ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa said the party has listened to communities’ concerns ahead of the elections.

Speaking at a campaign rally in Mdantsane, he said the ANC heard calls for better working conditions, action against gender-based violence, and greater support for people with disabilities.

Ramaphosa pledged the party’s commitment to addressing these issues.

" We heard very clearly what the aspirations of our people are, but we also heard the enthusiasm as well as the encouragement of our people. We've heard them repeating that they want us to work diligently to advance the lives of our people. We have listened to the workers of our country talking about, yes, the need that they want to see to improve the conditions of employment.

" It is also the ANC's ability to listen and to have deep exchanges with our people. We've also gone around Simamele, Okumkani namakosi ethu, as they too were raising many issues that concern them. We have listened to the women of our country as they too have raised issues that concern gender-based violence. We have listened to people who are disabled, and we have heard too the issues that concern them."

World.title: Tens of thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
World.content:
"It is the theft of the voice of every single citizen of India," he said during a speech.

"This protest does not belong to any political party. It is India's protest to save the democracy and constitution."

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the opposition campaign.

The overhaul of India's voter rolls has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings.

Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.

Members of the BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls.

- 'Power of the people' -

Election authorities say the revision was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries, and that eligible voters remain entitled to apply for inclusion on the roll.

Among the protestors on Sunday was 46-year-old Nandita, who said she had been struck off the electoral list despite being a voter since she was 18 years old.

"It's important to be here because of the way things are going... The only option is to take to the streets peacefully," Nandita told AFP, giving only one name.

Health Minister and senior BJP leader Jagat Prakash Nadda called the rally "a meticulously planned drama by those who have been defeated and repeatedly rejected by the people."

World.title: Longest truce of Ukraine war, in Kherson region, set to end
World.content:
KYIV - The longest truce of the Ukraine war, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and limited to just the Kherson region, was set to end on Sunday evening after neither side announced an extension.

The rare pause in fighting, which began early Tuesday, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and came as the Ukraine war grinds through its fifth year.

Neither side reported violations after the truce began, in what one Ukrainian lawmaker described as the "biggest de-escalation since 2022".

The conflict, sparked by Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion, has destroyed parts of eastern and southern Ukraine, left hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians dead, and forced millions to flee their homes.

AFP spoke to several Kherson residents, one of whom said the ceasefire had been a "breath of fresh air".

"We have to use this time to get things done," said Volodymyr Omeltchenko, a 38-year-old gardener. "We're pruning the rose bushes for winter."

The ceasefire was due to end later Sunday.

A Ukrainian military officer, speaking on the condition of anonymity, expressed concerns that the fighting would be "worse than before" when it resumed.

Russian forces, positioned on the other side of the Dnipro river, have taken advantage of the calm of the past few days to amass new troops, transport ammunition stocks, and collect intelligence on Ukrainian positions using surveillance drones, the officer said.

- Refinery reportedly hit -

Fighting continued elsewhere in Ukraine.

Russia said Sunday that a drone had struck an "industrial enterprise" east of Moscow overnight.

World.title: Irish European athletics champion Ciara Mageean dies aged 34
World.content:
BELFAST - Irish middle-distance runner Ciara Mageean, who won European gold and competed at two Olympic Games, has died aged 34, her family announced on Sunday.

"At 6:30am this morning, Ciara lost her battle with cancer surrounded by her loved ones," said a statement posted on the athlete's Instagram account.

Mageean's death comes just weeks after she married her long-term boyfriend in Belfast.

She had been receiving treatment for bowel cancer, revealing her diagnosis in July 2025 and subsequently disclosing that the disease was at an advanced stage.

Originally from Portaferry in County Down, Northern Ireland, Mageean established herself as one of Ireland's leading middle-distance runners, setting several national records.

She represented Ireland at the 2016 Rio Olympics and the Tokyo Games held in 2021.

Her greatest sporting achievement came in 2024 when she claimed the 1,500 metres title at the European Athletics Championships in Rome.

But an Achilles injury prevented her from competing at the Paris Olympics that year.

Mageean remained remarkably positive throughout her period of illness saying she was "continuing to find the joy in everyday" as she thanked people for their support following her diagnosis.

Speaking to the BBC in June, she said she was "grateful" for having a career "that many others didn't get to have".

Tributes poured in for Mageean, who also won a European silver and bronze in the 1500m (2022/2016 respectively) and finished second in the event in the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

"The country has lost a hero," the Olympic Federation of Ireland said in a statement.

"Beyond the medals, records and sporting accolades, Ciara will be remembered for her warmth, courage and tremendous strength of character," said Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill.

Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin said he was "deeply saddened" by Mageean's "untimely passing".

World.title: Lesufi gives progress report on presidential directives
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi reports that 21 presidential directives are already complete. He updated the province on its fight against GBV and femicide.

This progress follows presidential directives and a four-point plan to combat the scourge.

"Today is the 1st of November, it is approximately day 33 of the 90 day period that the President gave us. Of the 67 specific directives, 21 have been fully completed, 38 are underway and eight have not yet started. Four directives have moved into the implementation stage.

"The provincial government has recovered crime kits from all five districts for processing to strengthen evidence management," he said.

World.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on security forces
World.content:
PARIS - France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.

On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and some other cities after hundreds of thousands of people staged a third weekend of protests against soaring living costs.

The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has decried an "extraordinary" level of violence from some rioters.

"Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers," the prosecutor's office said on Sunday.

Gendarmes are military police officers who are part of the French armed forces.

Prosecutors said an investigation had been opened for "attempted murder of persons vested with public authority".

Dramatic images, including AFP photos and video, showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in eastern Paris, engulfing his lower body in flames.

An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding that the reported injuries include second-degree burns.

Initial complaints were expected to be filed on Sunday.

World.title: North West farm robbery suspects arrested
World.content:
VENTERSDORP - North West police have arrested two suspects for a violent farm robbery and attempted murder in Ventersdorp.

A 50-year-old farmer was shot and had his ears cut off during Wednesday's attack.
