World.title: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack
World.content:
A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

National Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula confirmed that Egypt's Deputy Ambassador to Malawi was admitted to a hospital in the capital after the attack.

"Police are following up on the matter and will give more details later," she said.

Chiwaula gave few details.

She did not say where the attack happened, what led to it, or how serious the diplomat's injuries are. Police have also withheld the deputy ambassador's name.

Officers say they are investigating, but the incident is likely to raise alarm over the safety of foreign envoys in the country.

World.title: South Africa: African Horse Sickness Confirmed in Western Cape's Cederberg
World.content:
The Department of Agriculture has confirmed a case of African horse sickness (AHS) in a single horse on a property in the Cederberg Local Municipality in the Western Cape, prompting movement restrictions and intensified surveillance to contain the disease.

Laboratory tests conducted by the University of Pretoria's Veterinary Genetics Laboratory confirmed the presence of AHS virus serotype 7 on the property, which is located within South Africa's established AHS Protection Zone.

Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp said the case was detected through the country's veterinary surveillance systems, enabling authorities to respond swiftly and implement containment measures.

"The swift detection of this case in the Cederberg Local Municipality is a good example of how South Africa's veterinary surveillance system works. As a result, the authorities were able to move quickly to the affected area and take the required stringent actions as stipulated in the Animal Diseases Act and deploy containment protocols," Aucamp said.



In accordance with the Animal Diseases Act, 1984 (Act 35 of 1984), and the Western Cape Department of Agriculture's AHS contingency plan, an outbreak containment area has been established and movement controls implemented.

Horse movements within the controlled area ordinarily require a permit issued by the State Veterinarian: Boland. However, the department has advised that no permits will be issued for moving horses out of the affected area, while investigations and surveillance continue.

Veterinary Services, working with authorised veterinarians and industry partners, have also commenced intensive surveillance, tracing and census activities to determine the extent of the outbreak and identify any additional cases.

The department has urged equine owners in the controlled area to cooperate with Veterinary Services and report any animals showing signs consistent with AHS, including unexplained fever, swelling of the head or neck, breathing difficulties or sudden death.

Horse owners are also encouraged to take precautions against Culicoides midges, which transmit the disease. Recommended measures include stabling horses, where possible, from two hours before sunset until two hours after sunrise, avoiding low-lying and wet areas, and appropriately using registered insect repellents and insecticides.

The department has strongly discouraged AHS vaccination at this time, explaining that the currently registered vaccine is live-attenuated and that vaccination during periods of vector activity could result in the vaccine strain being spread by midges, potentially worsening the situation.

Close 

"While there is no proof of large-scale disease activity outside the said property, the department is focused on total vigilance and calls on all horse owners to refrain from AHS vaccination during this period. Veterinary Services will continue to monitor the situation closely and will provide updates as additional information becomes available," Aucamp said.

The department said international trade partners will be notified of the outbreak, with further information on the implications for international trade to be provided in due course.

Updates on containment measures, movement restrictions and permits will be issued by the Western Cape Department of Agriculture. Further information is available from Veterinary Services and at www.myhorse.org.za

World.title: Kenya: No, Kenyan Pastor Victor Kanyari Was Not Killed in a Road Accident
World.content:
No, Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari was not killed in a road accident

IN SHORT: A fake Citizen Digital news graphic claims Kenyan pastor Victor Kanyari died in a road accident. But the image is fabricated and uses an old photograph of a separate crash.

Social media posts circulating in Kenya feature what appears to be a Citizen Digital breaking news alert, dated 5 October 2026. It claims that pastor Victor Kanyari has died in a road accident along Kangundo Road in the capital, Nairobi.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The graphic shows Kanyari alongside a badly damaged white vehicle surrounded by onlookers.

Collectively, the posts we sampled received more than 162,000 views and 2,000 likes.

Who is Kanyari?

Kanyari is a Kenyan preacher who heads the Salvation Healing Ministry in Nairobi. He made headlines in 2014 after a KTN investigation exposed staged miracles at his ministry and his controversial KSh310 donation scheme, which he later acknowledged was intended to lift him out of poverty.

Kanyari was previously married to gospel singer Beatrice Wairimu Mbugua, popularly known as Betty Bayo. They had two children. Bayo died of leukaemia on 10 November 2025, prompting a custody dispute between Kanyari and the children's stepfather, Hiram Gitau, popularly known as Tash.

On 26 October 2026, a court awarded Kanyari legal custody but ordered a gradual transition, allowing the children to remain temporarily with Tash.

The dispute, along with his active social media presence, has kept Kanyari in the public eye. He has also announced plans to contest the Kasarani parliamentary seat in Kenya's 2027 general election.

Citizen Digital is the online news platform of Citizen TV, owned by Royal Media Services.

But did the broadcaster report Kanyari's death in a road accident? We checked.

Old accident photo used in fake graphic

We found no credible news reports confirming Kanyari's alleged death or a corresponding report on Citizen Digital or Citizen TV's social media accounts.

In contrast, Kanyari's social media accounts feature recent photos and videos of him going about his usual activities.

A reverse image search revealed that the photo of the wrecked vehicle had been shared on Facebook on 27 June 2024, more than two years before the supposed news alert.

Close 

The earlier post was captioned: "Bad accident on Ngong road joining on to Karen road. Multiple casualties."

The vehicle and onlookers match those in the circulating graphic, confirming the photograph predates the alleged October 2026 crash.

The graphic is fabricated. It uses an old accident photo to support a false claim about Kanyari's death. His recent public activities also contradict the rumour.

World.title: Kenya: 46 Ebola Contacts Set for Discharge From Quarantine On November 3
World.content:
Nairobi — Public Health Principal Secretary May Muthoni says 46 contacts under quarantine are expected to be discharged on November 3 after completing the required monitoring period.

Muthoni has directed health teams to prepare the necessary discharge packages and support for those completing quarantine.

"We must also be able to complete the full 21 days of followup and every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed discharge package and support... we must also continue to follow up the nine contacts outside Kenya with the countries concerned," she said.



She said every person leaving quarantine must receive the agreed assistance as authorities maintain surveillance to prevent further transmission.

The PS urged response teams to ensure all arrangements are in place ahead of Tuesday's planned discharge.

"Kenya is making progress in containing the Ebola outbreak, with no new cases reported in the last 10 days, following coordinated efforts by the Ministry of Health, County Governments and development partners," Muthoni stated.

So far, the country has recorded nine cases and two deaths;.

Following confirmation of the first Ebola case on 6 October, the health ministry conducted "robust contact tracing of anyone who may have been exposed", the World Health Organization (WHO) says. By 22 October, all contacts had been traced, both in Kenya and internationally, and placed in quarantine, it adds.

The government says that the confirmed cases so far are connected and there is no evidence that the virus has spread to the community.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Four in Plateau Community Despite Curfew
World.content:
The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.

At least four people were killed after gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night.

The attackers reportedly stormed the community at about 8 p.m. and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to contain insecurity.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

A resident of Barkin Ladi, Bulus Jok, said the gunmen operated freely for some time, shooting indiscriminately.

"The gunmen struck the community around 8 p.m. despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically," Mr Jok said.

He added that the attack threw residents into panic, leaving four people dead.

Mr Jok expressed concern that the incident occurred despite an early warning reportedly sent to relevant authorities a day before the attack.

"It is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack," he said.

The Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the incident.

Mr Tengwong condemned the killings, describing the attack as unacceptable and expressing concern over the continued assaults on communities despite security measures.

He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance, strengthen their presence in vulnerable communities and respond promptly to intelligence and early warning reports to prevent further attacks.

The latest incident adds to the series of attacks on communities in Plateau State, raising fresh concerns about the effectiveness of security measures, including curfews, in protecting residents.

Efforts to reach security operatives for official confirmation and further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Ethiopia: U.S. Customs Releases Ethiopia-Made Solar Cell Shipments After Supply Chain Review
World.content:
Addis Abeba — US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has released shipments of solar cells manufactured at a Japanese company's facility in Ethiopia following a review of its supply chain documentation, SolarQuarter reported.

TOYO Co., Ltd., a Japan-headquartered solar manufacturing company, announced on 29 October that CBP had completed its review after the company submitted documentation demonstrating the traceability of its supply chain, including the origins of polysilicon and wafers used in manufacturing the solar cells.

The company said it cooperated with US authorities throughout the review process and provided detailed documentation on the sourcing of its production materials.

The release of the shipments comes as TOYO seeks to expand its international manufacturing operations and strengthen its presence in the US market. The company operates a manufacturing facility in Humble, Texas, and is pursuing certification under CBP's Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) programme, which is designed to strengthen supply chain security and import compliance.



TOYO Chief Executive Officer Takahiko Onozuka welcomed the completion of the review, expressing appreciation for what he described as CBP's professional approach. He said the company remained committed to transparency and regulatory compliance as it expands its US operations.

Onozuka also stressed the importance of providing customers with confidence in the origins of solar products through greater supply chain traceability.

The development highlights the importance of supply chain documentation and regulatory compliance for solar manufacturers operating across multiple countries, particularly as scrutiny of the origins of imported products increases.

The release of the shipments follows an ongoing US investigation into whether solar cell manufacturers operating in Ethiopia are circumventing existing American trade duties on Chinese solar products.

In July 2026, Addis Standard reported that the US Department of Commerce had launched a country-wide investigation into imports of silicon solar cells from Ethiopia to determine whether they were circumventing longstanding antidumping and countervailing duty (AD/CVD) orders on Chinese solar products.

The investigation followed a petition filed in May 2026 by eight US solar manufacturers -- DYCM Power, First Solar, Qcells, Silfab, Solx, Suniva, Swift Solar and Talon PV -- alleging that two manufacturers operating in Ethiopia, TOYO and Origin Solar, were using Chinese-origin wafers to produce solar cells in Ethiopia before assembling them into solar modules locally or in Vietnam for export to the US.

According to the petition, nearly 70% of finished solar modules exported from Ethiopia contained Chinese components and underwent processing allegedly covered by existing US trade restrictions. Solar Power World reported that imports of Ethiopia-origin solar cells and modules, which were virtually nonexistent before July 2025, reached an estimated $277 million in the second half of that year, with shipments continuing to increase in 2026.

The petitioners argued that the surge in exports coincided with increased shipments of key solar manufacturing inputs from China to Ethiopia. Both TOYO and Origin Solar subsequently submitted factual information to the Department of Commerce in response to the allegations.

The investigation is expected to reach a preliminary determination by 10 December 2026, with a final decision anticipated around 10 May 2027. In the meantime, US Customs and Border Protection was instructed to suspend liquidation of relevant imports and apply cash deposit requirements pending the outcome. Any duties imposed could be applied retroactively to the investigation's initiation date.

Close 

The dispute first emerged publicly in May 2026, when Addis Standard, citing Reuters, reported that a coalition of US solar manufacturers had petitioned the Department of Commerce to investigate imports from Ethiopia over alleged tariff circumvention.

The petition came weeks after Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed inaugurated solar manufacturing facilities at Hawassa Industrial Park on 25 April 2026. According to state media, the facilities included TOYO Phase 2, Origin and Lumintech, which were expected to have a combined annual production capacity of 11.3 gigawatts.

At the inauguration, Abiy said the projects reflected Ethiopia's ambition to expand its industrial base and renewable energy sector.

World.title: Ethiopia: 'Ethiopia's Return to a Sea Port Is Inevitable': Navy Commander Calls for Regional Maritime Cooperation
World.content:
Addis Abeba — Ethiopian Navy Commander Vice Admiral Kindu Gezu has called for closer regional cooperation and dialogue on maritime security, saying Ethiopia's return to a seaport is inevitable and requires stronger engagement with neighboring countries.

"Since Ethiopia's return to a sea port is inevitable, working closely and through dialogue with regional countries is essential," Kindu said on Friday, a day after the conclusion of a regional maritime security forum organized by the Ethiopian Navy Headquarters, according to the army.

The forum brought together naval commanders and representatives from Yemen, Oman, Djibouti, Somaliland, and Puntland to exchange experiences and explore joint approaches to maritime search and rescue operations and regional security challenges. ENDF said the forum was organized with the support of the European Union.

Kindu described the gathering as "the first of its kind in Ethiopia" to discuss regional maritime search and rescue plans, saying it demonstrated the Ethiopian Navy's growing capabilities and readiness to engage in regional and continental maritime affairs.



He also highlighted growing security challenges around the Strait of Hormuz, warning that threats in the area could increasingly affect the wider region. No country, regardless of its strength, could independently ensure maritime security or resolve emerging challenges, he said, emphasizing the need for countries of different sizes to pool their capabilities.

"The participating countries of the forum must work together to solve the problems observed in the region," Kindu said, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime threats and ensuring safe maritime movement.

Ethiopian Navy Deputy Commander for Operations Commodore Jemal Tufisa said the forum had helped establish practical foundations for regional cooperation through cross-border information sharing, identifying areas of concern, and conducting joint operational exercises.

"We trust that upon returning to your respective countries, you will translate the lessons gained from the workshop into action, working effectively on regional maritime security and performing tasks with international acceptance," Jemal said.

Rear Admiral Kenneth Nyagah, a search and rescue project expert, and Master Kuraja Mishini, manager of the Djibouti Code of Conduct, commended the Ethiopian Navy's initiative in creating communication channels for information sharing, coordinated decision-making, and joint responses to regional threats. Both expressed their commitment to continued cooperation.

Close 

The forum concluded on Thursday with discussions on "existing maritime security conditions and potential future scenarios", including the actions participating countries should take in responding to specific emergencies and threats.

World.title: Liberia: Congo Town Overpasses Spark Political Storm
World.content:
The ongoing construction of two overpass bridges along Tubman Boulevard in Congo Town has sparked a political dispute between supporters of former President George Manneh Weah's Congress for Democratic Change (CDC) and President Joseph Nyuma Boakai's ruling Unity Party (UP), with both sides claiming credit for the Chinese-funded infrastructure project.

While CDC supporters insist that the project was initiated and negotiated under the Weah administration, supporters of the ruling Unity Party point to the Boakai government's role in overseeing its implementation and advancing construction.

The controversy has revived debate over which administration deserves recognition for major infrastructure projects initiated under previous governments but implemented or completed by their successors.

Official records indicate that the Congo Town overpass project originated during the Weah administration, following diplomatic engagements between Liberia and China.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

On September 1, 2018, former President Weah met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, where discussions centered on strengthening bilateral relations and supporting infrastructure development in Liberia.

According to an Executive Mansion statement issued at the time, the discussions included plans to construct two overpasses at SKD Boulevard and near the Ministerial Complex in Congo Town.

The initiative gained momentum on September 9, 2019, when Liberia and China signed an agreement for the construction of the two overhead bridges, according to records from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Another significant milestone came on June 8, 2021, when the two countries signed an implementation agreement for the project along Tubman Boulevard.

The Ministry of Public Works subsequently identified the overpasses as part of China's infrastructure assistance to Liberia.

CDC supporters argue that these diplomatic engagements and agreements establish that the project was conceived and negotiated under the Weah administration, contrary to suggestions that it originated under President Boakai.

However, supporters of the ruling Unity Party maintain that the current administration deserves recognition for advancing the project through the construction phase.

The disagreement underscores the distinction between initiating and securing financing for infrastructure projects and supervising their implementation and eventual completion.

Close 

The controversy also comes amid a broader political exchange between officials of the current and former administrations over the ownership of ongoing development projects.

Finance and Development Planning Minister Augustine K. Ngafuan recently challenged claims by former Finance Minister Samuel Tweah that several projects being implemented by the Boakai administration were inherited from the CDC government.

Ngafuan argued that completing unfinished projects inherited from previous administrations does not prevent the government from pursuing new development initiatives.

"If you had completed the old projects, we would have been doing only the new projects. But we now have to complete the old projects while doing the new ones simultaneously," Ngafuan said.

His remarks reflect the administration's position that completing inherited infrastructure projects forms part of its responsibility to ensure continuity in national development.

Meanwhile, construction of the two Congo Town overpasses remained underway as of October 28, 2026.

The bridges are expected to ease traffic congestion, improve road safety and reduce travel times along Tubman Boulevard, a major transportation corridor connecting Monrovia and Paynesville.

The project, estimated at approximately US$36.6 million, is being financed by the Chinese government through an assistance grant.

Although the political debate over credit continues, the project's documented history spans successive administrations, from diplomatic negotiations and agreements under Weah to ongoing construction under Boakai. -Editing by The New Dawn

Capturing Bigfoot

I watched the "Capturing Bigfoot" documentary when it came out on Bigfoot Day, which is October 20, for those who didn't know.

The documentary is about the famous 1967 Patterson-Gimlin Bigfoot footage. The footage that supposedly shows Bigfoot out for a stroll in California.

There were a few things about the Patterson-Gimlin film that I didn’t know before I sat down and watched it. On the top of that list is that people still believed, at least before this documentary, that footage was real.

That blew me away. I thought it was agreed upon long ago that it was fake. Apparently not. There were some out there who believed it was real video evidence of Bigfoot.

The documentary (spoiler alert) shows another piece of footage that was believed to be a test run a year before Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin filmed the footage we have all seen.

I debated whether I would write a standalone article about the documentary and I decided that it belonged in "America's Best Daily Column." I said in a prior edition of Sunday Screencaps that I would watch it after all, and I did purchase it and waste my time watching it.

CARMEN ELECTRA OFFICIALLY KICKS OFF HALLOWEEN SEASON AT A GAS STATION, POSTGAME POLICE CHASE & BALL-SAC

Back to the doc. Another piece of information I learned about the Patterson-Gimlin film was how much money it generated when it first came out. I had no idea that it was shown in venues around the country.

I didn’t get into Bigfoot because of the Patterson-Gimlin film.

As I've mentioned before, it was the fine work and incredible confidence in the existence of Bigfoot (despite an overwhelming lack of evidence) by the folks on the show "Finding Bigfoot" that got me hooked.

So, if you're interested in learning more about the Patterson-Gimlin film, the documentary will fill you in. They spoke to many people involved in and around the famous footage.

If you're hoping this documentary finally debunks the Patterson-Gimlin film, I'd point you at the original footage. That does a decent job of debunking it all by itself.

Oh, and one more thing I learned from this doc. The Bigfoot in the Patterson-Gimlin is female and has boobs.

World.title: Ancient Roman treasure unearthed at military base, two coins aren't what they seem
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Archaeologists in Sweden recently made an unusual discovery. They found 45 ancient Roman silver coins, including two believed to be counterfeits.

The discovery was announced by the Swedish Armed Forces earlier this fall.

The coins were unearthed during archaeological excavations ahead of an expansion of Sweden's Gotland Regiment military base, according to officials.

MYSTERIOUS FIND BENEATH FIELD LEADS MAN TO MASSIVE TREASURE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES

"During one of the excavations, an unusual find was made — a silver treasure with Roman coins from the second century A.D.," the Swedish Armed Forces said in a translated statement.

The discovery came as archaeologists were wrapping up an excavation of a farmhouse foundation dating to the Migration Period, which spanned roughly the fifth and sixth centuries A.D.

The archaeologists were making "one final sweep with the metal detector" before the discovery, according to officials.

"Then an insistent beeping indicated that something was in the ground near one of the foundation stones," the statement said.

"They carefully dug a small silver coin out of the soil — and more finds would follow."

RARE COIN BEARING FACE OF KING WITH INFAMOUS NICKNAME UNEARTHED AFTER 1,000 YEARS

When archaeologists brushed off the coin, they discovered a stamped portrait of Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius, who ruled from 138 to 161 A.D.

"The metal detector's persistent beeping indicated that more objects were hidden near the same foundation stone," officials said.

"Before the workday was over, archaeologists had counted 45 coins and a gold finger ring. All the coins are Roman, minted during the second century for five emperors and four empresses."

The coins were identified by Lennart Lind, a Swedish expert on Roman coins.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER SPRAWLING ROMAN ESTATE BURIED FOR CENTURIES BENEATH FARMLAND

The coins feature five Roman emperors — Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius and Commodus — as well as four empresses: Vibia Sabina, Faustina I, Faustina II and Lucilla, according to officials.

Experts believe the coins arrived on Gotland during the fourth century and were used in trade for generations before being buried alongside the gold ring around 450 A.D.

"It looks like it was slowly abandoned, and some of the people might even have come back to this place to get more things back to a new settlement."

Two of the coins, however, were ancient counterfeits that may have originated in what is now Ukraine, according to archaeologists.

Elsewhere on the military grounds, archaeologists found nine graves believed to be around 2,000 years old, including one containing nearly 10 pounds of burned human bones, according to the release.

The remains belonged to at least two individuals, including an adult man, officials said.

Archaeologists also discovered bronze fittings believed to have been attached to a sword suspension and a shield.

The coins may have been buried as part of a sacrifice, said Per Widerström, an archaeologist at Gotland Museum.

Widerström told Fox News Digital the silver coins were largely what archaeologists would expect to uncover at such a site, but the gold ring was unusual.

Widerström also said newly received radiocarbon dating results indicated activity at the settlement from the fourth through sixth centuries, consistent with archaeologists' expectations.

"Perhaps it was abandoned around 540 when there was a low in human history in this part of the world because of natural disasters from 536 A.D. and on for 10 years," Widerström said. "Maybe that is the reason behind them leaving the farm."

The Roman coin hoard is the latest in a series of ancient discoveries in Sweden.

The bigger surprise, he said, was the number of buildings identified at the site — six in total, apparently belonging to two neighboring farms.

World.title: Why people really stopped having kids: New study uncovers the surprising reasons families are shrinking
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

High housing costs and unequal chore loads may not fully explain the drop in birth rates around the world, according to a new report from the Institute for Family Studies and the Wheatley Institute.

The survey of nearly 10,000 respondents across more than a dozen countries points to culture, finding that peer pressure, anxiety about the future and the rise of "pet parenting" strongly influence whether couples choose to start or grow a family.

"Ultra-Orthodox Jews in Brooklyn have six kids each. Their hipster neighbors have 1.6 kids each," Lyman Stone, senior fellow and director of the Pronatalism Initiative at the Institute for Family Studies, told Fox News Digital. "They live in the same economy. They have very different outcomes. Why? Different culture."

AGE OF FIRST-TIME MOTHERS HITS RECORD HIGH IN BLUE STATES AS BIRTH RATES KEEP FALLING

The report also tested whether sharing chores affects fertility intentions, finding no statistically significant relationship between family planning and either the division of household responsibilities or perceptions of fairness.

"There's been a lot of research on, you know, 'If men did more laundry, would birth rates go up? If men helped out more at home, would birth rates go up?' And the answer is basically no," Stone said.

ALEX BERENSON: GENTLE PARENTING CAN'T REPLACE THE STRENGTH OF A GOOD DAD

"The last 30 years have seen a revolution in involved fatherhood. Dads are doing more at home than ever before and fertility rates keep plummeting," he added to Fox News Digital.

One of the strongest associations researchers identified was between fertility intentions and having a supportive circle of friends. Believing that one's friends would celebrate a new baby was linked to a 10% increase in desired family size and a 20% higher likelihood of intending to have another child.

TRADITIONAL TWO-PARENT FAMILIES VANISH FROM BIG AMERICAN CITIES AS 'MARRIAGE DESERTS' EXPAND

"All around the world, we just found that friends are really important," Stone said. "Where peer culture ratifies and encourages family life, family life is more successful."

The association extended beyond friends to admired public figures. Respondents who admired a celebrity with more children than they had were 14% more likely to intend to have another child.

DRIVEN BY PROGRESSIVE DOOMISM, LIBERALS ARE HAVING FEWER BABIES THAN CONSERVATIVE FAMILIES

Researchers also identified a connection between attitudes toward pets and decisions about having children. Respondents who expressed a preference for being a "pet parent" rather than having children reported a 30% lower desired family size and showed a 50% drop in intentions to have more children.

"The animal is not the problem. The problem is the attitude," Stone said. "That says that, you know, changing a litter box is truly as meaningful as changing a diaper. And I just have to tell you, it isn't."

AMERICA’S BABY BUST MAY BE LINKED TO THE IPHONE, STUDY SAYS

Researchers found that risk aversion, anxiety about the future and general pessimism were also associated with smaller desired families. Respondents who were more comfortable taking risks and optimistic about their futures tended to desire and have more children.

"Some decline in fertility may just be because there's bad vibes," Stone said to Fox News Digital. "There's just the internet constantly telling you that everything is bad, everything's getting worse and there’s a million things to be worried about and you shouldn't take any risks."

"I hate to tell you, but yeah, having children has a possibility of hurting you, both physically, financially and emotionally, in the long run, you know, a child who grows up to reject you is a very painful thing. So yes, there is risk with having kids. But there is also great reward," he added.

Encouragement from parents was another significant factor associated with fertility intentions. According to the study, "Parental encouragement to have children is associated with an 11% increase in desired number of children and a 30% increase in the likelihood of intending to have another one." Encouraging childless, cohabiting adult children to marry was also associated with a 14% higher likelihood of intending to have a child.

FAMILY BREAKDOWN IN PENNSYLVANIA PROMPTS FAITH-BASED EFFORT TO BRING MARRIAGE BACK

But Stone cautioned that guilt-tripping adult children into having kids may be ineffective. Instead, he suggested parents share the joy they experienced raising children and offer practical support.

"If you're a parent and you want grandbabies from your adult children, you probably won't get very far telling them that they owe you grandbabies," Stone said. "But you may get somewhere telling them stories of how much you enjoyed raising them and how much fun you think you're going to have helping them raise their children."

NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD

Religion was another factor linked to larger families. Respondents with the highest levels of religious devotion had 9% more children and were 12% more likely to intend to have another child.

But researchers found no statistically significant relationship between hearing clergy speak about family and family size. Instead, the findings suggest religious communities may be associated with fertility intentions through friendships and networks of practical support, including help with meals and celebrating the arrival of a new baby.

"Where religion really does matter is it shapes the friendships people have. Religious people were overwhelmingly more likely to have friends who would be supportive of them having kids," Stone said.

"So, it seems that what's going on is religious communities are religious communities. They are places where people form friendships that create bonds of mutual support that exist almost secondary to the doctrines and theology of the organization. And first and foremost are about mutual investment in one another," he added.

For Stone, the findings suggest that efforts to encourage family formation do not depend solely on government policies or financial incentives. Friends, relatives and neighbors can also play a role by creating communities where raising children is supported and encouraged.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"You matter to the people around you and you have influence on them," Stone said. "You don't have to wait for the government to pass a law to make a difference for family formation. Regular people can influence this just by being good friends, good neighbors, good parents, good leaders and good members of the community, and telling young families: 'We're here for you, we support you, we think this is a good and admirable thing to do.'"

World.title: Trump's DOJ makeover hasn't changed where the political cash is flowing — and the gap is growing
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Trump administration has sought to eliminate what it alleges is partisan bias within the Justice Department, but the vast majority of political donations from individuals identifying themselves as DOJ employees are still going to Democratic-aligned committees, according to a Fox News Digital analysis of federal campaign finance records.

Between January 2025 and August of this year, just over 75% of campaign contributions from individuals identifying themselves as Department of Justice employees went to Democratic committees, the analysis of federal campaign finance records found.

Fox News Digital analyzed roughly $300,000 in political contributions recorded by the Federal Election Commission between January 2025 and August 2026 from donors who listed their employer as "Department of Justice," "DOJ" or a variation of those names. Contributions were categorized by the political affiliation of the recipient candidate or committee, while independent-expenditure committees were classified according to the candidates or parties they supported. When exporting data from the Federal Election Commission's dashboard, an option to include donations from "unique individuals only" was selected to filter out duplicative records.

As the Trump administration has progressed, the partisan slant of DOJ donations has become more pronounced. Through 2025, about 70% of donations from those identifying themselves as DOJ staff went to Democratic committees, a figure that rose to just under 90% in 2026, according to Fox News Digital's findings.

TODD BLANCHE EXPOSES HOW AGGRESSIVE BIDEN DOJ TARGETED LOW-LEVEL MAR-A-LAGO EMPLOYEES

Attorney General Todd Blanche and his predecessor, Pam Bondi, both claimed that the Trump administration inherited a deeply corrupt DOJ, pointing to allegations that the agency was inundated with political bias under President Joe Biden's tenure.

"There are a lot of people in the FBI and also in the Department of Justice who despise Donald Trump, despise us," Bondi said in early 2025. "Right now, we’re going to root them out; we will find them, and they will no longer be employed."

Critics have pushed back against claims of political weaponization during the Biden administration, arguing that high-profile investigations into President Donald Trump and other conservatives originated from legitimate legal concerns.

DOJ DANGLES MASSIVE SIGNING BONUSES FOR LAWYERS READY TO FIGHT ‘LAWLESS’ CITIES FAR BEYOND DC

Both of Trump’s attorneys general under his second administration have made strides to recruit a greater number of ideologically aligned lawyers while attempting to push those out who may not be willing to advance the administration’s interests.

In early February 2026, DOJ chief of staff Chad Mizelle publicly encouraged lawyers who "support President Trump" to contact him about becoming federal prosecutors. Stephen Miller amplified the appeal on social media with the caption "patriots needed," and sitting U.S. Attorney Jason Quiñones reposted the appeal alongside the phrase "we are hiring!" Mizelle later defended the approach as ensuring that executive-branch lawyers were in line with the elected president’s agenda.

LEGAL WAR ON TRUMP’S AGENDA GAINS FIREPOWER AS FEDERAL LAWYERS DEFECT TO DEMOCRATS

The administration's personnel overhaul has coincided with a substantial exodus of attorneys from federal service.

Over 10,000 attorneys have left federal service since Trump took office for a second term.

Fox News Digital reported in July that well over 100 federal attorneys had left the Trump administration for roles in Democratic-run state attorneys general offices. Many of these lawyers took decades of experience with them, prompting concerns that the Trump administration could be depriving itself of the ability to handle highly technical legal matters.

Some of these seasoned former federal lawyers have since joined legal action against the Trump administration.

While a significant number of government lawyers have left federal service under Trump, and some prominent conservatives have joined the administration, campaign finance records show that Democratic committees continue to receive the overwhelming majority of political contributions from donors identifying themselves as Justice Department employees.

Among the most common recipients of donations from those identifying themselves as DOJ employees were Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Georgia, and Emily’s List, a pro-abortion group associated with the Democratic Party. Some conservative committees, such as those in Trump’s network of PACs, were also common targets for Justice Department donors.

DEMOCRAT POLITICOS RERUN UNDERHANDED LEFTIST PLAYBOOK IN EFFORT TO TORPEDO TRUMP’S AG NOMINEE

Much of the DOJ's work concerns investigations and prosecutions unrelated to partisan politics, and the campaign finance records do not establish whether employees' political preferences have influenced the department's day-to-day operations.

Progressive critics, to the contrary, have alleged that the Trump administration is using the Justice Department to target its political enemies.

"Those who were fired from the Department were fired for a reason. Those who resigned or took the fork in the road option likely aligned more with the priorities of President Biden and would naturally leave, which is common during transitions," a DOJ spokeswoman previously told Fox News Digital. "The Administration gave career employees the fork in the road option to intentionally reduce the size of the government and eliminate unnecessary layers of staff who don’t effectively contribute to the mission of aggressively tackling crime."

The DOJ did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday.

"I've been pleasantly surprised," she explained. "I've had a really warm welcome, and a lot of cheering on from people just saying, 'Go get it, have fun.' And there's always going to be naysayers. Whether it's OnlyFans or some other job I've done, there's always somebody who wants to say something mean. You know, trolls. I just ignore it, honestly."

"I think the stigma around joining OnlyFans has changed," she said. "It's continuing to evolve. It's sort of like a modern-day fan club where you get to be directly with your fans. The content is right there. And especially as women in the entertainment industry, you want to have control over your own image. It's so important. It made total sense for me to join. And I think it's timely for people who want to take control of their own created image and content online."

Eleniak said she's comfortable embracing her sexy side while maintaining control over the content she shares.

"To me, sexy means being confident in your skin, being confident in who you are, as opposed to just the aesthetics of what you look like," she said. "I think sexiness comes from inside and feeling good in your skin. Back in 'Baywatch,' I was so young, and you're just figuring things out in your 20s. But now that I'm in my 50s, I feel like I've got it figured out. I feel sexy and confident in ways that make me feel empowered. I'm having fun and calling the shots."

As Eleniak continues to find success on OnlyFans, she's hoping to make a splash on "Baywatch" once again — decades after hanging up her iconic red swimsuit.

She is set to reprise the role in a guest appearance on Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot, which is scheduled to premiere Jan. 6, 2027.

World.title: Angel Reese after Atlanta Dream's disappointing WNBA Finals Game 7 loss: 'We'll be back'
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO – Angel Reese is already looking toward another championship run after the Atlanta Dream fell one win short of a title Saturday night.

"It is tough in the moment, but we’ll be back," Reese said after the Dream’s 68-63 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals at Chase Center.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

ANGEL REESE, ATLANTA DREAM FALL SHORT IN GAME 7 AS GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES WIN FIRST WNBA CHAMPIONSHIP

Reese finished with eight points on 3-for-7 shooting, 12 rebounds and four turnovers. She scored one point and did not attempt a field goal in the fourth quarter as Golden State secured its first championship.

Gabby Williams scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half and was named Finals MVP. Reese finished a fourth consecutive game with more turnovers than made baskets.

But afterward, Reese said she remained proud of her season and grateful for the teammates who helped Atlanta get within one victory of a championship.

"I’m really proud of the year that I had," Reese said. "I mean, I’ve done a lot of great things this year, but I wouldn’t be able to do it without this group."

"I’m a young player and I’m very vocal, but I think they really helped me a lot mature in different ways that I haven’t really been challenged," Reese said. "And they really challenged me to be better every single day."

Reese described a locker room where players supported one another’s accomplishments.

"There’s no egos in the locker room and nobody’s selfish," she said. "Like, everybody just wants to see each other succeed."

WNBA FINALS TEAMS END SEASON WITH ONE FINAL NATIONAL ANTHEM SNUB AS DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT

That, Reese argued, was a reason to believe Atlanta could eventually finish the job.

"When you have a team like that, I’ve been a part of some teams and I know what it takes to win a championship," she said. "And that’s the winning mindset."

Reese won a national championship at LSU in 2023 and was named the Final Four’s Most Outstanding Player. Famously, she taunted Iowa star Caitlin Clark as the clock wound down on her team's victory.

Reese combined for 51 points and 28 rebounds in Atlanta’s victories in Games 2 and 3, helping the team build a 2-1 series lead.

Before Game 4, she spoke about getting into Golden State’s head.

"They’re playing into my mental game where I can take their confidence and just try to do whatever to mess them up," Reese said.

USA SPORTS, NBC CLAIM RECORD WNBA FINALS RATINGS, BUT COMPARISONS LEAVE OUT IMPORTANT CONTEXT

Atlanta lost three of the next four games. Over that stretch, Reese averaged 9.5 points while shooting 12 for 45 (26.7%) and committing 19 turnovers. She continued to rebound, averaging 12.5 per game, but her scoring dropped sharply from the two victories that put Atlanta ahead.

The Dream forced Game 7 behind Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard’s combined 44 points in Thursday’s 80-69 win. In the deciding game, Atlanta led by nine midway through the third quarter before Williams took over.

Reese’s last field goal came with 2:12 remaining in the third. Her only point in the fourth came at the foul line with 18.6 seconds left.

Following the loss, she spoke about how much she had wanted to win for her teammates and Atlanta’s supporters.

"I love these girls. I love the coaches," Reese said. "I think it also sucks because our fan base back home poured into us so much this year, and we really wanted to do it for them, but we’re forever grateful."

She also expressed enthusiasm about another offseason working with Dream coach Karl Smesko.

"When individually you get better in the offseason, you get better collectively," Reese said, and then added that she was "looking forward to another year under Karl and his development and his system."

"Just because we didn’t win today doesn’t mean that we won’t be champions in the future," she said.

World.title: JONATHAN TURLEY: Pope Leo XIV casts ballot in US election, raising questions about foreign leaders voting
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

"So, the Pope doesn’t take sides. Prevost has another opinion, but we won’t do that now."

That funny quip from Pope Leo XIV, born Robert Prevost, referred to the historic game in Rome when the Villanova and Notre Dame basketball teams play each other.

However, a story this week raised a different question of when the Pope, as opposed to Prevost, can "take sides."

POPE LEO MEETS WITH CHICAGO'S FAR-LEFT MAYOR, GEORGE FLOYD'S FAMILY LAWYER AT THE VATICAN

This month, American-born Pope Leo XIV became the first pope ever to vote in a U.S. election.

A longtime Chicago native, the Pope mailed an absentee ballot to Will County, and the clerk’s office confirmed to Fox News Digital that "Robert Prevost is on the list of individuals who requested a Vote by Mail ballot."

There is no question that the pope can vote in the Holy See. Indeed, he is the ultimate and final vote in the Vatican, but can he actually vote in Illinois races — including the governor’s race involving incumbent Democrat J.B. Pritzker? The answer appears to be yes, but it raises some novel questions.

Now, as a threshold matter, I want to shed some bias. I was raised Catholic in Chicago. No, that is not the bias. There is that lingering conflict with the pope coming out as a White Sox fan. Many of us on the North Side hoped for a conversion to restore our faith in papal infallibility. However, he has remained entrenched in his South Side allegiance.

This column rises above that historic rivalry and does not suggest that White Sox fans can be challenged at the polls. Besides, I previously explained that the pope is a Cubs fan without knowing it.

CHICAGO MAYOR JOHNSON HOPES TO ENLIST POPE IN REPARATIONS FIGHT AFTER HE APOLOGIZED FOR 'SCOURGE OF SLAVERY'

Rather, what surprised me was that the head of a foreign state could vote in U.S. elections. The Vatican is a distinct nation with a diplomatic corps, a court system, a local government, and even a military in the form of the legendary Swiss Guards.

The Holy See Press Office declared, "Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen whenever he was eligible to do so. The Holy See Press Office confirms that, in keeping with this long-standing practice of civic participation, he has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago."

The Holy See maintains that Pope Leo retains his status as a U.S. citizen while serving as the head of a foreign nation. There is support for this position.

The State Department has maintained that dual citizens do not have to choose between their countries, though it does not expect them to serve as the head of another country.

"U.S. dual nationals owe allegiance to both the United States and the foreign country (or countries, if they are nationals of more than one). They are required to obey the laws of both countries, and either country has the right to enforce its laws. Claims of other countries upon U.S. dual-nationals may result in conflicting obligations under the laws of each country. U.S. dual nationals may also face restrictions in the U.S. consular protections available to U.S. nationals abroad, particularly in the country of their other nationality."

Notably, the State Department requires dual citizens to use a U.S. passport to enter the country. Does that mean that, when traveling as head of state, Pope Leo has to use a U.S. passport? Unlikely, but intriguing.

It strikes me as odd that a person can lead another country and still vote in U.S. elections. With all of those worried about Russian interference in elections, imagine if Putin could actually vote in U.S. elections. Obviously, Pope Leo is greatly loved and represents someone whose values are aligned with this country. Yet, he is also the head of state of a foreign nation.

SUPREME COURT RULES ON MAIL-IN BALLOTS RECEIVED AFTER ELECTION DAY

Under the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA), military personnel and citizens abroad are allowed to vote in U.S. elections. It is no longer considered an absentee vote requiring an excuse but simply a mail-in ballot.

The question is whether this right should be suspended when you assume a position in a foreign nation, let alone the head of such a nation. Dual citizenship has long been debated over the difficult questions raised by nations with opposing values and interests. However, being the head of a foreign government with potentially opposing interests and actions to the United States creates a curious status.

STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS

It turns out that when Gov. Pritzker met with the pope last year, he was actually meeting with a constituent and voter.

I am most surprised that the Vatican does not have a policy against such voting, though this is admittedly unprecedented. I would think that the head of the Catholic faith and the head of a foreign government would have a single national citizenship running to the Holy See. All popes are selected from the global faithful by the College of Cardinals and thus have national citizenship with other countries.

In assuming their positions, the cardinals "pledge and swear, as individuals and as a group, to observe faithfully and scrupulously the prescriptions contained in the Apostolic Constitution."

They also reaffirm that they are not subject to countervailing allegiances or pressures from outside the College: "And never to lend support or favour to any interference, opposition or any other form of intervention, whereby secular authorities of whatever order and degree or any group of people or individuals might wish to intervene in the election of the Roman Pontiff."

However, it is fascinating that, once elected, popes do not shed that status upon assuming the head of the Holy See.

It is an uncomfortable question since it also raises whether the head of a foreign government should have dual citizenship. Most people were legitimately thrilled, including myself, by the first American pope and can view this as an unlikely "one-off." However, it could just as easily happen with another nation and a dual citizen.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

At the risk of my own excommunication, it seems a worthy question for discussion, even though I doubt any politicians would relish such a debate.

For his part, Pope Leo stated before the Villanova-Notre Dame game that the pope will not take sides in the U.S. elections, but Robert Prevost will.

World.title: Wyoming mom reported missing after not picking up kids; sister, police search for answers
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Wyoming mother of two has been reported missing for days after she failed to pick up her children from an after-school program, prompting her sister to raise the alarm.

Kandice Gunter, 30, was last seen Thursday morning in Natrona County, according to the Casper Police Department. Her sister, Kayla Gunter, told Cowboy State Daily she reported her missing after Kandice did not collect her children, ages 9 and 6, from the Boys & Girls Club on Wednesday.

"That's why I started freaking out," Kayla told the paper. "It's totally out of character for her not to show up to get her kids."

FAMILY OF CRITICALLY MISSING DC MOTHER SAYS POLICE STILL TREATING HOME AS ACTIVE CRIME SCENE

Police said Gunter was last known to be traveling in a gray 2016 GMC Canyon pickup with a Wyoming temporary registration. Her cellphone was last located around 12:30 p.m. MT on Friday along Highway 387, near the Natrona County line.

The sisters last spoke by phone at 10:41 a.m. local time Wednesday. Kayla said the conversation gave no indication anything was wrong, and Gunter stopped answering calls afterward. The family was also told her phone pinged near Gillette around noon Wednesday, according to the report.

Gunter had reportedly moved from Nevada to Casper about a month earlier to be closer to her children. She had been staying with their father and helping care for them.

BAHAMIAN AUTHORITIES APPROVE SEARCH OF 25-FOOT-DEEP ZONE FLAGGED BY BRIAN HOOKER'S PHONE GPS DATA: SOURCES

"I looked so hard but there’s so much wide open spaces with one set of sad eyes hope you’re okay!! 14 years you’ve been in my life and can’t end it like this Kandice Gunter," Facebook user TK Kentopp posted early Saturday morning.

NEW YORK GRANDMOTHER VANISHES IN LAS VEGAS AS FAMILY GETS MYSTERIOUS TEXTS FROM HER PHONE ASKING FOR BITCOIN

In the days before she disappeared, Gunter posted on Facebook: "Success for me, happens in silence." She had also written in June about "focusing on a better me. Again," alongside a heart-mending emoji.

Kayla said the move appeared to be going well and her sister had not indicated she planned to leave or cut off contact. The sisters typically spoke by phone at least three times a day.

Gunter was last seen in person on the morning of Oct. 29 in Natrona County and was reported missing to police later that evening, the Casper Police Department said. She was last known to be traveling in a gray 2016 GMC Canyon pickup with Wyoming temporary registration. Her cellphone was last located along Highway 387, near the Natrona County line, around 12:30 p.m. Friday, Oct. 30.

Gunter is described as 5 feet 7 inches tall and weighing about 185 pounds, with black hair and blue eyes. She has a butterfly tattoo on her neck.

World.title: Poll: Voters demand change and a check on Trump, fueling a steep Democratic midterm advantage
World.content:
Democrats have a sizable advantage in the battle for control of Congress days ahead of the midterm elections, a new national NBC News poll finds, with voters clamoring for change and voicing all-time high disapproval of President Donald Trump.

Registered voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress by a 7-point margin, with Democrats leading Republicans 52%-45% — 2 points more than in last month’s poll. That includes a 21-point lead among independents.

Three percent of voters remained undecided as the poll was conducted from Oct. 28 to Oct. 30, and how they shift in the final days could tilt the outcome in dead-heat House and Senate races around the country. While the overall poll suggests that Democrats are poised to capitalize on a well of dissatisfaction with the president and his policies, there are findings that complicate the favorable picture.

When it comes to which party better handles key issues, voters give Republicans and Democrats about even marks, and the Democratic Party remains deeply unpopular. Meanwhile, Republican voters in GOP-held districts and in states Trump won in 2024 are sticking with their party — which is notable because much of the battle for control of both the House and Senate runs through this red terrain.

But there are also numerous signs of trouble for the GOP, with Trump at the center of a difficult political environment for Republicans and their slim majorities in both houses of Congress. The president’s disapproval rating has climbed to 60%, a new high mark in the NBC News poll across his two terms, and his approval rating stands at 40%.

After Trump won a second term in 2024 promising to bring down prices and restore the economic conditions of his first term, roughly 3 in 4 voters head into the midterms dissatisfied with the state of the economy. Nearly two-thirds of voters are calling for a change from the direction Trump has been leading the country, with 50% calling for “a great deal” of change, a new high mark in NBC News polling data.

And for the first time in 30 years of NBC News polling, more voters say they are dissatisfied with their financial situation (51%) than satisfied (49%).

“The Trump presidency can be summarized as the promise of two years ago and the peril of two days from now,” said Democratic pollster Jeff Horwitt of Hart Research Associates, who conducted the survey with Republican pollster Bill McInturff of Public Opinion Strategies.

Horwitt noted Trump returned to the White House after promising economic prosperity and peace. But now voters are expressing widespread concerns about the economy, with prices rising during the Iran war.

Amid those concerns, 64% of voters — including a third of Trump voters — say the president has fallen short of their expectations, with 34% saying he has lived up to them. Seventy percent of voters say the country is on the wrong track, a 9-point increase over the last year.

Voters continue to rank inflation and the cost of living as the most important issues facing the country, followed by government corruption, threats to democracy and immigration and border security.

“Democrats are in total control of the 2026 issue agenda,” said McInturff, the Republican pollster, noting that only voters who think immigration is a top issue are breaking for his party right now.

Democrats have a 1-point advantage on which party would better control inflation, a slight decline from September but still a warning sign for the GOP, which led on the issue in 2024. Republicans have a 2-point advantage on the economy, a marked decline from the party’s double-digit advantage on the issue in recent years.

Voters are also signaling that they are fired up about the midterms, with 70% ranking themselves as a “9” or “10” on a 10-point scale of interest in the election. Democrats have a 12-point advantage among those most-engaged voters, while Republicans have a 2-point edge among voters who are less interested in the election.

Self-described MAGA Republicans also say they’re significantly more interested in the election than Republicans who don’t identify with the MAGA wing, as Trump and his party push to turn out voters who typically sit out midterm elections.

That dynamic could be one reason why Republicans have leaned into culture war arguments in key races, attacking Democrats on transgender issues. The new poll shows a potential limitation of that strategy: Democrats have a 5-point advantage on the question of which party would better handle transgender issues, despite those Republican attacks.

It’s not all good news for Democrats, and the poll contains fresh signs that a number of voters are pushing back on the GOP, as opposed to falling in love with the Democratic Party, which remains deeply unpopular.

Just 29% of voters view the Democratic Party positively, while 38% have positive views of the Republican Party. Around half of voters have negative views of both parties.

Still, some voters who are wary of Democrats are still planning to support them this year.

“Republicans have proven that they are not to be trusted. So I would rather see the balance of power shift, than maintain one party’s control,” one poll respondent from Texas, who voted for Trump in 2024 and is supporting Democrats for Congress this year, said in an expanded response.

“I don’t trust Republicans or Democrats, really,” the man added.

Republican disappointment

Frustrations among voters like that man from Texas, who backed Trump in 2024 and typically backs Republicans, are dragging down the president and GOP candidates this year.

Republicans are torn on whether the country is moving in the right direction (48%), or the wrong direction (43%). One year ago, Republicans said the country was going in the right direction, 75%-24%.

Now, a majority of Republicans (53%) are dissatisfied with the state of the economy. And 37% of Trump’s own party believe he’s fallen short of his promises.

Trump still maintains an important hold on his base, with near-unanimous job approval (93%) among Republicans who say they support the MAGA movement. But he’s slipped significantly with Republicans who don’t consider themselves part of the MAGA movement: 54% of them approve and 46% disapprove of his performance. Meanwhile, 20% of those non-MAGA Republicans say they prefer to see Democrats control Congress after this election.

The president has seen other important voting blocs drift away, too.

His net approval rating has dropped 18 points among white voters without college degrees compared to the first NBC News poll of his second term, in 2025. He’s also seen significant declines among young voters and Latino voters, groups that he overperformed with on his way back to the White House in 2024.

One of Republicans’ big advantages in 2026 is a favorable political map: Democrats have to win back districts and states Trump won in 2024 to take back Congress. In the Senate, they need to win at least two states Trump carried by double-digit margins.

But the president’s approval rating is underwater in states he won in 2024: 53% of registered voters there disapprove of his job performance, while 47% approve. In March 2025, his approval rating in those states was 10 points higher.

Democratic warning signs

There are some warning signs for Democrats, on top of the fact that a lower share of voters have positive views of the Democratic Party compared to the Republican Party.

The fight for control of the House and especially the Senate will take place in Trump-won areas, and Republicans are leading on the congressional ballot in GOP-held districts and in states Trump won in 2024. The big question is whether that’s enough to withstand shifts in some key places.

Government corruption has been a central theme of Democrats’ message this year, but voters narrowly trust Republicans to better handle the issue by 5 points. Even so, Democrats are leading on the congressional ballot among the 28% of voters who do not trust either party on the issue.

Republican leaders in Congress are also slightly better off than their Democratic counterparts, but that’s mostly because voters don’t know how to feel about them.

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., has the highest positive rating of congressional leaders: 24% have positive views of him and 34% have negative views. Just 10% of voters have positive views of Johnson’s counterpart across the Capitol, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, while 22% view him negatively.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries is viewed positively by 18% of voters and negatively by 35%. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, who’s led Democrats in the body for almost a decade, is far better defined — to his detriment. Just 13% of voters view him positively, and 53% view him negatively.

“It’s not great for the Democrats … for 2028,” said McInturff, the Republican pollster, when asked about the low marks for Democrats. “But I don’t see it as a barrier for how well they can do in 2026 when midterms are about Trump and these economic numbers.”

Half of voters have negative views of tech billionaire Elon Musk, who has emerged as one of the most prolific Republican donors in the country over the last two years, while 34% view him positively.

Voters are more split about a pair of prominent progressives, Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. Sanders is more popular: 41% view him positively and 42% view him negatively, while Ocasio-Cortez’s numbers stand at 31%-42%.

Democrats hold a significant lead in the battle for Congress despite those factors. But there are indications throughout the poll that the party’s lead is propped up strongly by anti-Republican sentiment, not warm feelings for Democrats.

Voters who want Democratic control of Congress are divided between whether their vote is more in favor of Democrats or driven more by opposition to Republicans.

“Get your s--- together, Democrats,” an Ohio Democratic woman said when asked what message she wanted to send with her vote this year. “I’m voting for you, but work it out.”

The NBC News poll surveyed 1,000 registered voters Oct. 28-30 via a mix of telephone interviews and an online survey sent via text message. The margin of error is plus or minus 3.1 percentage points.

World.title: Democrats in key battlegrounds throw Joe Biden under the bus on the border
World.content:
WASHINGTON — Democratic candidates in 2026 battleground races are directly criticizing Joe Biden’s handling of border security when he was president, seeking to neutralize a political vulnerability and signaling a new path for the party on the thorny issue.

Candidates are throwing the ex-president under the bus on border policy in key states that will decide control of the Senate and some battleground House races across the country.

“I called out Joe Biden for failing us on the border,” Texas’ Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico says in a recent ad airing in the closing stretch of his neck-and-neck race against Republican Ken Paxton. He also criticized Biden in July for having “failed us on our southern border” as he rolled out his own border security plan.

He’s not alone.

In Kansas, a longtime Republican stronghold, Democrat Adam Hamilton criticized Biden in a recent debate with Republican Sen. Roger Marshall.

“I want to be crystal clear, first of all: Immigration at the border under Biden was a disaster. That is how we ended up where we are today,” he said. “Second, what we did in response to that has been a disaster for people across the state of Kansas.”

Hamilton, like other Democrats in areas that voted for Trump in 2024, paired their critique of Biden with criticism that the current president has gone too far on enforcement. Polls show many Americans have soured on Trump’s handling of the issue in the wake of immigration officers fatally shooting two Americans in Minnesota and one in Maine this year.

Still, the comments reflect a recognition that the issue of border security remains a vulnerability for Democrats as Republicans continue to accuse them of promoting “open borders” in a bid to mobilize their base and win swing voters. Biden’s ratings on the issue tanked amid a surge in migrant crossings during his presidency, which Trump successfully weaponized in 2024.

Entering office in 2021, Biden inherited a Covid-era migration surge that intensified in the United States after he made good on his pledge to roll back Trump-era policies and restrictions, allowing more asylum-seekers to stay in the country as their cases were being considered. The collective result was a huge spike in border crossings that became associated with the Biden presidency and brought down his approval ratings.

Even as Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 38%, polls show border security continues to be one of his highest-polling issues, although that number has fallen from the highs of his early second term.

“The Biden administration failed at the border,” Democratic House candidate Paige Cognetti said at a debate Thursday night.

Cognetti, who is vying to unseat Rep. Rob Bresnahan, R-Pa., in a highly competitive Scranton-area working-class district, later added: “The Biden administration did fail. We need to make sure that the border is secure. It’s a good thing that it is. We do need to make sure that the pathways to citizenship are there.”

In South Carolina, Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews said in a debate, “Democrats have failed on the border.”

Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said it’s “very smart” for candidates to distance themselves from Biden and that “there’s nobody contesting that interpretation” that he blundered on the border.

In the 2024 election, “immigration was playing a major, major role, and it was energizing Republicans. And it was the best issue among swing voters for Republicans,” she said. “ICE has gone too far, and that has backfired now.”

She added that the “best messaging” on immigration is “some control for the border plus a humanitarian process for immigration.”

Iowa’s Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek traveled more than 800 miles to Laredo, Texas, to film an ad at the border touting his support for tougher enforcement.

“I came to the border to meet firsthand with the people who work to keep it secure. What happens down here affects us up in Iowa, so we’ve got to address it,” Turek says in the ad. “I voted with Republicans to allow law enforcement to arrest and deport criminals.”

Weeks earlier, he released another ad speaking to Iowans and vowing that he would “work with anyone” to fix immigration — “including President Trump, to secure the border.”

Closer to the border, Democrat Johnny Garcia is trying to win Texas’ redrawn and Republican-friendly 35th Congressional District against GOP nominee Carlos De La Cruz.

Garcia criticized Trump’s ICE raids as detrimental to the economy. But at a recent forum, he also blamed Biden’s policies for failures at the border and referred to a fatal smuggling conspiracy in 2022 that led to the deaths of dozens of people.

“We’ve also gotten to see, unfortunately, how Biden got it wrong on the border,” Garcia said. “I’ll admit that every single day. We got to see one of the largest migrant fatalities in this district in south San Antonio, with 53 migrants that were locked in a trailer.”

“So we can’t afford to just turn a blind eye to our border,” he added. “But at the same time, we can’t turn a blind eye to what we’re seeing happening on our streets.”

World.title: Alaska officials ask judge to deny DOJ’s ‘impossible’ demand to set aside ballots
World.content:
The Republican-led state government in Alaska implored a federal judge on Saturday to permanently dismiss the Trump administration’s lawsuit seeking to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate race if GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses.

“The United States’ opposition provides no reason for this Court to entertain this meritless lawsuit any longer,” the filing said, adding that “the relief demanded is inappropriate and not even possible given Alaskan voters’ vital right to ballot secrecy.”

The filing from Alaska officials comes just three days before Election Day and as the judge is expected to rule on whether to dismiss the lawsuit or allow it to continue.

The Trump administration has claimed that Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting a retired teacher, Dan J. Sullivan, with the same name as Dan S. Sullivan to run in the race, creating confusion that it says will unfairly take away votes intended for the incumbent. Peltola has denied the allegations.

The Trump administration filed a lawsuit on Oct. 22 against local election officials, arguing that the results of the competitive Senate race should not be certified unless Dan S. Sullivan is declared the winner.

Alaska officials on Saturday criticized the Trump administration’s claim that it has standing to intervene in the election, as election certification is left up to the states.

The filing noted that the Alaska Supreme Court approved the second Sullivan’s name to be on the ballot months ago and that “state officials carefully designed the ballot to minimize voter confusion.”

Alaska officials also took aim at the Justice Department’s proposal for “segregating” ballots that rank Dan J. Sullivan, writing, “this unexplained idea makes no sense.”

“No matter how the ballots are physically stored, it will be easy to tell which ballots rank Daniel J.,” the filing said. “If the United States means something different — as it seems to — its ballot segregation proposal is both disturbing and impossible.”

The Alaska attorney general’s office asked the judge to “immediately dismiss this lawsuit with prejudice and allow state officials to conduct the general election — including ballot counting and certification — free from unwarranted federal interference.”

The Trump administration amended its complaint this week to cite a new story in The New York Times, which reported that Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan and that Peltola herself was aware of the situation. The Times story citied a former campaign manager who later attempted to retract her statements.

At a rally Friday night, Peltola told a crowd of her supporters that she was “so deeply offended by these accusations about having any involvement with anyone else’s candidacy.”

“I want fewer candidates in the primary. I’m not out soliciting more competition,” Peltola said, adding she did “not need any help” defeating Dan S. Sullivan.

Dan S. Sullivan took aim at Peltola in a Fox News interview on Saturday, saying that “there’s no way Peltola doesn’t know about” the scheme to recruit Dan J. Sullivan.

“It’s deception. But at its worst, it’s disdain for us Alaskans,” he said. “Think about what they did. They’re trying to make sure that Alaskans throw away their vote.”

World.title: Golden State Valkyries defeat Atlanta Dream for franchise’s first WNBA title
World.content:
In only their second season in existence, the Golden State Valkyries are WNBA champions.

The Valkyries won their first-ever title on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Forward Gabby Williams led with 30 points.

Confetti rained down onto the court as the crowd erupted in cheers, and the Valkyries celebrated the historic victory.

00:43 Valkyries win their first WNBA title 00:00 00:00

“I love moments like this,” Williams said after the final buzzer. “Nat told me to be patient in the first half. It was hard, but I listened to her. She’s right as always and she got us here,” she said, referring to head coach Natalie Nakase.

Williams was named the Finals MVP following her stunning performance, scoring more points than anybody in a half in WNBA postseason history. Though she scored just two points in the first half, she rallied with 15 points in the third quarter and 13 in the fourth.

Accepting her award, she said, “I wasn’t gonna lose on Halloween.”

World.title: Stores looted in German riots as Gen Z activists protest living costs, military service
World.content:
Rioters looted stores and set fires to barricades in Frankfurt on Saturday as protests across Germany demanded lower living costs and better education.

Tens of thousands of people across more than 30 cities took to the streets, including in the capital Berlin and financial hub Frankfurt, in protests organized by the campaign group Gen Z regelt (Gen Z takes charge).

The activists demand spending on schools, climate protection and housing, and are against plans to return to mandatory military service.

But the largely peaceful protests, which coincided with Halloween and came weeks after some of the worst rioting in decades erupted in neighboring France, turned violent in some areas.

“In ⁠the city centre, windows have been smashed at several shops,” Frankfurt police said on X. “Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at the emergency services. We urge all bystanders to avoid the ​city center or to leave the area.”
