World.title: Anbar launches expanded afforestation campaign to combat desertification
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Contemporary Environmental Team in Al-Baghdadi subdistrict, Anbar Governorate, has launched an afforestation campaign under the direct supervision of the Anbar Environment Directorate and the Hit Environmental Unit, in coordination with the local administrations of Al-Baghdadi and Jubba subdistricts and the Al-Baghdadi Municipal Directorate.

The initiative falls under broader Ministry of Environment efforts to execute sustainable ecological initiatives across the governorate.

Ahmed Al-Mahmoud, head of the Contemporary Environmental Team in Al-Baghdadi, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the campaign involves planting diverse climate-resilient tree and shrub varieties suited to local environmental conditions. The project aims to expand green cover, enhance air and environmental quality, and combat desertification across western Iraq.

Al-Mahmoud stressed the critical role of inter-agency cooperation among municipal departments, local administrative units, and grassroots volunteer initiatives in executing successful afforestation projects. He emphasized that these greening efforts should be continuous rather than seasonal, noting that the campaign will expand into other areas of Anbar Governorate in upcoming phases.

He also highlighted that long-term campaign viability requires continuous care, systematic irrigation networks, and ongoing maintenance to guarantee sapling survival, transforming planted zones into sustainable green spaces capable of restoring ecological balance and mitigating climate vulnerabilities.

World.title: US dollar edges down in Baghdad, holds steady in Erbil at 167,900 IQD
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged down slightly across Baghdad’s main currency exchanges on Saturday, October 31, 2026, while holding steady in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, at the opening of the weekly trading cycle.

According to market data, wholesale rates at Baghdad’s central Al-Kifah and Al-Harithiya exchanges slipped to 167,900 dinars per $100, marking a slight decline from 168,000 dinars recorded at the close of trading on Thursday.

Retail exchange desks across local markets in Baghdad saw retail selling rates stabilize at 168,500 dinars against buying bids of 167,500 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, parallel trading counters maintained flat levels, quoting selling prices at 167,750 dinars alongside purchase bids of 167,650 dinars per $100.

World.title: Iraqi government denies 16 trillion dinar foreign loan reports to cover deficit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi federal government denied reports on Friday, October 30, 2026, alleging that Baghdad intends to borrow 16 trillion Iraqi dinars from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, China, Germany, and France to plug the sovereign budget deficit, confirming that state fiscal strategy relies on deploying domestic revenues to sustain public expenditures.

In statements delivered to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Government Spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi stated that widely circulated claims regarding foreign borrowing arrangements to offset budget shortfalls are entirely unfounded.

Al-Aboudi affirmed that there is no fiscal necessity for external borrowing, citing sustained crude export performance and favorable revenue flow.

Al-Aboudi explained that the executive administration adheres to a disciplined economic policy centered on optimizing state revenues to fund public commitments and sovereign operational requirements.

He noted that elevated crude export ceilings have bolstered treasury inflows, enabling the government to maximize available financial resources and fulfill state obligations without turning to foreign debt.

World.title: Health Minister highlights global partnerships at 6th Iraq International Health Expo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Minister of Health, Abdul-Hussein Aziz Al-Mousawi, underscored on Friday, October 30, 2026, the imperative of expanding international healthcare partnerships, transferring advanced medical technologies, and upgrading clinical healthcare delivery across the country.

Speaking during his inspection tour on the third day of the 6th Iraq International Health Exhibition and Conference, Al-Mousawi highlighted the exhibition’s role as a platform for exchanging technical expertise, acquiring advanced healthcare systems, and driving modernization across state and private healthcare infrastructure, according to a ministerial statement reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The minister commended the wide international turnout at this year’s edition, which brought together 375 healthcare corporations representing 24 countries.

Al-Mousawi noted that the significant global participation reflects growing commercial confidence in Iraq’s healthcare sector and opens viable investment pathways with international pharmaceutical and biomedical institutions.

During the walkthrough, Al-Mousawi inspected newly introduced medical diagnostic devices, surgical machinery, and specialized pharmaceutical supplies, engaging with company representatives and technical specialists on modern clinical solutions, hospital management technologies, and localized healthcare supply-chain integration.

World.title: International Digi Yatra trials to begin at 7 airports for Indian nationals this year for wider rollout in 2027: Government
World.content:
File photo: India will trial Digi Yatra for international passengers at seven airports over the next three months

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Travelling abroad from India could soon be a seamless experience just like taking domestic flights with Digi Yatra (DY). India will hold trials for international passengers at seven airports in the three months of this year, allowing eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use DY at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.The aviation ministry said trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. âEligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, security hold areas (SHA) and boarding gates, wherever the required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027,â it said in a statement.To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based âverifiable credentialâ (VC) through DY mobile application. âThe process involves scanning the machine readable zone (MRZ) of e-passport, reading the embedded chip using the near field communication (NFC) feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. The credential is stored in the passengerâs Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials,â the statement said.The facility will complement, and not replace, existing travel processes. âPassengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all mandatory airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities,â it added.IndiGo said eligible passengers can upload their boarding pass to the Digi Yatra app. After completing mandatory document verification at airline check-in counter, they can proceed through the security hold area and boarding gates using DY biometric face authentication.IndiGo chief digital and information officer Neetan Chopra said: âAt IndiGo, we are committed to redefining air travel by making it more seamless, efficient, and customer centric, and we believe that technology can be a key catalyst in this evolution. Having been a key part of the technical proof of concept earlier this year, we are pleased to partner with Digi Yatra for the launch of these international passenger trials. Expanding secure digital identity and biometric technologies to international departures is a significant step forward for Indian aviation. We are committed to delivering a seamless travel experience for our customers at every touchpoint. The successful deployment of this technology marks an important step in reimagining the airport experience, combining enhanced security, convenience and operational efficiency. As the aviation industry continues to evolve, such innovations will play a key role in shaping the future of passenger travel.âDigi Yatra Foundation CEO Suresh Khadakbhavi said: âDigi Yatra has demonstrated how digital identity can simplify domestic air travel. With the start of international passenger trials, we are taking an important step towards extending this experience to eligible Indian nationals travelling internationally.Interoperability with global frameworks such as IATAâs One ID and ICAOâs Public Key Directory (PKD) will be an important part of this journey, helping explore how e-passport-based digital credentials can enable more seamless and secure passenger journeys across borders, while keeping passenger consent, privacy and security central to the experience. âDigi Yatra platform has over 2.6 crore users at present and has enabled more than 11 crore journeys across 39 domestic airports, serving domestic airlines. A further 25 domestic airports are planned to be covered by 2027. âThe aviation ministry remains committed to leveraging technology to improve airport operations and facilitate seamless air travel, in line with govt's vision of Digital India and ease of flying. â

World.title: CBI extradites Mahadev App kingpin Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a major breakthrough against transnational organized crime, CBI in coordination with other Central agencies, has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, the promoter and alleged kingpin of the Mahadev App illegal online betting syndicate, from the Sultanate of Oman.

A special CBI team travelled to Muscat, took custody of Chandrakar, and escorted him back to India. Following a mandatory medical examination and the acquisition of a transit remand, he will be taken to Raipur and produced before the CBI Special Judge Monday.

Chandrakar is wanted in two CBI cases, in which chargesheets have already been filed, as well as an Enforcement Directorate (ED) case where a prosecution complaint has been submitted and several properties in India and abroad have been attached.

The investigation into the Mahadev Online Book cases was taken up by the CBI at the request of the Chhattisgarh government.

The probe revealed that the syndicate operated as one of the country's largest illegal online betting networks run from outside India, facilitating unlawful betting on cricket, football, card games, and other events through a widespread system of franchised "panels" and "branches."

Proceeds from the illegal betting network were funneled through numerous mule bank accounts, layered via multiple transactions, and moved overseas through hawala channels.





CBI investigations also established that a portion of the illicit funds was used to pay protection money to public servants to ensure the unhindered operation of the syndicate.

Chargesheets in the matter have been filed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, provisions of the Indian Penal Code relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating, and forgery, as well as the Chhattisgarh Gambling (Prohibition) Act, with Chandrakar named as a key accused.

Chandrakar was initially located and detained by the Royal Oman Police following a Red Corner Notice issued against him. Subsequent extradition proposals, accompanied by gathered evidence, were submitted by the CBI and ED, and pursued in close coordination with Indian government agencies, the Interpol National Central Bureau, and Omani authorities.

The CBI expressed gratitude to the Government of the Sultanate of Oman and the Royal Oman Police for their cooperation, highlighting the strong bilateral relations and mutual commitment to combating international crime. The extradition represents a key milestone in India's ongoing efforts to hold foreign-based fugitives accountable under Indian law, CBI said.

World.title: 'Vote chori, yes papa': Mamata takes 'Johny Johny' jibe at CEC Gyanesh - video
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Bengal chief minister

took a swipe at chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar through a parody of the popular children's rhyme 'Johny Johny Yes Papa' at a rally in Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday.

Leading the crowd in a series of call-and-response slogans, Mamata accused the

of stealing votes, undermining democracy and denying people's rights. She also mocked the CEC by calling him 'Vanish Kumar', alleging that more than one crore votes had been removed in West Bengal during the election process.

In an apparent reference to the alleged manipulation of votes and election results, Mamata adapted the familiar rhyme to target the BJP and the chief election commissioner.

She asked the crowd a series of questions, with the audience responding in the style of the nursery rhyme.

"Vanish vanish? Yes, Papa!

Vote theft? Yes, Papa!

Democracy theft? Yes, Papa!

Who looted? BJP Papa!

And who is behind the robbery? BJP Papa!

Job theft? BJP Papa!

Dignity theft? BJP Papa!

Farmer's respect theft? BJP Papa!

Destroying laborers' homes? BJP Papa!

Do we want BJP? No, Papa!

Do we want 'Vanish Kumar'? No, Papa!"

The TMC leader also directly targeted Gyanesh Kumar, using the nickname 'Vanish Kumar' to accuse him of making votes disappear.





She alleged that the Election Commission had not only removed votes but also undermined the counting process in the state.

"Now central... 'Vanish Kumar' Ji (referring mockingly to an official), you didn't just make votes vanish, you made the entire counting process vanish! By centrally hijacking, you removed more than 1 crore votes in our Bengal! Before the votes... we didn't lose, we were made to lose! We will take revenge for this through politics, we will fight through democracy, we will fight!"

Mamata also accused the BJP of using the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise to benefit itself.

Taking a dig at the name of the exercise, she offered her own interpretation of the acronym and alleged that it was being used to provide political relief to the ruling party.

"What does SIR mean? Special Incentives... meaning Special Incentive Relief to a political party like the BJP! What haven't they been given? Now EVMs were looted! Democracy was looted! The Constitution was looted! Rights were looted! Now our election counting was looted!"

Calling West Bengal a victim of the circumstances surrounding the SIR exercise, Mamata said her party would continue to resist what she described as an attempt to undermine the state's electoral rights.

"I want to say... Bengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not back down! We will give our lives, we will fight! We will not back down, our Bengal was looted! From Delhi... we will not loot, we will save democracy, we will bring democracy back."

She went on to accuse the BJP of looting institutions, places of worship and public resources. Referring to alleged incidents involving temples, mosques and gurdwaras, she questioned whether such actions could continue unchecked.

"What hasn't been looted? Temples were looted! Ram Janmabhoomi's money was looted! In our Bengal, temple money was looted, temple money was looted! Gurudwaras... they enter Gurudwaras wearing boots! We have never heard of such a thing! Mosques were looted, Waqf property was looted, the Treasury was looted! What wasn't looted? Dignity was looted, democracy was looted, the Constitution was looted! Will things keep going on like this?"

Mamata also alleged that the BJP was using police personnel and central agencies for political purposes. Appealing to police officers not to become involved in party activities, she said:

"Using the police, you make them do party work, political organization work! Police became their comrade... BJP comrade! The BJP has no other organization! That is why I want to say, police personnel are like our brothers and sisters... Agencies, don't work with BJP!"

Taking another swipe at the BJP's slogan of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas', she contrasted it with what she described as the consequences of the party's rule.

"You used to sayâ'Development for all', 'Together with all, development for all'! And now people sayâ'Together with BJP, destruction for all'!"

Earlier in her address, Mamata expressed solidarity with the CJP leadership, Gen Z, students and young people, while acknowledging the presence of opposition leaders, lawyers and civil society groups at the rally. She named several opposition leaders and lawyers who had attended the gathering and praised their efforts.

"...actually, the Leftist party, all are present here, from Mehbooba Mufti to everybody, and the NGOs, and the social team, who are civil society. They are really trying their best. I am congratulating [and extending] my solidarity to CZP leadership and Gen Z, all the students, and the young generation for their solidarity, for their support, for their fighting."

For many Indians, the day begins with a cup of milky chai, followed by breakfast cooked in ghee. Lunch may come with a bowl of curd and paneer on the menu, while a Sunday meal is often incomplete without chicken curry.These familiar food habits are so deeply woven into everyday life that giving up all animal-derived products can seem like a difficult choice.But for people who turn vegan, the change goes beyond replacing meat with vegetables. It means rethinking everyday ingredients, from milk and butter to honey, as well as choices involving clothing, cosmetics and other products.âThere are alternatives for practically everything. You can make curd at home using plant milk, use tofu instead of paneer, and use different nut and soy milks,â says Sarahana, who has been vegan since 2018.On World Vegan Day, observed on November 1, the question is not just why people choose veganism, but what it takes to follow the lifestyle.According to The Vegan Society, veganism is a way of living that seeks to exclude, as far as possible and practicable, all forms of animal exploitation and cruelty.While a vegan diet avoids meat, fish, eggs, dairy and honey, the lifestyle also extends to products made from animals, those tested on animals and activities that use animals for entertainment.For some, the decision is rooted in animal welfare; for others, environmental concerns or health considerations play a role.But the experiences of vegans show that the transition is as much about changing everyday habits as it is about changing one's perspective.India has a long tradition of vegetarian food, but veganism goes a step further by excluding all animal-derived products, including milk, curd, ghee, paneer and honey.According to estimates compiled by World Population Review, around 9% of India's population followed a vegan diet in 2021, amounting to an estimated 121.5 million people. The country also has a substantial vegetarian population, reflecting its diverse food traditions.However, the figure should be treated as an estimate rather than a definitive count, as veganism surveys often rely on self-reported responses and vary in methodologies.A vegan diet does not necessarily mean giving up familiar Indian food or relying on expensive, imported alternatives. Dal, rice, roti, rajma, chole, idli, dosa, poha, upma and vegetable dishes can all be part of a vegan diet, provided they are prepared without animal-derived ingredients.Utkarsh Garg, a representative of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA), says their meals are a mix of familiar Indian dishes and plant-based alternatives.âBreakfast is usually a protein smoothie bowl or soaked oats, although Iâm definitely not above a plate of poha, chhole-kulche or one enormous aloo paratha when the mood strikes!ââLunch and dinner usually include things like tofu, soybeans, dals, rajma and plenty of vegetables. My current obsession is tempeh. I seem to be finding increasingly creative excuses to put it into everything I eat.ââAs for living without milk, paneer, curd or ghee, I genuinely donât find it difficult anymore. There are so many vegan alternatives available now, and many things are surprisingly easy and inexpensive to make at home as well.â Utkarsh said.Sarahana says she relies largely on everyday Indian food rather than packaged substitutes.âAs for food, my everyday diet is actually quite simple and Indian. Dal, rice, roti, vegetables, chickpeas, rajma, seasonal produce and different legumes. There are so many naturally plant-based foods available in India. You donât need expensive imported alternatives or packaged vegan products to survive without dairy.âThere are alternatives for practically everything. You can make curd at home using plant milk, use tofu instead of paneer, and use different nut and soy milks. Ghee is essentially clarified butter, and personally, I donât feel the need to replace it.âThe distinction is important. A vegan diet does not require a direct substitute for every non-vegan food. It can instead be built around naturally plant-based ingredients that are already widely used in Indian kitchens.For Utkarsh, the decision began in childhood. Watching a chicken being slaughtered made them connect the food on their plate with the animal it came from. He turned vegetarian that day and later went vegan.âFor me, veganism has always been about animals. Iâve loved animals for as long as I can remember. While most kids my age were watching Cartoon Network or Pogo, I was glued to National Geographic, completely fascinated by dogs, cats, cows, snakes, and pretty much every animal I came across,â Utkarsh said.As he learnt more about animal exploitation, vegetarianism no longer felt enough. âMy love for animals naturally led me to veganism. Iâve been vegan for four years now, and honestly, it is one of the best decisions I have ever made. More than changing what I eat or wear, it has changed the way I look at the world and my place in it.âFor Sarahana, the turning point came in 2018, when she watched a video of a pregnant cow being slaughtered after she was no longer productive for the dairy industry.âMy decision came from questioning something very basic: why do we, as human beings, consider ourselves superior to other animals? Why do we love some animals, consider some family, see some as entertainment, and others as food?â she said.While studying gender, Sarahana began drawing parallels between the exploitation of women's bodies and that of female animals in the dairy industry.âHow can I study feminism, gender and the exploitation of female bodies and not extend that understanding beyond human beings? How can I talk about patriarchy and exploitation while continuing to pay an industry that repeatedly impregnates female animals, takes away their babies and exploits their reproductive systems?â she said.Coming from a Dalit community, Sarahana also views veganism through the lens of social justice, questioning how societies decide whose lives are valued.âWe love cats and dogs, welcome them into our homes and call them family, but we look at chickens, goats and buffaloes and see food. We have created categories of animals that deserve affection and animals that can be exploited,â she added.One common perception is that veganism is an expensive lifestyle, largely because plant-based milk, meat substitutes and other packaged alternatives can cost more than conventional products. However, both Utkarsh and Sarahana say that a vegan diet need not depend on these products.Utkarsh points out that many Indian staples are naturally plant-based. âIndia is one of the easiest places in which to eat vegan, because so much of the food we already know and love either naturally contains no animal-derived ingredients or can be veganised with ridiculously small changes.âThink about dal, rajma, chole, idli, dosa, poha, upma, roti, sabzis, rice dishes and countless regional foods. Veganism doesnât have to mean buying an expensive imported mock meat or drinking a fancy packaged plant milk every morning. Those products are great if you enjoy them, but they arenât what veganism depends on.âSarahana agrees that the bigger challenge is often social rather than financial.âI donât think being vegan in India is inherently expensive. Our traditional food already has so many affordable plant-based options. What can become expensive is the packaged vegan alternatives, not the basic diet itself. The bigger challenge is social conditioning. At family gatherings, weddings or even casual conversations, you constantly have to explain why you donât consume something that everyone else considers normal. âBoth say their families initially had questions and reservations. Utkarsh says their family is now supportive and has started incorporating more vegan foods and products into their lives. Sarahana, meanwhile, says she continues to face comments that she has been âbrainwashedâ.Veganism is often associated with better health, but a plant-based diet is not automatically a balanced one. Its nutritional value depends on the foods included and whether essential nutrients are adequately supplied.Dt Gausiya Aziz, consultant and head of nutrition and dietetics at SPARSH Hospital, Yelahanka, says a well-planned vegan diet can support cardiovascular and metabolic health.âResearch suggests that plant-based dietary patterns rich in fibre, antioxidants and unsaturated fats can help lower LDL cholesterol, improve blood pressure and support healthy weight management. They may also reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes,â she says.However, claims that veganism automatically prevents cancer, reverses chronic diseases or guarantees a longer life are exaggerated, she cautions. Health outcomes depend on overall diet quality, lifestyle and individual medical conditions.A key concern is meeting nutritional requirements. Vitamin B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc, omega-3 fatty acids and protein need particular attention.Vitamin B12 is especially important because reliable natural plant-based sources are limited. Fortified foods or supplements may therefore be necessary.Aziz recommends a varied diet containing whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruits, nuts and seeds, along with appropriate supplementation and regular nutritional assessment.Utkarsh says he pay close attention to their nutritional needs and take vitamin B12 supplements.âI am also quite particular about my nutrition. I take my B12 regularly and pay attention to vitamin D and other essential nutrients. B12 supplementation is important for vegans, and these supplements are accessible at pharmacies,â he said.The PETA representative added that he has noticed less bloating since turning vegan and feel healthier, but stresses that dietary planning matters.âOf course, I think any diet needs to be properly planned rather than treated as automatically healthy simply because it carries a particular label. For me, veganism has actually made me more conscious of what I eat and what my body needs.âAziz also warns that highly processed vegan foods are not necessarily healthy. Packaged snacks, meat substitutes and desserts can contain high amounts of sodium, refined carbohydrates, added sugars and saturated fats. She advises prioritising minimally processed foods and checking nutritional labels.âChildren, pregnant women and older adults have specific nutritional requirements that demand careful consideration before adopting a vegan diet. During childhood, adequate energy, protein, calcium, iron, vitamin B12 and vitamin D are essential for growth and development. Pregnant women must additionally ensure sufficient folate, iodine, choline and omega-3 fatty acids to support maternal health and fetal development. Older adults should prioritise protein intake, calcium and vitamin D to preserve muscle strength and bone health. Vitamin B12 supplementation is particularly important across these groups,â Aziz added.Nutritionist Aziz also recommends consulting a qualified dietitian or healthcare professional before making significant dietary changes.Animal welfare is not the only reason people choose veganism. Environmental concerns are also part of the conversation.Aziz says vegan diets generally have a lower environmental footprint than diets containing substantial amounts of animal products, particularly red meat and dairy.Plant-based food production typically requires less agricultural land and generates fewer greenhouse gas emissions than livestock farming. It can also reduce pressure on biodiversity and freshwater resources.However, the environmental impact varies with farming methods, transportation, processing and food waste. Choosing locally available, seasonal and minimally processed plant foods can help reduce the footprint further.For Utkarsh, the values behind veganism are also connected to ideas of compassion and non-violence.âWe grow up hearing about ahimsa and vasudhaiva kutumbakam, the idea that the world is one family. To me, animals shouldnât be excluded from that circle of compassion simply because they belong to another species,â he said.Going vegan involves more than changing what is on the plate. It can mean checking product labels, asking about ingredients when eating out and finding alternatives to everyday items.Some medications and personal-care products may also contain animal-derived ingredients, making it important to check rather than assume that a product is vegan.For someone considering the transition, Utkarsh suggests starting by understanding where everyday products come from.âFor anyone considering going vegan because they care about animals, I would say: start by looking. Look honestly at where our milk, meat, eggs, leather, wool, silk, cosmetics and entertainment come from.ââOnce I did that, veganism stopped feeling like something I was âgiving upâ. It started feeling like the most natural extension of something I had believed all along.âSarahana says the idea is to extend compassion beyond the animals people traditionally consider companions or pets.She also points to the growing number of Indian businesses offering vegan alternatives. For her, such businesses are helping make animal-free choices more accessible.For those thinking of making the switch, the practical starting point may be simple: understand what a vegan diet excludes, plan for essential nutrients and explore the plant-based foods already available in the kitchen.World Vegan Day was established in 1994 by Louise Wallis, then president of The Vegan Society, to mark the 50th anniversary of the organisation's founding in November 1944.The day is now observed annually on November 1 to raise awareness about veganism and its ethical, environmental and health-related aspects.

World.title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar
World.content:
External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said India has held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on protecting civilian shipping, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.

According to news agency ANI, Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said India was engaging with the parties on three key aspects of the conflict, including the safety of civilian vessels and seafarers, the restoration of grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine, and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure. He said India was trying to bring the concerned parties together to address these issues.

"One, not to attack civilian shipping and seafarers," he said, outlining the first of the three areas discussed with Russia, Ukraine and Europe.

On the second issue, Jaishankar stressed the need to restore grain shipments from both Russia and Ukraine, warning that exports through the Black Sea had declined sharply amid the conflict.

"The second, to find a way by which the grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine, these are two major exporters of grain for the global markets, can be restored, because that flow has cut down very sharply in the Black Sea," he said.





Jaishankar further highlighted the complexities involved in ensuring the safety of energy infrastructure, saying different parties had different interpretations of what should be covered under such an understanding.

"And the third is with regard to energy. Non-attack on energy is probably the most complicated piece because it means different things to the different players. There is energy infrastructure itself.

To some, it would mean a refinery; to some, it would mean grids. There would be issues relating to ships carrying fuel," he said.

He added that India is attempting to bring the concerned parties together to find common ground on these issues, particularly on the protection of energy infrastructure and fuel shipments.

The concerns raised by Jaishankar extend beyond the immediate conflict, given the Black Sea's importance to global trade.

Any disruption to commercial shipping can affect the movement of essential commodities, raise freight and insurance costs and put pressure on international supply chains.

Similarly, attacks on refineries, electricity grids and fuel-carrying vessels can disrupt energy supplies and push up global prices. Together, the safety of maritime routes, grain exports and energy infrastructure remains critical to maintaining stability in global food and energy markets.

World.title: 'Stay quiet or I'll speak for an hour': Kharge's playful warning to supporters at Ramlila Maidan rally
World.content: The Congress chief also launched a sharp attack on the BJP, accusing its governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh of coming to power through what he called 'vote theft'

World.title: 'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?': Mamata mocks CEC; Akhilesh invokes Haldighati - who said what at INDIA bloc rally
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc on Sunday held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The rally held over allegations of âvote choriâ, saw senior INDIA bloc leaders accuse the BJP of electoral manipulation and undermining democratic institutions.

Several opposition leaders targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission was favouring the ruling party.

They demanded Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.

'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?' Mamata mocks CEC

Former West Bengal chief minister

accused the BJP of trying to influence the West Bengal elections and vowed to fight against the alleged actions.

âBengal is victim of SIR. We will not spare them, we will fight,â she said, adding, âGyanesh, when will you vanish?â

Mamata also accused the BJP of looting funds linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi and Waqf properties, and alleged that the police had become the party's âcomradesâ.





âWhat haven't they looted? They looted the money of Ram Janmabhoomi, Waqf properties... The police became their comrades. The BJP has no organisation of its own. That is why they make the police do party work. Agencies don't work with the BJP. The BJP will go,â she said.

Accusing the BJP of undermining democracy and the Constitution through alleged âvote theftâ, Mamata said the party had also deprived young people of jobs, compromised women's dignity and misused donations.

âThese people have looted the country's democracy and constitution through 'vote theft', and attacked it on top of that. The BJP has stolen youth's jobs, stolen women's honor, stolen donationsâwe must remove them from power,â she said.

âBengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not give up. We will give our lives, we will fight, but we will not surrender. They looted our Bengal. We will save democracy and bring it back...

We will take revenge through politics. We will take revenge through democracy. We will fight...â she added.

'After Gyanesh, you're next': Rahul warns PM Modi, Shah

Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

also targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission had helped the BJP manipulate elections.

âListen to me. What I say always turns out to be true, doesn't it? I am telling every citizen and every youth of India: Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of Chief Election Commissioner.

Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail,â he said.

He also alleged that PM Modi and Amit Shah would not have reached their current positions without Kumar's help. âWithout Gyanesh Kumar, neither Narendra Modi would have become Prime Minister nor Amit Shah would have become Home Minister,â Rahul said.

Rahul said the opposition was not driven by hatred towards the BJP leadership but was fighting to protect the Constitution and the rights of citizens.

âWe do not hate Narendra Modi, Amit Shah or Gyanesh Kumar. We are people who open the shop of love, not hatred. We are people of non-violence. For me, there is no enemy. Neither Narendra Modi, nor Amit Shah, nor Gyanesh Kumar. But the voice of every citizen of India is more important to me, even more important than religion. That is my religion,â he said.

He added that the INDIA bloc would not resort to violence or spread hatred but would continue to oppose any attempt to undermine the Constitution.

âWe will not use violence, we will not harm anyone and we will not spread hatred. We will work with love. But we will not let you destroy the Constitution. No matter what happens, we will not let it happen,â Rahul said.

Rahul also raised concerns over unemployment, farmers' rights and the concentration of wealth, alleging that the country's resources were increasingly in the hands of a few people.

âThe farmer is not getting his rights. The youth are not getting employment.

The labourer is not getting his rights, and the entire wealth has gone into the hands of two or three people. We do not want such an India, and we will not accept such an India,â he said.

He said the country should ensure that farmers received the benefits of their hard work and that students who worked hard had access to employment.

âAnyone can join Shiv ki Baraat. Every living being can join it. Can anyone be stopped from participating in that? No.

We want that kind of India. If a farmer works hard, he should reap the rewards. If a student studies for 18 hours, they should get employment. We do not want a country that belongs only to two or three people,â Rahul said.

Referring to Amit Shah's remarks that PM Modi would remain in power, Rahul said the opposition would continue its campaign after demanding action against the CEC.

âAmit Shah ji said Narendra Modi is not going anywhere. I am telling you the opposite: Narendra Modi cannot go anywhere.

Even if he wants to leave, we will not let him go. After Gyanesh Kumar, we are going to stand right in front of you. Legal action will be taken against them,â he said.

Rahul described Kumar's removal as the first step towards putting the country back on the right track. âThe first step to get the country back on the right track is to remove Gyanesh Kumar,â he said.

Kharge accuses Modi, Shah of shielding CEC

Congress president

alleged that the BJP government had come to power through a âstolenâ mandate.

He said removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi was necessary to protect democracy.

Kharge accused Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of attempting to take away the voting rights of Dalits, women and young people. He alleged that the two leaders were shielding CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

âModi and Shah have attempted to snatch the vote of Dalits, youth and women. Modi ji wants to take away their votes through his man -- Ganesh Kumar.

We will keep fighting until he goes, and ensure his exit,â Kharge said.

He further alleged that the BJP-led governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh had been formed through âvote choriâ.

âBe it the central government, governments in Maharashtra, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, they are 'chori' governments (formed on stolen mandate). We have to throw out these 'vote chor',â he said.

Kharge also said the opposition would continue its agitation until Kumar resigned.

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your perception of the current state of democracy in India? It's in danger and needs protection. It's functioning well for now. It's improving with active political engagement. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

âNo matter how many attempts Narendra Modi makes.. until Gyanesh Kumar resigns, we will not stay silentâwe will keep fighting,â he said.

He added that opposition leaders would not be intimidated by central agencies or the police.

âWe have the strength to fight and will not be intimidated by the police, CBI, ED or any other government agency. Neither will our INDIA alliance leaders be scared. Everyone on this stage is ready to fight,â Kharge said.

He also reiterated his call for Modi's removal, saying: âModi jayega to hi loktantra bachega, Modi ko hatayenge tabhi loktantra ko bachenyenge, Modi ko hatao loktantra ko bachao (Remove Modi to save democracy).â

Akhilesh invokes Haldighati, predicts âparivartanâ

Samajwadi Party president

Akhilesh Yadav

described Ramlila Maidan as the âHaldighati of democracyâ and said the rally signalled that political change could come at any time.

âToday, Ramlila Maidan has turned into the Haldighati of democracy. The massive public support and slogans of revolution are proof that change can happen at any moment,â he said.

Akhilesh also targeted the BJP, saying those who had once claimed to be an âunmovable foot of Angadâ had lost their political ground.

He alleged that the party was turning to the Election Commission because it feared losing elections.

âThe people of UP know how to welcome and how to bid farewell even better.

In 2027, such a farewell will happen that the Bharatiya Janata Party and its allies will not be able to return again,â he added.

'J&K was, is & will remain a part of India': Abdullah

Jammu & Kashmir National Conference President Farooq Abdullah says, "...Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will remain a part of India. They will not be able to separate it."

"These people point fingers at Muslims and call them Pakistanis. I want to tell the BJP and RSS: We have given our blood for India.

We gave it in the past, we are giving it today, and we will give it tomorrow. This is Ambedkar's Constitution. This is India's Constitution. We are all equal, and everyone has an equal vote. Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will remain a part of India. They will not be able to separate it," he added.

Tejashwi compares rally to Mahabharata

Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav compared the opposition rally to the Mahabharata, accusing those in power of manipulating elections.

âWhile the Ramlila Maidan is traditionally meant for staging the Ramayana, today we have organised a 'Mahabharata' for those who steal votes,â he said.

Referring to the dice game in the epic, Tejashwi said, âYou are all aware of the game Shakuni played in the Mahabharata. You know your history: the Mahabharata began not on a battlefield, but with a game of dice. And now that Shakuni is playing his game, we are compelled to fight the battle...â

Several senior opposition leaders attended the rally, including Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby, CPI general secretary D Raja and CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya.

Earlier, INDIA bloc leaders travelled in an open vehicle from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction towards Ramlila Maidan, as hundreds of supporters marched alongside them.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu | Paddy farmers in Telangana fear crop damage amid high market prices
World.content:
The rain forecast under the impact of cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum) in various districts of Telangana from Monday to Wednesday (November 2 to 4) is giving jitters to farmers whose paddy and cotton crops are in various stages of cultivation.

According to farmers, when rice panicles get soaked in rain and droops, machines used for harvesting paddy have to be hired for some more time, which results in spending more money. The soaked produce has to be dried, which may result in loss of some weight.

Labour also need to be hired to channel water away from damaged paddy crops. And those in the pre-flowering stage might suffer greater damage.

High prices

Currently, paddy crops are in various stages — depending on the time of sowing — ranging from harvest, nearing harvest and pre-flowering stage. The cyclonic storm is posing a threat to farmers at a time when they are getting relatively more prices for harvest — ranging from ₹3,500 to ₹4,500 per quintal of fresh produce, against around ₹2,900 (MSP and ₹500 bonus for fine rice) of dried crop earlier. Cotton crops, which are nearing harvest, may suffer similar damage.

Telangana paddy farmers anxious over rain forecast

Sankranthi Narasiah, a paddy farmer from Lalapuram village, Konijerla mandal, Khammam, said that his and other crops around him are in various stages — ranging from pre-flowering to panicle formation. “Wind and rain in this stage will cause us great loss,” said Mr. Narsaiah. Khammam is one of the six districts forecast to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall on Monday (November 2, 2026). Mahabubnagar, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Nagarkurnool and Wanaparthy are the remaining five. Muralidhar Reddy from Balanagar in Mahabubnagar said that rain for standing crops is bad news and will lead to damage.

Paddy harvesting machine charges

Donthu Rambabu, joint secretary, Telangana Rythu Sangham, said that it costs between ₹2,500 to ₹3,000 to hire machines for an hour to harvest paddy. “When crops get soaked in rains, panicles may drop into rain water which stagnates in farms. A machine which takes one hour to harvest grains over an acre, will take two hours. This means farmers have to spend double the amount. Besides, the grains have to be dried, which leads to loss of some weight,” said Mr. Rambabu. M Sudhakar Reddy, vice-president of the Sangham, said that grains which change colour appreciates lesser price.

Agriculture Department officials said that they have sounded an alert to farmers and directed officials concerned to provide them with resources like tarpaulin sheets to protect harvested grains. As the demand for paddy has risen, relatively less farm produce is reaching paddy procurement centres; they are picked up right from the farms by private persons.

Tarpaulin sheets used to dry paddy harvest

Mahabubnagar District Marketing Officer G. Balamani said that a few farmers have spread the grains on tarpaulin sheets rather than pouring them onto roads for drying.

World.title: El Nino: Telangana employees seek five-day work week
World.content:
Telangana government employees have reiterated their demand for the introduction of five working days a week as the State Government is struggling hard to mitigate the adverse impact of the El Nino phenomenon.

They said implementation of five working days a week can save water, power, reduce pollution on roads and enhance efficiency of the employees. Moreover, there will be no burden on the exchequer with the decision which will in fact benefit it. In a representation submitted to the Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju, the employees suggested that the office timing be between 10 a.m. to 5.30 p.m., seven and a half hours a day.

This was in comparison with the current working hours of 6.30 hours between 10.30 a.m. and 5 p.m. for six days totalling to 39 hours a week and employees can be asked to work an extra hour once a week, which would benefit the Government. This will be on par with the Central Government departments/institutions.

The Joint Action Committee of Telangana Employees, Gazetted Officers, Teachers, Workers and Pensioners which submitted the representation, recalled that Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy too has appealed to the people to save water, power & fuel/oil and implement energy conservation measures. The Central Government was also taking various steps in this regard to reduce dependence on imported petroleum and increase the use of sustainable public transport by the Government employees.

Accordingly, the Joint Action Committee requested the Chief Secretary to apprise the Chief Minister about the need to introduce five working days a week so that it could help save water, power and fuel, and also increase the efficiency of the employees.

World.title: Four held from Malda as West Bengal STF busts inter-State drug network
World.content:
Four people were arrested after the Special Task Force (STF) of the West Bengal Police busted an inter-State drug network in Kaliachak in Malda district on Saturday (October 31, 2026) night.

According to officials, the operation was part of the STF’s ongoing crackdown on narcotics syndicates. On Saturday (October 31), an STF team intercepted a vehicle on National Highway 12 near Madhughat in Kaliachak and recovered 2.688 kg of morphine, estimated to be worth around ₹3 crore.

Four key operatives, including the main supplier, Sahibar Ali, were arrested. All four are residents of Malda. A case has been registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act at Kaliachak police station.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari praised the officers for acting swiftly on a tip-off about the smuggling operation. “Let me remind the drug smugglers, racketeers and syndicate operators: they will be dealt with an iron fist, as our government maintains an uncompromising Zero Tolerance Policy against drug peddling to safeguard the future of our youth and strengthen our collective resolve under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan,” he said.

Earlier, on October 21, an STF team raided a location in Baishnabnagar in Malda district and seized 505 g of morphine. A 26-year-old man, Sahinur Ali, a resident of Kaliachak, was arrested. The investigation found that the narcotics had been sourced from Ershad Alom of Thoubal in Manipur for Habibur of Sujapur Danga in Malda.

On October 11, the police arrested five more people in Nimta in North 24 Parganas district. They seized 90 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth approximately ₹44.5 lakh, ₹5 lakh in unaccounted cash and three vehicles. Two of those arrested were from Odisha and had allegedly come to deliver the contraband, while the others were the intended recipients.

As part of the State government’s anti-narcotics campaign, Mr. Adhikari had earlier driven a road roller over nearly two lakh bottles of banned cough syrup in Balurghat in Dakshin Dinajpur district in September. The event was intended to send a strong message about the government’s zero-tolerance policy towards illegal drugs. Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar and State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee also attended the programme.

On September 23, Mr. Adhikari also drove a road roller over around 3.1 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup at a ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat’ programme in New Town in North 24 Parganas district. The seized bottles were estimated to be worth ₹31 crore.

World.title: 3.3 km corridor from Delhi Gate to Kashmere Gate to get a makeover, says CM
World.content:
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Sunday said that Netaji Subhash Marg, which connects Delhi Gate to Kashmere Gate, will be redeveloped by the Indraprastha Virasat Punarvikas Nigam (IVPN) to turn the 3.3 km stretch into an organised, attractive and safe corridor, as per a release by CM’s Office (CMO).

“The government aims to develop the stretch not merely as a transport route, but as a vibrant link between Delhi’s history, heritage, architecture, culture and modern urban life,” Ms. Gupta said.

A key feature of the project, the CM said is the integrated development of historic, cultural and public spaces located around Netaji Subhash Marg like the Red Fort, Jama Masjid, St James’ Church, the Kashmere Gate area, the Chandni Chowk intersection, Subhash Park, Hindi Park, Agrasen Park and Sunehri Masjid.

“The idea is to develop the available green spaces along the route more effectively and make this historic part of the city more attractive,” the CM said.

Three sections

According to details shared by the CMO, the proposed corridor will begin at Delhi Gate and extend up to Kashmere Gate. Based on the available road width, the beautification plan has been divided into three sections.

“The first section will extend from Kashmere Gate to General Post Office (GPO) Chowk. This is the busiest part of the corridor, with a road width ranging from 12 to 24 metres. The second section will cover the stretch from GPO Chowk to Brij Mohan Chowk, the intersection leading towards Jama Masjid, and has an average width of 45 metres. The third section will extend from Brij Mohan Chowk to Delhi Gate intersection, with an average width ranging from 16.8 to 26 metres,” the statement added.

The area around Delhi Gate is proposed to receive special attention under the plan, with a Heritage Interpretation Park envisaged at the site, the CM said. The park will feature a statue, an attractive pavilion, green spaces, pedestrian access and parking facilities. Its design will give prominence to greenery, ornamental plants, trees and architectural elements reflecting the area’s heritage.

“The plan provides adequate space for vehicular traffic as well as pedestrians and non-motorised transport. The proposed facilities include footpaths, bus lanes, motor vehicle lanes, parking spaces, pedestrian plazas and cycle tracks,” the CM said.

She added that public toilets will also be constructed on both sides of the road, while existing bus stops will be upgraded in accordance with the design guidelines shared by the Public Works Department (PWD) for its existing streetscape project.

Wishing people on the occasion of Delhi’s foundation day, the CM said that Delhi is not just the national capital but also a reflection of centuries of history, a glorious heritage, diverse cultures and vibrant traditions.

“Our vision is to ensure that development does not come at the cost of Delhi’s historic soul and cultural identity. Instead, modern facilities should add to the pride and dignity of its heritage,” she said.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh municipal elections: Polling ends, Jagan demands repoll in Pulivendula | LIVE
World.content:
Workers of the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) clashed in Pulivendula, the home turf of YSRCP chief and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, during Andhra Pradesh’s urban local body elections on Sunday (November 1, 2026). Stones were thrown in some wards before the police brought the situation under control.

Polling elsewhere, so far, has been largely peaceful, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said.

The overall turnout in the State reached 48.03% by 3 p.m. About 46.54 lakh of the 96.89 lakh voters had cast their votes. Smaller towns have seen higher turnout than the big cities. Visakhapatnam, the largest corporation, had the lowest turnout at 39.72%.

Voting for 100 urban local bodies, 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities and nagar panchayats, began at 7 a.m. It will end at 5 p.m. Votes will be counted on November 3.

Also Read: Arrangements in place for polling in 222 wards across NTR districts

Eight municipalities and nagar panchayats are not voting at all: Allagadda, Dachepalli, Darsi, Gurajala, Kamalapuram, Piduguralla, Proddatur and Rayachoti. Their chairpersons and ward members were all elected unopposed. The polls were originally due on October 28. They were put off on the Supreme Court’s directions after complaints that candidates had been prevented from filing nominations.

Follow LIVE updates here:

World.title: YSRCP leaders in Palnadu asked to remain indoors
World.content:
Police in Palnadu district asked YSRCP leaders, including former Minister Vidadala Rajani in Chilakaluripet and former legislators Pinnelli Ramakrishna Reddy in Macherla and Bolla Brahmanaidu in Vinukonda, to remain at home until polling concluded in their respective municipalities on Sunday.

At the same time, the police said that they have been allowing all voters, including leaders to cast their votes in their respective polling booths, even though they were asked to remain at homes in view of ensuring smooth elections.

Meanwhile, Superintendent of Police Jagadish Adahalli told The Hindu that preventive measures had been strengthened in view of previous election-related violations in the district. These included police pickets, binding over troublemakers, asking potential troublemakers to leave the towns and intensified surveillance.

SP inspection

The SP inspected polling stations, including sensitive booths in Sattenapalli, to review polling arrangements and security measures. Special surveillance was maintained in sensitive, highly sensitive and problematic areas to ensure peaceful polling and enable voters to exercise their franchise without fear.

Police personnel monitored queues, facilitated the smooth conduct of polling and extended assistance to elderly voters, persons with disabilities and those unable to walk. Continuous patrolling and vehicle checks were conducted to prevent untoward incidents.

Mr. Jagadish issued instructions to personnel through wireless communications, directing them to remain alert, coordinate with election officials and take legal action against anyone disrupting public order. The police appealed to voters to participate freely in a peaceful atmosphere.

World.title: RSS cadre participate in rally to mark centenary
World.content:
As part of its centenary celebration, a uniformed cadre route march was held by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) at Singampunari in the district on Sunday.

A retired teacher, Dhanushkodi, presided over the event. Parameswaran, the State organiser for RSS cultural classes, inaugurated the march.

Starting from Vathiyar Temple, the procession passed through key stretches, including Karaikudi-Dindigul National Highway, Periya Kadai Street and Koothadi Amman Temple Street, before reaching Seerani Arangam. More than 200 cadre participated in the march.

In Ramanathapuram, more than 200 RSS cadre took part in a rally that was led by a businessman, Gandhi Krishnan.

World.title: Congress condemns violence during ULB polls in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) on Sunday condemned the incidents of violence and clashes reported during the local body elections in Pulivendula, Kadapa and Arnada panchayat in Kurupam mandal of Vizianagaram district, stating that such incidents pose a serious threat to democracy.

In a statement, APCC vice-president Kolanukonda Shivaji cited reports of TDP leaders, with the alleged support of police personnel, forcibly removing YSRCP leaders and polling agents from polling stations in Pulivendula to facilitate booth capturing. He said there were reports of polling agents being attacked with sticks and stones, with videos of the alleged incidents also emerging.

He said arguments and physical altercations between polling agents in Kadapa and Pulivendula had reportedly disrupted polling for some time. Similarly, he said, tension prevailed at Arnada panchayat in Vizianagaram district following an argument and scuffle between TDP MLA T. Jagadeeswari and Jana Sena activists during the election campaign. Police had to intervene to bring the situation under control.

Mr. Shivaji questioned the effectiveness of the police machinery, particularly when elaborate security arrangements, including deployment of a large number of police personnel and 1,000 paramilitary forces, had reportedly been made to ensure peaceful polling.

Demanding a comprehensive inquiry into all the incidents, he urged the State Election Commission to initiate stringent action against police officials found negligent and those responsible for the violence. “Every voter must be allowed to exercise their franchise freely and without fear,” he said.

World.title: PIA's first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner arrives in Islamabad
World.content:
Pakistan International Airlines’ (PIA) first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, acquired on lease last month, arrived in Islamabad from London as flight PK786 on Sunday.

A PIA spokesperson, in a statement, said that the carrier is the first Pakistani airline to have added a Boeing 787-9 to its fleet.

PIA Chief Executive Aamir Hayat, accompanied by his team, welcomed the Dreamliner at Islamabad airport, according to the statement.

The plane is equipped with modern technology, including in-flight entertainment, and features a spacious and comfortable cabin, PIA said.

“The inclusion of the Dreamliner is part of a strategy to modernise PIA’s fleet and strengthen its international network,” the spokesperson said.

Photo shows the inside of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, which arrived in Islamabad on Sunday. — Photo courtesy PIA

“PIA’s objective is to provide international-standard travel facilities and a more comfortable air travel experience to passengers through modern aircraft.”

The Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner is a long-range, twin-engine plane with up to 325 seats. Previously, PIA’s fleet consisted of 12 Boeing 777 jets, 15 Airbus A320 planes and five smaller ATRs.

Photo shows the inside of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, which arrived in Islamabad on Sunday. — Photo courtesy PIA

Last month, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Sunday.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the airline’s expansion.

By expanding its fleet, the airline aims to meet rising demand with direct flights and broader global connectivity, he added.

The aircraft would operate direct long-haul flights from Pakistan to the United Kingdom, he said, adding that they would support PIA operations between different points in the UK and Pakistan.

The development also comes as the government in September clarified that it was not buying any aircraft for the former national carrier after reports emerged of a federal minister arranging and negotiating sovereign-linked financing for PIA jets.

World.title: Terrorist attacks drop by 37pc in October: PICSS
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators during October, with terrorist attacks declining by 37 per cent compared with September, it emerged on Sunday.

According to statistics released by the Islamabad-based Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), the country experienced 143 terrorist attacks during October, compared with 226 in September. The decline reversed two consecutive months of increasing terrorist violence.

The improvement was particularly pronounced in Balochistan and mainland Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, while suicide attacks also declined substantially. However, an increase in kidnappings, particularly in Balochistan, remained a major area of concern.

Data gathered by PICSS showed that terrorist attacks claimed 111 lives in October, compared with 260 in September, representing a reduction of 57pc. The number of people injured in these attacks dropped even more sharply, from 242 to just 69, a decline of 71pc.

The improvement in the security situation was also reflected in the overall human cost of violence.

According to PICSS, terrorist attacks and security forces’ counterterrorism operations collectively resulted in deaths of 53 security forces personnel, 45 civilians and five peace committee members, while 169 terrorists were killed.

The 71 injured included 29 security forces personnel, 11 peace committee members, and 31 civilians.

A rolling 12-month comparison conducted by PICSS revealed several encouraging developments. Injuries resulting from terrorist attacks fell to their lowest monthly level in the past year. The combined number of injuries from terrorist attacks and security operations also reached a 12-month low, as did injuries among security forces personnel.

— Screengrab via PICSS report.

The number of suicide attacks was jointly the lowest recorded during the same period. However, the number of terrorists killed, at 169, was also the lowest monthly figure in the past 12 months, reflecting a decline in terrorist fatalities, the report noted.

Suicide attacks declined sharply during October, with only one such incident, compared with three in September. The October incident involved a vehicle-borne suicide attack but caused no fatalities or injuries.

In contrast, the three suicide attacks recorded in September, including two vehicle-borne attacks, resulted in 45 deaths and 138 injuries. Consequently, fatalities and injuries from suicide attacks both declined by 100pc during October.

According to PICSS, continued counterterrorism operations across the country by security forces resulted in the killing of 156 terrorists and the arrest of seven suspected terrorists during October. Two security forces personnel and three civilians lost their lives during these operations, while two security forces personnel were injured.

Balochistan

Balochistan recorded one of the most significant improvements, with terrorist attacks declining by 46pc, from 132 in September to 71 in October. Fatalities from terrorist attacks dropped from 136 to 44, representing a reduction of approximately 68pc, while injuries declined from 63 to 37, a decrease of 41pc.

Separately, security forces’ operations in the province resulted in the killing of 79 terrorists.

Three civilians lost their lives, and two security forces personnel were injured during these operations.

In October, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) had confirmed that an army major was martyred in an improvised explosive device (IED) attack in Balochistan.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

Mainland KP, excluding the formerly federally administered tribal areas, also witnessed a substantial improvement. PICSS reported 40 terrorist attacks in October, compared with 58 in September, representing a decline of 31pc. Fatalities from these attacks decreased from 90 to 38, a reduction of approximately 58pc, while injuries fell from 165 to 19, an improvement of 88pc.

Counterterrorism operations in the region resulted in the killing of 42 terrorists, while two security forces personnel lost their lives.

The erstwhile FATA region experienced a comparatively modest decline in terrorist violence, the report said. The think tank recorded 30 attacks during October, compared with 34 in September, a reduction of 12pc. Deaths resulting from terrorist attacks declined from 33 to 25, while injuries increased slightly from 11 to 13. Security forces’ operations in these districts resulted in the killing of 35 terrorists.

Sindh and Punjab

Punjab witnessed two terrorist attacks during October, compared with none in September. These incidents resulted in four deaths and no injuries.

Sindh recorded no terrorist attacks during the month. However, counterterrorism operations in the province resulted in the arrest of seven suspected terrorists. Islamabad, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan also remained free of recorded terrorist attacks during October.

— Screengrab via PICSS report.

Kidnappings ‘serious security concern’

Despite the overall improvement, kidnappings emerged as a serious security concern, particularly in Balochistan.

PICSS recorded 88 people kidnapped in terrorist incidents nationwide during October, compared with 72 in September, an increase of 22pc. This was the highest monthly kidnapping figure recorded during the preceding 12 months. Balochistan accounted for 70 of these kidnappings, representing nearly 80pc of the nationwide total.

The increase suggests that, despite the reduction in attacks and casualties, kidnapping remained a significant tactic employed by terrorist groups, the report said.

While October’s figures indicate a significant month-on-month improvement, the longer-term security picture remains challenging.

According to the report, Pakistan experienced 1,376 terrorist attacks during the first 10 months of 2026. These attacks, alongside security forces’ counterterrorism operations, collectively resulted in 3,902 deaths, including 645 security forces personnel, 65 peace committee members, 595 civilians, and 2,597 terrorists.

Another 1,953 people were injured during the January–October period, including 639 security forces personnel, 62 peace committee members, 1,055 civilians, and 197 terrorists.

Compared with the corresponding 10-month period of 2025, the number of terrorist attacks increased by 53pc, while the combined death toll rose by 36pc.

World.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
World.content:
Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to “take care” of more targets.

Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the US and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections.

“A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion,” said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television.

In the most intense phase of the war, which began on Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the region. Armed groups joined the fighting in Lebanon and Yemen.

Akraminia’s remarks followed Trump’s suggestion that the US could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.

“We still have to take care of, I would say one or two sites, but we can do that in 10 minutes,” Trump told reporters at his Florida residence.

“You probably could look at Pickaxe Mountain, and you have to take care of that. We can do that all very quickly,” he added, referring to a suspected underground nuclear complex.

‘No geographical limitations’

Top military and political officials in Iran have warned against any new attack.

Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi on Sunday echoed a warning issued a day earlier in a written message by Iran’s new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.

“In a conflict with America, there are no geographical limitations; a vast theatre has been defined for inflicting damage upon the enemy,” Mohebbi said, according to state television.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said “we hope the other side will exercise rationality and choose diplomacy”, adding that Iran “remains prepared for both defence and diplomacy”, according to the official IRNA news agency.

The warnings came as Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei disclosed on Saturday that he had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance seeking to revive talks.

Rezaei noted what he described as a positive change in “tone” from the US side but said he had yet to respond.

He said Tehran had previously told Washington that unless its conditions were met, “neither would the Strait of Hormuz be reopened nor would there be any negotiations”.

Those conditions include unfreezing Iranian assets abroad, ending the months-long US naval blockade of Iranian ports, lifting longstanding sanctions and ending the war on all fronts.

Since the war began, Iran has claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit, and repeatedly targeted vessels attempting to cross without its authorisation.

The US has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

‘Braced for the worst’

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the Emirati president, said on Sunday that the United Arab Emirates hoped the exchanges would yield a breakthrough but was preparing for the worst.

“We’re hoping that there is a diplomatic breakthrough,” he told a conference in Manama.

“It is not the interest of the region to go through another round… But I think we’re also, as we’ve shown before, braced for the worst.”

In Tehran, some residents described a sense of helplessness as threats of renewed fighting mount.

“The news coming in is truly worrying. However, no matter how much I, as an ordinary citizen, immerse myself in these reports, there is nothing I can actually do about it,” Mohadese, a 27-year-old health inspector, told AFP.

Others, including 48-year-old vendor Ebrahim, saw no reason to be concerned.

“We do not fear another war; we have been at war for 48 years now — we are always at war,” he said in downtown Tehran.

World.title: Sialkot police say 6 held as TikToker nominated in case over stampede at mehndi event
World.content:
NAROWAL: Sialkot police on Sunday said they had arrested six suspects and registered a case after a stampede at a mehndi (henna) event, the deaths from which have risen to two.

TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, known as “Mr Pattlo”, had announced holding a mehndi event and prize-distribution ceremony at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road on Friday night.

With hundreds gathered at the site, a stampede occurred when the stadium gates opened. While Rescue 1122 initially said one man had died and 13 others were injured, residents had put the number of injured higher because many were taken to nearby hospitals by attendees at the event.

On Sunday, Sialkot Police said 18 people were injured in the stampede. One of them succumbed to his injuries at a government hospital, taking the deaths to two, the public relations officer for the district police officer (DPO) confirmed.

Noting that Jatt had immediately fled the scene after the incident, police said their investigation and raid teams were conducting operations to apprehend the TikTok influencer.

The police statement added that they had taken 50 motorcycles and a car — intended for Friday’s lucky draw — into their custody.

Sialkot DPO Dost Muhammad confirmed the arrest of six individuals involved in managing the event.

He added that police teams have been constituted to apprehend the remaining suspects with the help of modern technology, human intelligence sources, and traditional policing methods.

The retired captain noted that according to preliminary police investigations, organisers had invited a large number of people by advertising a lucky draw featuring prizes such as motorcycles, a car and other valuable items via social media.

During the event, an announcement was made over the loudspeakers instructing all attendees to enter the grounds simultaneously. This simultaneous entry into the sports stadium triggered a severe stampede, the DPO said.

He stated that the organisers violated the terms of their permit, as well as established safety standard operating procedures (SOPs). The stampede also disrupted the flow of traffic on the main Daska-Sialkot Road.

Noting reports of unruly behaviour by attendees and damage to public and private property, DPO Muhammad emphasised that protecting citizens’ lives and property is the police’s primary responsibility.

“Negligence regarding safety arrangements at any public gathering or event which puts human lives at risk cannot be permitted,” he said.

The Sialkot DPO declared that legal action would be taken against all those responsible for the incident, without any discrimination.

NOC revoked

According to a spokesperson for the Sialkot district administration, a no-objection certificate (NOC) had been issued to the TikToker for holding a mehfil-i-samaa (a gathering for devotional music/poetry) during a private event within an enclosed space in Daska.

The spokesperson stated that the event was cancelled before it could even begin, due to violations of the stipulated terms and conditions. According to the spokesperson, the NOC specified that the programme was to commence after the Isha (night) prayers on Friday.

However, reports were received regarding alleged irregularities in the event arrangements by the organisers as early as 4pm.

Upon reviewing the reports, Sialkot Deputy Commissioner Awais Mushtaq took immediate preemptive action and revoked the previously issued NOC.

FIR registered

The first information report (FIR), dated Oct 31 and available with Dawn, was registered at the Motra Police Station on the complaint of Inspector Mubeen Ahmed.

The FIR names Jatt, his brother, the owner of Faraz Cricket Ground, and six others who were organisers of the event, as well as 40-45 unidentified security guards.

It invoked sections 322 (punishment for qatl-bis-sabab), 188 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object), 431 (mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel), 440 (mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt), and 109 (abetment if the act abetted committed in consequence) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), along with Section 16 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

In the FIR, the inspector accused the suspects of violating the terms of the permit granted by the Sialkot district administration, as well as the established SOPs.

The alleged violations included the misuse of loudspeakers, the blocking of a main road, the vandalism of citizens’ motorcycles, and the infliction of loss of life and property.

The FIR noted that a large crowd managed to enter the Faraz Sports Stadium due to inadequate security arrangements at the venue.

According to the FIR, dozens of attendees at the mehndi and prize distribution ceremony reported that their mobile phones had gone missing and unidentified thieves picked their pockets, depriving them of cash and important documents.

World.title: Pakistan becomes chair of G-24 bloc of developing nations, reaffirms pledge to fairer global financial system
World.content:
Pakistan assumed the chairmanship of the Group of 24 (G-24) on Sunday, with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb expressing the country’s resolve to strengthen the collective voice of developing economies and “advancing a more responsive, fair and development-oriented international financial system”.

The intergovernmental group is a coalition of developing countries established in 1971 to coordinate their positions on international monetary and financial issues, according to its website.
